articles.title: Google pauses bug bounties for open source because AI slop reports are drowning its reviewers
articles.text:
Security slop: Generative AI models are exceptionally good at working with code, and vibe coding is now spilling over everywhere. So much so, in fact, that many open-source projects are struggling with an untenable volume of contributions if they want to keep a proper vetting process in place.
Google is temporarily pausing monetary rewards for capable bug hunters because its human staff can't keep up with the current influx of automated reports. The "vast majority" of these submissions are slop, Google warns, containing invalid information and hallucinated vulnerability data.
Tech Trivia: Which tech company launched the world's first bug bounty program?
The program being paused is Google's Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program (OSS VRP), which the company designed to encourage capable researchers to report vulnerabilities in Google's own open-source projects. Researchers get paid for their findings, and Google benefits from better, more secure code in Go, Angular, Fuchsia, and other major FOSS codebases.
Then came vibe coding. The Google Bug Hunters team recently announced that the OSS VRP is no longer accepting product vulnerability submissions. The pause follows a significant rise in automated reports that put too much strain on reviewers. On top of that, the majority of these vibe-coded reports are simply useless.
 – Google VRP (Google Bug Hunters) (@GoogleVRP) October 1, 2026
Google also updated the OSS VRP rules to say the program won't accept new vulnerability reports submitted after October 1, while reports filed before then are still being processed. Some Google Cloud repositories might still accept new reports, but the main VRP is being "reformatted" to cope with the new chaos vibe coding has brought to the open-source world. Google plans to share an update on the program's future in the first quarter of 2027.
Google is making a specific exception for supply chain reports, which can have a massive reach compared to other "simpler" bugs. Reports about particularly dangerous flaws are safe as well. In any case, Mountain View is directing capable bug hunters looking for a reward to other VRPs that still accept reports, as well as its Patch Rewards Program.
Vibe coding is now seeping into every open-source codebase with public access. Microsoft Edge, Linux, and other major FOSS projects are facing the same issues as Google, while smaller teams have simply decided to shut the door on AI-generated contributions to avoid being overwhelmed by slop.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 5, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 5, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Monday, October 5, 2026.
From PanIIT Alumni India and the Andhra Pradesh government’s plan to create a Rs 500 crore venture fund focused on deeptech companies, to Ola Electric’s Chairman, Bhavish Aggarwal pledging a 4.32% stake in the company to raise funds, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured Stories
PhysicsWallah retreats from direct student lending
Edtech firm PhysicsWallah (PW) has moved decisively to reduce its exposure to direct student lending, with its wholly-owned subsidiary FinZ Finance agreeing to sell a Rs 95.79 crore loan portfolio to Auxilo Finserve, an RBI-registered NBFC focused on education finance.
The deal covers a substantial or major part of FinZ’s loan book and is expected to result in a partial closure of its lending operations, PW said, adding the transition of the loans and borrowers should be completed within 60 days.
The significance of this move lies in the speed of the reversal.
Latest news
Bhavish Aggarwal pledges 4.32% stake to back Ola Electric
Ola Electric founder Bhavish Aggarwal has stepped up to back the company’s upcoming Rs 1,000 crore rights issue, pledging a 4.32% stake in the EV maker to fund his participation.
The move comes days after Ola Electric’s board greenlit the plan to raise fresh capital through partly paid-up shares and appointed Deepa Bansal as its new compliance chief to bolster governance.
According to stock exchange filings on Sunday, Aggarwal pledged 20 crore shares against non-convertible debentures issued by Krutrim Data Centre Private Limited—a non-operative promoter entity owned by Aggarwal—to CTL Trusteeship Limited. The company clarified that no shares are being sold, no other pledges exist on his holdings, and Aggarwal will subscribe to the issue on the same terms as all other shareholders.
Other news
DigiCert launches global Partner Network to accelerate digital trust and quantum readiness
DigiCert has introduced the DigiCert Partner Network, a global initiative designed to help partners deliver, manage, and scale digital trust solutions across six distinct business models, including a dedicated MSP Program.
Built on the DigiCert ONE platform, the network enables partners to move beyond basic certificate lifecycle automation into high-growth areas like PKI modernisation, software and device security, AI trust, and post-quantum cryptography transition, unlocking recurring, services-led revenue streams.
Table Space expands Hyderabad portfolio, partners DoorDash
Table Space, India’s largest flexible workspace operator by leased area, has expanded its Hyderabad footprint to 1.56 million sq. ft. across eight years. As the market expands beyond established hubs like HITEC City into emerging corridors like Neopolis, global local-commerce platform DoorDash has chosen Table Space to establish its first India talent hub. Table Space will oversee the leasing, design, build, and management of DoorDash’s initial and long-term HITEC City offices.
This collaboration highlights Table Space’s enterprise-focused managed-office model. Nationally, GCCs account for 53.50% of the company’s leased area, positioning Table Space to capture growing global demand across key Indian commercial hubs.
WeWork India expands Bengaluru and Pune footprint with 4,500+ desks
WeWork India Management Limited has expanded its footprint by opening two new centres in key commercial hubs: WeWork Infinix Palladium in Bengaluru and WeWork Millennium Towers in Pune. Together, the locations add approximately 2.25 lakh sq. ft. and over 4,500 desks to the company’s national portfolio, responding to rising demand in self-sustained urban corridors.
Spanning 1.7 lakh sq. ft. near the Singayyanapalya Metro Station, the standalone Whitefield centre in Bengaluru offers 3,100+ desks tailored for large enterprise scale. In Pune, the LEED Platinum-certified Wakad facility adds 55,000 sq. ft. and 1,400 desks, capitalizing on proximity to the Hinjewadi tech hub and the Mumbai-Pune Expressway.""
Razorpay teams up with OpenAI to launch ChatGPT ads for Indian brands
Fintech giant Razorpay has partnered with OpenAI to help Indian businesses run ad campaigns on ChatGPT via its Razorpay Engage platform. The collaboration enables brands to optimize product catalogues, manage feeds, and run targeted, AI-driven campaigns as consumers shift toward conversational product discovery over traditional keyword searches.
Prominent early adopters include Tanishq, Tata Neu, Fastrack, Axis Max Life, Traya, Shaadi.com, Palmonas, and NMIMS. Powered by an AI agent with human oversight, Razorpay Engage handles campaign setup, catalogue readiness, and performance tracking, allowing local businesses to seamlessly tap into conversational AI discovery without building in-house technical infrastructure.
Snabbit appoints rormer PhonePe executive Ramesh Srinivasan as Head of Growth and Revenue
Quick home services platform Snabbit has named former PhonePe marketing leader Ramesh Srinivasan as Head of Growth and Revenue. Srinivasan, who previously held senior roles at Flipkart and PhonePe, will oversee customer acquisition, retention, brand strategy, and monetization across home help, cooks, and beauty verticals.
His mandate focuses on scaling demand across Snabbit's nanomarkets through hyper-local planning and brand building. The hire follows the recent appointments of Chief Business Officer Abhinav Ankur and Operations Head Pradeep Yadav, bolstering Snabbit's leadership team as the company expands across five major urban centers after surpassing 10 million completed jobs.
MathWorks and MapmyIndia Mappls partner to Accelerate ADAS validation for India
MathWorks has partnered with MapmyIndia Mappls to integrate high-definition maps into MATLAB, Simulink, and RoadRunner workflows, enabling automotive engineers to simulate and validate Advanced Driver Assistance Systems for Indian driving conditions. By capturing local nuances like lane-level geometry, variable traffic, potholes, speed breakers, and faded markings, the integration creates realistic digital twins of complex road environments.
This allows engineering teams to test ADAS controllers early using Model-Based Design, reducing reliance on expensive physical testing and accelerating the deployment of automotive safety technologies built specifically for India’s unique traffic ecosystems.
Indian Specialty Coffee Debuts Across Greece and Cyprus
On International Coffee Day, Indian Ambassador Shri Ravi Shankar launched The Origin Box in Athens, introducing Indian specialty coffee to Europe. The initiative is a partnership between Karnataka-based venture The Coorg Coffee Club and Greek retailer Coffee Island, placing the curated collection in over 400 stores across Greece and Cyprus.
Featuring five specially processed coffees—spanning Arabica, Canephora, and Excelsa—from five distinct Coorg estates, each lot is documented from harvest to roast and carries its grower’s name. This collaboration establishes Indian shade-grown coffee as a traceable, premium origin, showcasing its distinct flavor profile to European consumers.

articles.title: AMD EPYC "Verano" CPUs to Use New SB1 Socket, Dynatron Cooler Listing Suggests
articles.text:
Monday, October 5th 2026
AMD EPYC "Verano" CPUs to Use New SB1 Socket, Dynatron Cooler Listing Suggests
AMD's upcoming EPYC "Verano" processors will apparently use a new socket called SB1. The name comes from server cooler maker Dynatron, which now states on its website that its cooling solutions support "AMD EPYC Verano on Socket SB1." Dynatron also has a product page up for a 4U active cooler listed as "SB1-4U-ACTIVE (TBD)," so the final product name is still pending. The "B" in SB1 could point to a BGA package soldered to the board, although that is a guess based on the name and nothing official. The listing doesn't help much either. Maximum power is marked as TBD, and the 128.05 x 106.6 x 130.7 mm dimensions are identical to Dynatron's J26 cooler for SP7, so the specs could simply be placeholders for now.
Verano is the codename for the EPYC 9006 LP, a Zen 6 part that AMD announced alongside the rest of its 6th Gen EPYC lineup. It tops out at 72 cores with boost clocks of up to 5 GHz, and it runs on 24 channels of LPDDR5X memory through replaceable SOCAMM2 modules. AMD is aiming it at AI racks as a host processor for GPU clusters, with a launch planned for the second half of 2027. The regular "Venice" chips use different sockets, namely SP7 for up to 256 cores and SP8 for up to 128. For "Verano," AMD itself hasn't revealed the socket name yet.

articles.title: Controlling the brain with light earns a physiology Nobel
articles.text:
Over decades of research, scientists have built up a partial picture of what specialized cells within the brain and spinal cord do. By studying how the brain develops, they could identify genes that were active in different populations of neurons and where in the brain those neurons resided. In some cases, these genes could then be used to genetically delete the neurons, allowing us to get some indication of what they might be doing, building on the information we’ve obtained from studies of brains with damaged regions.
But this approach has its limits. The brain is flexible enough to potentially adapt to the loss of some cells, and their loss early in development may alter the development of any neurons they would have normally formed connections with. It would be far more informative to activate and shut down the neurons in an otherwise intact brain.
Today’s Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine rewards three people—Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel—who developed our ability to do precisely that. Starting from studies of single-celled algae that are attracted to light, these and many other researchers built an entire field of study that we now call optogenetics: using light to alter the behavior of nerve cells marked by the activity of individual genes.
From algae to human cells
Nerve impulses are generated by proteins called ion channels, which sit in the membrane and allow charged atoms to cross it. The nervous system uses a population of ion channels that are only active under specific circumstances, like when they sense a neurotransmitter or experience voltage changes. It’s this fine level of control that allows specialized nerve cells to send impulses only under specific circumstances, keeping the brain from descending into a haze of electrical noise.
So if we want to find out what any of the multitudes of specialized nerve cells might be doing, the easiest way is to hijack this system: force the cell to send ion-based impulses when we tell it to, and see how the animal’s behavior changes.
The Nobel Committee notes that this idea was obvious enough that people tried several methods of doing so before developing optogenetics. But it turns out “the easiest way” did not mean “easy,” and most of these methods didn’t end up widely used because they involved some combination of needing to insert multiple genes, supplying the nerve cells with some very specific chemicals, or using lasers at an intensity that physically damaged the cells.
The ultimate solution, it turned out, was lurking in a single-celled algae called Chlamydomonas. The organism’s single cell is remarkably complicated, having two flagella that help it move around, and an eye spot that detects the light it moves toward. People had been studying the organism for quite some time as a model for basic biological processes.
This is where Hegemann, then working at Berlin’s Humboldt University, entered the picture. He and his coworkers managed to hook an electrode up to a Chlamydomonas and showed that exposing it to a flash of light resulted in a very rapid influx of ions, suggesting the light was triggering an ion channel to open. As other scientists started scanning the messenger RNAs made by Chlamydomonas, Hegemann spotted a couple of genes that were similar to a light-activated ion pump found in an archaeal species.
Suspecting these might be responsible for the ion fluxes in Chlamydomonas, Hegemann used RNA interference to block their activity. This did limit the flow of ions in response to light, clearly implicating these genes in the organism’s light sensing.
At that point, Hegemann started an extended collaboration with Nagel, then at the University of Würzburg, an expert in ion fluxes. They showed that one of the two genes was selective for only letting protons (which you can think of as a hydrogen ion) into the cell, while the other would allow a broad range of positively charged ions through. They were also sensitive to somewhat different wavelengths of light. The proteins also used a chemical relative of Vitamin A to sense light, just as the receptors in our eyes do. Collectively, this class of proteins is now termed “channelrhodopsins.”
Nagel was instrumental in broadening the use of channelrhodopsins, showing that the genes that encode these proteins could work everywhere from developing frog embryos to cultured human cells. He went on to show that, when active in the neurons of a small worm called C. elegans, exposing the worms to light could cause them to alter their behavior.
Lighting up the brain
Deisseroth and his coworkers at Stanford then played key roles in developing this into a broadly useful technology. They showed that the channelrhodopsins work in neurons, and the ion fluxes they trigger are transmitted as nerve impulses. They also found more members of the channelrhodopsin family, some of which are sensitive to different wavelengths of light. A version that allows negatively charged chlorine ions into the cell was also discovered, allowing researchers to selectively shut down nerve cells.
At the same time, Deisseroth and his team worked on the engineering side of the problem, developing compact light sources and small, flexible fiber optics that allowed the system to act in the brains of animals that were free to move about and behave relatively normally.
The result has been nothing short of a revolution in our ability to understand what different populations of nerve cells are doing. If we know a gene is active in a small population of nerve cells, then we can use the mouse version of that gene to activate channelrhodopsin there and start testing how light changes the behavior of the resulting mice.
We’ve described work that relies on optogenetics a dozen times or more. And the Nobel Committee cites its use in everything from understanding how memories are stored to figuring out what signals wake mice from sleep. In one amazing set of experiments they note, a research group took an area of the brain known to be needed for maternal care and showed it contained specialized cells that performed one of a long list of functions, like triggering mothers to search for their pups, or governing physical interactions with them.
Channelrhodopsins have even been used to restore limited light sensing in a patient with a form of blindness in which their rod and cone cells die off.
One of the clearest signs of how significant this development is has been the widespread adoption of optogenetics. While the three people being honored made key contributions to its development, they have only made a relatively small contribution to its use. Instead, the studies we see that rely on optogenetics are largely done by other people who recognized its utility and refined and extended it.
The award is also very timely for the US, where the current administration has been pushing for cutbacks in fundamental research and shifting funding to its priorities in applied fields like AI and quantum computing. It’s hard to imagine a more fundamental scientific question than “how does this bit of pond scum move to ensure it gets enough light for photosynthesis?” And it’s definitely the sort of question that gets asked without any sense that the answers would ultimately have practical applications.
But science’s story, again and again, has been one where seemingly trivial research has revolutionized entire fields of study and ultimately had implications for human health and technology. The Nobel Prize Committee, in honoring a clear breakthrough, has inadvertently provided us with a reminder of that story.
John is Ars Technica's science editor. He has a Bachelor of Arts in Biochemistry from Columbia University, and a Ph.D. in Molecular and Cell Biology from the University of California, Berkeley. When physically separated from his keyboard, he tends to seek out a bicycle, or a scenic location for communing with his hiking boots.

articles.title: Apple will start limiting Mac disk access for developers due to risk of AI agents
articles.text:
Apple will start limiting Mac disk access for developers due to risk of AI agents
'Full Disk Access' is getting a change on macOS
- Full Disk Access was introduced for system-wide backups, but agentic AI has introduced a new threat
- Apple has confirmed it will be "introduc[ing] additional controls" to protect sensitive data
- No word on when the changes could apply – no signs for macOS 27.2 just yet
Apple has announced plans to give users more control to the Full Disk Access setting on macOS in a bid to prevent agentic AI from gaining too much access to unwarranted information.
Typically, giving an app Full Disk Access would let it bypass many of macOS's privacy protections, including files and documents, emails, messages, browser history and other data.
It was introduced largely to support system-wide backups, which genuinely needed access to all that data, however with the rise of agentic AI, Apple has been forced to tighten that.
Apple makes major change to Full Disk Access due to AI
"Some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems," the company said in an October 2 announcement.
"We will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action."
The company specifically called out AI agents for prompting this change, referring to it as a critical measure in terms of safety.
Crucially, Apple hasn't yet updated the interface and options for Full Disk Access, however an upcoming version of macOS will likely include such changes. Currently, there's no indication that the changes are included in the beta version of the upcoming macOS 27.2, however both Beta 1 and Beta 2 predate the October announcement, so there's always the possibility that future beta versions or the full release could include the change.

The change was likely triggered by a recent report that Meta's Muse AI agent had accessed a user's messages, however Meta spokesperson Andy Stone did stress in an X post that both Full Disk Access and the Messages connector are "entirely opt-in" for each user.
Still, Apple's current Full Disk Access settings are very broad, so more granular controls can only be a good thing.

articles.title: Equs launches a personal AI platform with private storage to give users greater control over data - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Equs launches a personal AI platform with private storage to give users greater control over data
Equs Inc., a startup developing a trust layer for artificial intelligence data, today announced the launch of Equs X, a personal AI that lets customers retain control of their information.
Equs X pairs a personal AI with private data storage the user manages. The company said the AI model reads nothing unless the user allows it, file by file, and access is controlled by a toggle. The AI keeps what it learns in private storage rather than on the model provider’s servers.
“Most AIs now on the market require you to trade data ownership for speed and usability,” said Chief Executive Sandy Carter. “To Equs, that trade is unwarranted and most likely, short-lived.”
Carter added that customers want personal AI assistants, but they want assistants that help them without breaching their privacy. Too often, AI models are trained on user data; they are used to display advertisements, inform the company that runs the model about the customer or can leak sensitive information.
Because Equs X reads from the customer’s own storage, rather than copying it into a separate profile, revoking access ends access immediately. When access is denied, it’s not a deletion request to a provider that has already taken the data.
Headlines about users whose AI chats were exposed to the world are not hard to find. In August 2025, Google indexed nearly 300,000 Grok conversations, with Forbes counting more than 370,000 – users who pressed “share” created a link that also made chat searchable. Obsidian Security revealed in the same month that a researcher discovered over 143,000 Claude, Copilot and ChatGPT conversations publicly accessible on archive.org – the nonprofit digital archive of websites.
“Private data store means you are entrusting your data to an organization without relinquishing ownership and control of the data to them,” said Carter. “Trust stems from that company not being in the business of using your data.”
Equs X provides a Personal Data Store that delivers a unified data layer owned entirely by the customer, including a granular data switch that allows per-data-point access. This means that a user can choose exactly which documents or details the platform can access and when and retain the ability to revoke that permission.
Users also receive a daily brief, which assembles scheduled tasks and relevant updates sourced strictly from the user’s personal data store.
“What stood out in the Equs X beta was how much control I had over my own AI context: what information I bring in, what the AI can see, and when it gets access,” said Brian Silverman, founder of The Business of AI Roadmap. “As personal AI becomes more useful, that kind of control matters more, not less.”
Although the company’s platform is a consumer product, Equs also built what it calls the Equs Developer Toolkit. It includes a stack for issuing, holding and verifying digital credentials. People, organizations and the AI agents working on their behalf can interact with it. It supports industry-standard protocols and credentials.
Users can join a waitlist for the Equs X platform, opening later this month, which will be free for the first 90 days, but the developer toolkit is invite-only in private beta mode and is currently accepting applications.

articles.title: DC paraliza 'The Batman 2' por problemas personales de su director, Matt Reeves
articles.text:
Warner Bros y DC Studios anunciaron que la producción de The Batman 2 se ha pausado de forma temporal debido a problemas personales de Matt Reeves. El director de la película se ha visto obligado a alejarse del trabajo debido a una situación familiar que requiere de su atención, han confirmado las empresas.
Por lo pronto, se desconoce por cuánto tiempo estará frenado el desarrollo de The Batman 2 y si esto puede llegar a afectar su fecha de estreno, que tiempo atrás se postergó hasta 2028. Desde WB y DC emitieron un comunicado para enviar fuerzas a Reeves para atravesar esta situación.
"La producción de The Batman Parte 2 se ha suspendido temporalmente mientras Matt Reeves se ocupa de un asunto familiar. Matt cuenta con el pleno apoyo de DC Studios y esperamos continuar el viaje pronto", indicaron desde el estudio en un escueto comunicado enviado a la prensa.
De esta manera, The Batman 2 se topa con un inconveniente inesperado y del que aún se desconoce el alcance de sus repercusiones. Es lógico pensar que la pausa forzada a la producción se extenderá por el tiempo al que Reeves le lleve resolver los asuntos familiares que han obligado este parate.
The Batman 2 pausa su producción de forma temporal
Independientemente de las causas, no es la primera vez que The Batman 2 sufre un traspié en su desarrollo. Recordemos que la idea de Matt Reeves y DC Studios era lanzar la secuela de The Batman en octubre de 2025, aunque ello no fue posible debido a las huelgas sindicales de Hollywood.
Esto derivó en una primera postergación hasta 2026, aunque luego se volvió a aplazar hasta 2027. En julio pasado, el cineasta compartió el primer vistazo del regreso de Robert Pattinson como Bruce Wayne/Batman en una breve prueba de cámara. Dicha ocasión fue propicia para anunciar que la cinta finalmente llegaría a los cines a principios de 2028.
Más allá de la desilusión de los fanáticos por el retraso, The Batman 2 está generando gran expectación por la introducción de más figuras en su reparto. Más allá del regreso de Pattinson, Colin Farrell (El Pingüino), Jeffrery Wright (Jim Gordon) y Andy Serkis (Alfred), la cinta presentará a Sebastian Stan (Harvey Dent), Scarlett Johansson (Gilda Dent) y Charles Dance (Charles Dent).
Por lo pronto, The Batman 2 se estrena el 18 de febrero de 2028, solo en cines. Estaremos atentos a cualquier posible cambio en la cartelera según qué suceda con Matt Reeves y cuánto demore su alejamiento del proyecto.

articles.title: Menschlicher Linksdrall: Studie enträtselt unsere Fortbewegung
articles.text:
Studie zur Fortbewegung: Menschen laufen von Natur aus gegen den Uhrzeigersinn
Wissenschaftler:innen der spanischen Universität Navarra und der japanischen Universität Tokio haben ein bisher unbemerktes Verhaltensmuster in der menschlichen Fortbewegung nachgewiesen. Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Nature Communications veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, besitzen Menschen einen statistisch signifikanten Drang, beim freien Gehen gegen den Uhrzeigersinn zu laufen.
Bislang ging die Forschung zu Fußgängerströmen davon aus, dass dieses kollektive Linksabbiegen durch die soziale Interaktion in einer Menschenmenge entsteht, um Zusammenstöße zu vermeiden. Die neuen Daten zeigen jedoch, dass dieser sogenannte Lokomotions-Bias bereits im einzelnen Individuum verankert ist und durch die Gruppe lediglich verstärkt sichtbar wird.
Studie in Japan und Spanien schließt kulturelle Prägung aus
Für die Untersuchung führten die Forscher:innen um den Wissenschaftler Iñaki Echeverría-Huarte fünf verschiedene Experimente mit Erwachsenen, Teenagern und Vorschulkindern durch. Dabei spazierten die Testpersonen sowohl isoliert voneinander in leeren Räumen als auch in größeren Gruppen auf einem freien Schulhof.
Um kulturelle Unterschiede bei Ausweichmanövern zu überprüfen, fanden die Versuche absichtlich in verschiedenen Ländern statt. In Europa weichen Fußgänger:innen bei frontalem Kontakt meist nach rechts aus, während dies in Japan überwiegend nach links geschieht.
Das Ergebnis blieb über alle Versuchsanordnungen und Länder hinweg konstant und zeigte eine messbare Asymmetrie hin zu einer Linksdrehung. Wie ZME Science unterstreicht, traten diese Kreiselbewegungen besonders bei fünfjährigen Kindern stark auf, was darauf hindeutet, dass erlernte kulturelle Regeln nur eine untergeordnete Rolle spielen.
Zusätzlich führten die Verantwortlichen eine Umfrage zu sozialen Normen durch, um zu prüfen, ob Menschen unbewusst einer unausgesprochenen Regel folgen. Die Befragten gaben dabei mehrheitlich an, sie würden von anderen Personen eher eine Bewegung im Uhrzeigersinn erwarten.
Anatomische Faktoren beim menschlichen Linksdrall ausgeschlossen
Das Team untersuchte im Anschluss, ob anatomische Eigenschaften für die asymmetrische Fortbewegung verantwortlich sein könnten. Sie testeten Personen mit unterschiedlicher Händigkeit, der Dominanz eines bestimmten Fußes sowie unterschiedlicher Augendominanz.
Auch Geschlechterunterschiede oder das absichtliche Verdecken des rechten Auges durch eine Augenklappe zeigten keine signifikanten Abweichungen vom dokumentierten Linksdrall. Die Forscher:innen konnten damit nachweisen, dass die Bewegungstendenz unabhängig von diesen biologischen Merkmalen existiert.
Relevanz des Lokomotions-Bias für Architektur und Stadtplanung
Die Erkenntnisse aus der Untersuchung bieten konkrete Anhaltspunkte für die künftige Gestaltung öffentlicher Räume und Gebäude. Stadtplaner:innen und Architekt:innen können das Wissen über den natürlichen Linksdrall nutzen, um Laufwege in Flughäfen, Museen oder Einkaufszentren effizienter zu strukturieren.
Wenn Räume künftig asymmetrisch konzipiert werden, könnte dies den Verkehrsfluss unterstützen und Staus in dichten Menschenmengen reduzieren. Digitale Simulationen von Fußgängerströmen, die zur Planung von Notausgängen dienen, lassen sich durch die Integration dieses individuellen Faktors genauer steuern.
Die neurologische Ursache für das Phänomen bleibt zum aktuellen Zeitpunkt ungeklärt. Der an der Untersuchung beteiligte Wissenschaftler Claudio Feliciani vermutet, dass winzige Asymmetrien im Gleichgewichtssinn des Innenohrs eine Rolle spielen könnten. Die starke Voreingenommenheit, die bei Menschen nachgewiesen wurde, deute laut Feliciani auf eine Asymmetrie auf biomechanischer Ebene hin.
Bemerkenswert ist in diesem Zusammenhang ein Blick in die Historie des Sports, bei dem Laufbahnen in der Leichtathletik traditionell gegen den Uhrzeigersinn angelegt sind. Bis weitere Studien den genauen Mechanismus entschlüsseln, bleibt das Wissen um den menschlichen Linksdrall eine statistisch belegte Eigenheit unserer Fortbewegung.

articles.title: Desde hoy, las empresas tienen que explicar a sus trabajadores cómo funciona el algoritmo que gestiona su puesto de trabajo
articles.text:
Nuestras vidas cada vez están más supeditados a las decisiones que toma un algoritmo: decide qué noticias nos pueden interesar, cuál es la siguiente canción que te apetece escuchar o qué series te va a encantar. Sin embargo, lo que mucha gente no sabe, es que los algoritmos también deciden qué turnos de trabajo debes cubrir, qué tareas debes hacer e incluso cuál va a ser tu salario.
Lo malo es que nadie te ha contado cómo toma esa decisión el algoritmo. Hasta ahora. Hoy entra en vigor la nueva directiva sobre transparencia laboral con la que las empresas ahora deben contarte cómo decide el algoritmo todas esas variables que afectan de forma directa a tu puesto de trabajo.
Un mandato de Europa. Llevamos ya algún tiempo hablando de la necesidad de aplicar mayor transparencia a las decisiones que afectan al ámbito laboral. De hecho, la directiva europea 2019/1152 que regula la aplicación de esa transparencia laboral lleva cinco años de retraso en su trasposición a la legislatura española. El Real Decreto 723/2026 que entra en vigor hoy, es la materialización de ese mandato europeo haciendo que los empleos sean más previsibles para los empleados.
El artículo 3 de este Real Decreto obliga a las empresas a informar a los empleados de "la existencia de sistemas algorítmicos o automatizados de toma de decisiones". Es decir, si es un algoritmo quien decide tu carga de trabajo en función de la demanda, y eso puede afectar a tu salario.
Avisar no basta, hay que explicarlo. Si el sistema algorítmico o una IA fija la jornada, reparte tareas o calcula salarios, la empresa debe, además de avisarlo a los empleados afectados, explicar "las pautas, criterios y reglas de funcionamiento" del algoritmo para que el empleado sepa cómo afectan las distintas variables a sus condiciones laborales. Lo mismo se aplica para aquellas empresas que utilizan algoritmos para decidir quién asciende, en qué puesto trabaja o qué factores le convierten en candidato a un hipotético despido.
El objetivo es que el empleado sepa cómo afectan todas las variables del entorno laboral a su puesto de trabajo y así evitar sorpresas o discriminaciones. La información sobre el funcionamiento debe llegarle por escrito antes de comenzar a trabajar, en el contrato o en un documento aparte que el SEPE ya ofrece en su portal con el título de Documento informativo sobre los elementos esenciales del contrato de trabajo.
Una idea con nuevo destinatario. La normativa que entra hoy en vigor no es la única que cuenta con una cláusula que legisla sobre la transparencia de los algoritmos laborales en España. La Ley Rider ya daba al comité de empresa el derecho a conocer los "parámetros, reglas e instrucciones" de los algoritmos que afectan al puesto de trabajo de los empleados.
Aquella norma se aprobó con las plataformas de reparto de última milla en el punto de mira. El RGPD, el Reglamento de IA de la Unión Europea e incluso el artículo 64.4.d del Estatuto de los Trabajadores ya reconocía el derecho de los trabajadores de saber qué reglas, parámetros e instrucciones guiaban las decisiones del algoritmo, pero la nueva normativa le añade una nueva capa reconociendo el derecho individual a conocer esos detalles, no de carácter colectivo o en supuestos de algo riesgo, como especificaban las anteriores normativas.
El miedo a la caja negra. La hemeroteca nos da una explicación bastante clara del porqué de esta imposición de la Unión Europea a revelar qué tiene en cuenta el algoritmo para decidir sobre las condiciones laborales de los empleados. Según publicaba Reuters, Amazon descubrió en 2015 que su sistema de selección de personal no juzgaba igual a hombres y mujeres. Penalizaba los currículums con la palabra "femenino" y bajaba la nota a las graduadas de universidades solo para mujeres.
En Italia, el Garante de protección de datos sancionó con 5 millones de euros a Foodinho, filial de Glovo, porque había tratado de forma ilícita los datos de más de 35.000 repartidores. Entre los reproches que surgieron se hacía mención a las decisiones automáticas que los trabajadores no podían discutir porque no las había tomado una persona.
Lo que no te van a dar. De la misma forma que la normativa de transparencia salarial no publica salarios de personas concretas dentro de las empresas, sino que se hacen públicos los rangos salariales para un determinado puesto y experiencia, las empresas no tienen que hacer público el código de sus algoritmos. La normativa habla de pautas y criterios.
En declaraciones a ABC, Jonatan Amenedo, CEO de Welpay, lo confirmaba: "Nadie está obligado a entregar su modelo". Aunque sí deben ser suficiente para entender en qué criterios se basa la decisión y poder rebatirla. Tal y como dejaron muy claro compañías como Glovo durante la entrada en vigor de la Ley Rider, hacer públicos los entresijos de sus algoritmos podrían hacer que las empresas perdieran competitividad.

articles.title: Qualcomm signs its first 5G patent deal with Huawei, and agrees to buy some of its US patents
articles.text:
Cutting corners: Huawei and Qualcomm have signed a multiyear patent cross-license covering 5G, compute, AI, and networking, the first agreement between the two that extends to 5G, according to Huawei. As part of the deal, Qualcomm will also buy a batch of Huawei-owned US patents in compute, AI, and networking. Neither company disclosed financial terms, and the transaction won't close until regulators sign off.
Huawei made its first licensing payment to Qualcomm in 2001, back when it was a telecom gear maker building on other people's wireless standards. Twenty-five years later, the Chinese giant is selling patents to Qualcomm, and Huawei says the deal pushes the cumulative value of its licensing agreements to roughly $7 billion.
The joint announcement is short. It confirms cross-licenses to both portfolios, the US patent purchase, and a commitment to fair licensing. What we don't know: dollar figures, the deal's duration, or which patents are involved.
Each company published the same text with its own executive's quote on top, which says a lot about how differently they're framing it. Qualcomm licensing chief John Han said the deal reaffirms "the success of Qualcomm's 5G SEP licensing program," a nod to the standard-essential patents that drive its royalty business. Huawei's chief IP officer Alan Fan pointed instead to Huawei's own 4G and 5G standards work, singling out polar codes, the error-correction scheme adopted for 5G control channels, as proof of the value of Huawei's innovations.
Huawei added that its IP licensing business has generated positive revenue since 2021 and that it held more than 165,000 active granted patents at the end of 2025. The Qualcomm agreement follows a licensing deal with HP that Huawei announced in August.
Nikkei Asia is reporting that Qualcomm will pay to use Huawei's patents for the first time, framing the cross-license as one that makes Qualcomm the net payer. Bloomberg, citing a Huawei spokesperson, reported that Qualcomm is also licensing patents behind Huawei's LogicFolding chipmaking technique. Neither claim appears in the official statements.
 – Anshel Sag (@anshelsag) October 5, 2026
Industry analyst Anshel Sag pushed back on both, noting that the only confirmed payments come from Qualcomm buying Huawei's US patents and that LogicFolding hadn't been mentioned anywhere outside Bloomberg's report. In his words, "The Huawei PR machine is in full swing."
LogicFolding is Huawei's most-hyped chip idea of the year. Unveiled in May, it splits a chip's logic across two stacked tiers joined by hybrid bonding, shortening the longest signal paths instead of shrinking transistors, a workaround for being locked out of EUV lithography. Huawei claims the technique lifted its first LogicFolding Kirin SoC's density from roughly 155 to 238 million transistors per square millimeter, a 55% jump.
The deal also lands while Huawei is on trial in the US, facing racketeering charges that include conspiring to steal trade secrets from US tech companies. Huawei has pleaded not guilty. Still, the irony of a US chip giant buying patents from a company being prosecuted over American IP is hard to miss.
Huawei has been on the Entity List since 2019, so the deal will trigger a regulatory review in the US. Export controls are built to stop technology flowing to Huawei, not money, but a US company paying a blacklisted Chinese firm for AI and compute patents is exactly the kind of transaction that invites scrutiny.
So what's confirmed so far is narrower than the headlines suggest: a mutual promise not to sue, Huawei back under a Qualcomm 5G license, and Qualcomm buying an undisclosed set of Huawei patents for an undisclosed sum.

articles.title: WhatsApp vai barrar o login em celulares com sistema desatualizado • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
WhatsApp vai barrar o login em celulares com sistema desatualizado
Medida da Meta impede acesso à conta até que o usuário atualize o Android ou iOS do aparelho.
O WhatsApp vai bloquear o login em celulares com versões desatualizadas do Android e do iOS. A medida é aplicada pelos servidores da Meta e impede o acesso à conta até que o sistema operacional seja atualizado.
A mudança impede que o usuário entre na conta até a atualização do sistema. O bloqueio foi identificado pelo site especializado WABetaInfo e tem sido liberado gradualmente para contas selecionadas.
Ao tentar acessar o WhatsApp em um aparelho considerado incompatível, o usuário recebe o aviso “Atualize o software do seu telefone para entrar novamente”. A mensagem, que não pode ser ignorada, orienta a verificar as configurações do aparelho e instalar uma atualização disponível.
O WhatsApp já impõe restrições a celulares mais antigos: atualmente, o aplicativo só pode ser baixado nas lojas oficiais em aparelhos com versões superiores ao Android 6.0 ou ao iOS 15.1. O novo bloqueio, porém, é diferente por ocorrer no login e já está sendo liberado gradualmente para usuários. A empresa ainda não informou quais versões do sistema operacional serão afetadas.
De acordo com o site, a medida busca garantir que o app seja executado em um ambiente com mecanismos de segurança atualizados. A criptografia de ponta a ponta, por exemplo, não impede que um celular comprometido vaze informações que aparecem na tela ou que são armazenadas no aparelho.
No aviso, o WhatsApp menciona que versões antigas podem colocar o celular em risco de ataques por malware. Se um invasor conseguir comprometer o próprio sistema do celular, poderá ter acesso a informações antes ou depois de elas serem protegidas pela criptografia do aplicativo.
No que diz respeito à segurança no app, a empresa tem lançado outras ferramentas mirando especialmente a aplicação de golpes através do mensageiro. Em agosto, o WhatsApp trouxe recursos como novas opções de chave de acesso e a expansão do sistema de verificação em duas etapas, com possibilidade de definir um código alfanumérico. A Meta também investe em inteligência artificial para identificar mensagens fraudulentas e alertar as possíveis vítimas.

articles.title: Russian drones strike Ukraine’s data centers by exploiting air defense gaps
articles.text:
A surge in Russian jet-powered drone strikes on Ukrainian data centers has increasingly disrupted mobile phone and Internet services for thousands of people. Now Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and other government officials are warning of the need for more air defense capabilities, as such telecommunication outages could threaten Ukraine’s digital economy and undermine the country’s ongoing resistance to Russia’s invasion.
The Russian attacks on Ukrainian telecommunication infrastructure have focused on Ukraine’s capital of Kyiv since September 23, according to the nonprofit Reporters Without Borders. Ukraine’s digital transformation ministry reported that 100,000 households in the Kyiv region were temporarily experiencing Internet outages from those initial strikes—and Russia has only intensified its strike campaign against major Ukrainian data centers and mobile phone networks in recent weeks.
“Russian attacks on Ukraine’s telecommunication infrastructure are not new, with strikes and shelling previously damaging fiber optic lines, cell towers, and facilities belonging to mobile network companies,” said Tetiana Gaviuk, analyst for Europe at ACLED, in a post on October 1. “However, the recent concentrated attacks on Kyiv’s data centers and telecom networks stand out because multiple providers and facilities were hit within days, indicating Russia’s increased pressure on Ukraine’s digital infrastructure.”
Such repeated attacks could undermine the telecommunication networks that support Ukraine’s banks, payment systems, and public services, according to warnings from officials and industry figures, as reported by The Guardian.
Russia’s strike campaign
Russia has launched mass missile and drone attacks on Ukraine’s power grid infrastructure, railroad stations, shipping ports, and even residential apartment buildings since the first year of its full-scale invasion in 2022. But such long-range strikes have become even more damaging this year, as they have exhausted Ukraine’s supply of missile interceptors—and Russia has also upgraded many of its one-way attack drones to become faster jet-powered drones that are more difficult to shoot down.
For example, Zelenskyy stated on October 4 that Ukrainian air defenses currently intercept more than 85 percent of conventional Shahed-type drones originally developed by Iran and supplied to Russia. But such interception rates fall to just 50 or 60 percent when dealing with newer and faster jet-powered Shahed drones.

articles.title: Instinct brings its AI agent to group chats, even for friends without an account | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Instinct, the AI agent now valued at $10 billion as of its latest funding round, is expanding into group chats. The startup announced on Monday that users will be able to add the agent to chats with friends, which could be helpful in certain scenarios like travel planning, snagging event tickets, running fantasy leagues, organizing carpools, or managing who’s bringing what to Thanksgiving.
Notably, the group chats with the AI agent will work even if a user’s friends haven’t joined Instinct, the company said.
With the launch, Instinct moves ahead in its battle with top competitors in the space, like Meta’s Muse. The latter doesn’t yet offer the group chat functionality, though Meta’s older app, Meta AI, can be added to group chats on WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram, and Facebook.
Instinct and Muse have been running neck and neck recently, with both of them adding the ability to make phone calls over the past couple of weeks, as their agents try to win more of the consumer AI market. Last week, OpenAI launched ChatGPT Dots, personal AI agents that can also be used in ChatGPT Spaces, collaborative workspaces where the Dots and humans work together.
On X, Instinct founder Noah Shinn explained how Instinct handles users’ privacy and security in group chats. He said a user’s personal Instinct agent will ask permission before connecting with the group’s Instinct agent, and that users can also choose which groups they trust and can remove that trust at any time.
Shinn also said the group’s Instinct is siloed from the users’ personal accounts, which it cannot access. The personal agent will always ask the user’s permission before sharing information or taking any action.
If new members join the group chat, any pending replies from a user’s personal Instinct agent are held before those are shared with the group, too.
“Making plans with friends usually turns into a frustrating back-and-forth over times and places. With Instinct in the group, you can explore options together, agree on a plan and get it done, all in one thread,” Shinn wrote.
The feature is rolling out initially to Instinct’s early access users but will expand to all users “soon.” To gain access to the new feature (or other recent additions), users can ask their Instinct agent to put them on the list to try it out.

articles.title: Google AI data center project investigated after 420 football fields of Finnish forest razed — trees were removed before a mandatory environmental impact assessment, say reports
articles.text:
Google AI data center project investigated after 420 football fields of Finnish forest razed — trees were removed before a mandatory environmental impact assessment, say reports
300 hectares of Finland's forest gobbled up by data center development.
Google’s latest data center construction project in Finland is being investigated after the company representing the search giant allegedly cleared over 300 hectares of forest. The reported issue is that Google’s local operator, Tuike Finland, cleared the 420 football fields' worth of trees without obtaining a mandatory environmental impact assessment beforehand, says AFP.
Google sees Finland as an attractive European data center host country due to a number of favorable factors. The source notes that it is a country with a cool climate, plus stable and cheap energy supplies (mostly nuclear, wind and hydro). Moreover, Finland sees data centers as a solution to address some current woes such as slow economic growth and record-high unemployment levels.
This new development near Muhos, a small town with fewer than 9,000 residents, isn’t the first for Google in Finland. It already has a facility up and running in Hamina, in the south, but hopes to expand in Muhos, Kajaani, and Vaala, in the north. Overall, it is a massive expansion project, and part of a 13-billion-euro ($15-billion) investment in Finland over the next two years. Finland’s potential data center appeal has also made it a location of choice for Microsoft and TikTok.
While the local mayor looks forward to the massive investment, growth of business, and general economic boom for the region, residents are waking up to the experience of others where data centers have sprung up. Concerns about impacts on the environment, energy supply stability, and energy prices are simmering under the surface.
Google seems to have trampled on some of these concerns already, with these reports of trees already felled and excavators clearing the ground before government agency approval. Not a good start.
"In our view, operations at this construction site should be suspended until it is clarified whether the project is in compliance with the law," Hanna Halmeenpaa, chair of the board of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation, told AFP at the edge of the freshly deforested area near Muhos. Even some nature preservation areas have been logged, reckons the chair. Halmeenpaa was responsible for filing the suspension request with the conservation agency.
Google denies prematurely devastating the forest. It told AFP that tree felling had been "in compliance with Forestry Act requirements." Moreover, its Finland comms manager said, in a contrasting statement to that of Halmeenpaa, that Google has been ensuring "high-value nature zones within the sites have been protected during forestry works."

We haven’t seen any other reports indicating that preparation and construction work has ceased at the new data center development site near Muhos. So it seems like Google will plow ahead, hoping or knowing that the political and/or business will is sufficiently strong to ensure it won’t have to undo any of the actions it has already completed.

articles.title: Forward-deployed engineers help CoreWeave race the F1 clock - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
The modern F1 pit crew: AI engineers who race the deadline, not the car
AI providers increasingly embed forward-deployed engineers inside customer operations, and few settings test that model harder than Formula One. Races arrive every two weeks, budgets are capped and margins are measured in milliseconds.
That model is now on track with the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team, including new physical AI engineering service places cloud engineers alongside the team’s own. The value lies less in motorsport know-how than in lessons from running infrastructure for top AI labs, according to Richard Ahlfeld (pictured, left), senior vice president of physical AI at CoreWeave Inc.
“CoreWeave, over the last years, has helped most of the world’s leading AI companies set up infrastructure and run their models,” Ahlfeld said. “You can’t really do that without learning a thing or two about what is really needed to run AI.”
Ahlfeld and Eric Ernst (right), commercial technology ambassador of the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team, spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier and Dave Vellante at Fully Connected, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed the F1 team’s technology partners, whose stack runs from processors to the AI cloud. (* Disclosure below.)
Forward-deployed engineers race the F1 clock
Each car produces a million data points per second, and the team has to turn that flood into setup decisions between final practice and qualifying, according to Ernst. Outside engineers help because the calendar never pauses.
“We really need people that can be outside of the car development phase and come in with the fresh knowledge of what’s happening in this industry that is moving extremely quickly,” Ernst said. “You can build as many processes as you want, call it agile, whatever you want. You cannot stop that process. You got to hit a deadline.”
One early project tackled team radio. With dozens of open channels across the grid, teams have long relied on rooms full of people listening in, Ahlfeld explained. Then AI stepped in.
“The AI model listens to 40 people at the same time, puts a summary and immediately already knows [what to do] from a prompt,” Ahlfeld said. “If somebody is pitting, I need to do XYZ within the next 30 seconds.”
CoreWeave also taught the model driver lingo, so “oversteering” and “overheating” don’t blur together over engine noise, Ernst added. The work now anchors CoreWeave’s physical AI field engineering playbook, which spans more than 100 projects that start from a customer’s deadlines and work backward. For forward-deployed engineers, part of the job is knowing when AI isn’t the answer, since some steps can be handled by a simple rule.
“Not everything needs to be over-engineered,” Ernst said. “Look at the process first, and then say, ‘Where do we bring the tech in?'”

articles.title: Elon Musk s'aligne sur Donald Trump : SpaceXAI va devenir SpaceXSI
articles.text:
Donald Trump a banni le mot « IA » de l’administration américaine. Et Elon Musk va appliquer la consigne chez SpaceX avec un changement de nom majeur pour la division d’intelligence artificielle de l’entreprise.
Le 22 septembre, alors qu’il prononçait un discours devant l’Assemblée générale de l’ONU, Donald Trump a annoncé que les documents américains parleront désormais de « super intelligence », abrégée en SI, plutôt que d’intelligence artificielle. Car d’après lui, ce mot donnera l’impression qu’il s’agit d’une fausse technologie. Quelques jours plus tard, un décret présidentiel imposait ce vocabulaire aux agences fédérales.
Sa portée reste pour l’heure limitée : le texte ne concerne que l’administration fédérale, c’est-à-dire les ministères et les agences. Mais visiblement, Elon Musk a choisi d’aller dans le sens du président américain.
Encore un changement de nom
Car ce dimanche 4 octobre, le patron de SpaceX a confirmé, dans une réponse à un internaute sur X.com, que SpaceXAI, la division de SpaceX dédiée à l’IA, renommée ainsi après la fusion entre les deux entreprises, allait être prochainement baptisée SpaceXSI. Elle regroupe Grok, le réseau social et les centres données Colossus. « SpaceX est une entreprise de super intelligence », a également lancé l’homme le plus riche du monde.
Pourtant, ce terme est loin de faire l’unanimité au sein de l’écosystème de l’IA. En effet, dans le vocabulaire de la recherche, « superintelligence » désigne déjà un système hypothétique, capable de surpasser l’humain dans presque tous les domaines. Or, les IA d’aujourd’hui n’en sont pas là.
Un groupe de travail sur la « super intelligence »
Pas de quoi freiner Donald Trump. Ce dimanche 4 octobre, le républicain a présenté la « Super Intelligence Force ». Dirigé par le directeur du renseignement national, Jay Clayton, ce groupe de travail doit rendre sous 120 jours un rapport sur les risques et les opportunités de la technologie. Une réponse au climat d’incertitude qui règne actuellement, notamment en raison des nombreux incidents impliquant des agents IA.
Car le contexte outre-Atlantique est très tendu, alors que les manifestations contre les data centers et les craintes pour l’emploi se multiplient. Les alertes des chercheurs sur le danger de la technologie n’arrange rien : la défiance monte. Reste à voir si la timide réponse de la Maison-Blanche suffira à rassurer les Américains.
Sundar Pichai (Google), Dario Amodei (Anthropic), Mark Zuckerberg (Meta), Greg Brockman (OpenAI) et Jensen Huang (NVIDIA) ont signé l’accord sur la création du groupe de travail.
- Accès aux données X en temps réel
- Bon outil de veille médiatique
- Moins biaisé politiquement que sa concurrence

articles.title: ChatGPT mostrará anuncios cada que generes una imagen
articles.text:
ChatGPT está listo para mostrarte anuncios cuando generes imágenes. A unos meses de que el chatbot comenzara a desplegar publicidad dentro de las conversaciones, OpenAI ha dado el siguiente paso y confirmó que los anuncios ahora aparecerán junto a las imágenes que generas en la aplicación. El nuevo formato tendrá una etiqueta para diferenciar que es un contenido publicitario y se mostrará a un número de usuarios a partir de hoy.
De acuerdo con una publicación en su blog, OpenAI anunció un formato de anuncio visual para ChatGPT que aparecerá junto a las imágenes que le pidas. La compañía dijo que esta publicidad con imágenes de producto servirá para inspirarte, para mostrar cómo se usa algo o la experiencia que ofrece un servicio. Para evitar que los usuarios se confundan, las imágenes llevarán una etiqueta y permanecerán separadas del contenido que hayas creado.
Este formato es similar a lo que vemos con las respuestas de texto, donde la publicidad aparece con la etiqueta de "Patrocinado" en un párrafo independiente. “Los anuncios no influyen en las respuestas que ChatGPT te da”, mencionó OpenAI en una publicación de inicios de 2026 cuando anunciaba el despliegue de su programa de publicidad. “Cuando veas un anuncio, siempre estará claramente etiquetado como patrocinado y visualmente separado de la respuesta orgánica”.
Cuando generas una imagen, sueles tener una idea visual en la cabeza. Si le pides a ChatGPT ideas para pintar tu habitación, es probable que te muestre un anuncio de muebles u objetos para decorar tu casa. Por otro lado, si estás planeando un viaje y le pides generar ideas de atuendos, la IA podría añadir anuncios de ropa u hoteles en los lugares que mencionas durante la conversación.
Los anuncios de ChatGPT tendrán límites
Los anuncios en imágenes de ChatGPT solo se mostrarán a los usuarios mayores de 18 años. Para evitar situaciones incómodas, OpenAI implementó filtros de colocación que valoran si una conversación es adecuada para mostrar publicidad. La empresa busca mantener los anuncios lejos de contextos sensibles o en aquellos en donde el usuario se encuentre vulnerable a nivel emocional.
“Las barreras de seguridad están diseñadas para proteger a los usuarios, preservar la confianza y dar a las marcas confianza en la colocación de sus anuncios”, señaló. Como medida adicional, OpenAI usará supervisión humana y seguimiento para detectar si alguna publicidad infringe las políticas de uso.
Los anuncios en imágenes comenzarán a desplegarse en Estados Unidos a través de un número reducido de anunciantes. Al igual que vimos con los chats de texto, la prueba comenzará a ampliarse a más países, incluido México, en los próximos meses. El caso de España y el resto de la Unión Europea es especial, ya que OpenAI tendrá que cumplir con las leyes y asegurarse de que la información queda blindada, por lo que los usuarios españoles de los planes gratuito y Go no tendrán que preocuparse (por ahora).

articles.title: Fuite « extrêmement grave » en Europe : les données de 8 millions de personnes compromises au Danemark
articles.text:
La France n’est pas le seul pays à se retrouver dans le viseur des cybercriminels. Le Danemark vient en effet de faire les frais d’une cyberattaque massive, révèle le ministère danois du numérique ce lundi 5 octobre 2026. Des hackers sont parvenus à compromettre le CPR (Central Person Register), le registre central du pays.
Dans le système, les truands ont mis la main sur les noms, adresses et numéros d’identification de 8,8 millions de personnes. Le registre national du Danemark recense les résidents, mais aussi les personnes décédées ou parties à l’étranger. C’est pourquoi le nombre de victimes est supérieur au nombre de personnes qui composent la population danoise. Le Danemark ne compte en effet que 6 millions d’habitants en 2026.
À lire aussi : Une nouvelle fuite de données frappe l’État français, et l’Anssi fait partie des victimes
Une cyberattaque passée inaperçue
Pour entrer dans le registre, les pirates ont détourné les accès légitimes d’une entreprise privée danoise, qui était autorisée à interroger la base de données. L’administration a rapidement bloqué l’accès de cette société pour éjecter les pirates, mais le mal était fait. « Il s’agit d’un incident extrêmement grave », a réagi la ministre du Numérique, Christina Egelund, dans le communiqué de presse. « Avec toutes les autorités concernées, nous sommes en train de cartographier l’ampleur complète de l’incident », ajoute la ministre, qui précise avoir prévenu la commission parlementaire des Affaires économiques et du Numérique de l’incident.
Selon le ministère du Numérique, la cyberattaque remonte au mois de septembre. Pourtant, l’administration du registre national n’a découvert l’intrusion que ce week-end, dans la soirée du 2 vendredi octobre. L’autorité de protection des données du pays, la Datatilsynet, a été prévenue deux jours plus tard, et indique être en train de se pencher sur l’incident. De son côté, la police danoise a ouvert une enquête.
Notez que le registre peut aussi contenir d’autres informations, potentiellement sensibles, dont l’état civil, des détails de naissance, des liens familiaux, l’éventuelle appartenance à l’Église du Danemark, ou encore une mesure d’incapacité juridique. Il n’est pas impossible que ces données aient aussi été consultées par les intrus.
À lire aussi : Cyberattaque contre la Région Hauts-de-France – les RIB de 700 000 Français compromis
« J’appelle tous les résidents à la vigilance »
Face à cette cyberattaque d’envergure, le gouvernement danois promet de réagir et indique avoir « déjà lancé des initiatives concernant le CPR pour éviter des incidents similaires ». La ministre Christina Egelund a aussi demandé « un examen approfondi de la sécurité » du système et appelé la population à rester vigilante dans les prochaines semaines. « J’appelle tous les résidents à la vigilance », a-t-elle insisté.
« Il n’y a aucun précédent d’une fuite de données aussi importante venant d’une autorité publique. C’est grave que cela puisse arriver », a réagi le chercheur Jørn Guldberg, interrogé par la presse danoise.
Sans surprise, les données subtilisées peuvent servir à mettre au point des arnaques redoutables. Le numéro CPR sert d’identifiant personnel unique, un peu à la manière d’un numéro de sécurité sociale. Associé à un nom et à une adresse, il peut rendre une arnaque bien plus crédible, et servir de point de départ à de faux mails de l’administration, des SMS ou des appels frauduleux.
« Les gens ne peuvent pas faire grand-chose. Quelqu’un a désormais leurs données, connaît leur numéro CPR et peut faire le lien avec leur adresse et leur nom. C’est grave, car la confiance est rompue et les gens vont ressentir davantage d’insécurité. C’est probablement le plus gros problème », ajoute Jørn Guldberg.
Le chercheur rappelle que « tous les systèmes en ligne sont attaqués presque quotidiennement par des pirates, et certaines attaques réussissent ». La cyberattaque au Danemark illustre bien un problème récurrent du monde de la cybersécurité. Il suffit qu’un prestataire disposant d’un accès légitime se fasse pirater pour qu’un système sensible se retrouve à la merci de cybercriminels. C’est exactement ce qui est arrivé à la Région Hauts-de-France ce week-end, piratée par le biais de deux prestataires compromis, Atexo et Docaposte.

articles.title: From fintech to semiconductors, TechSparks 2026 brings more voices to the New Tech Order
articles.text:
From fintech to semiconductors, TechSparks 2026 brings more voices to the New Tech Order
Founders, investors, technology leaders, and policymakers from consumer businesses, fintech, healthcare, deeptech, and semiconductors join the TechSparks 2026 lineup.
Technology is changing how businesses are built, products reach consumers, and new industries take shape.
At TechSparks 2026, YourStory’s flagship startup and technology summit, founders, investors, technology leaders, and policymakers will come together under the theme ‘The New Tech Order’.
The three-day summit will take place in Bengaluru from October 13-15. Karnataka ministers Priyank Kharge, Minister for Home, IT, BT & E-Governance, and Krishna Byre Gowda, Minister for Greater Bengaluru Development, will join the conversations, alongside Pratyaya Amrit, Chief Secretary, Government of Bihar.
The lineup also includes entrepreneurs and technology leaders working across consumer businesses, healthcare, fintech, deeptech, semiconductors and defence.
Here are some of the speakers joining TechSparks 2026:
Ananth Narayanan
Ananth Narayanan, Founder and CEO of BRND.ME, has built and scaled consumer businesses across categories. He was previously CEO of Myntra and Co-founder of Medlife. He will bring his experience in building consumer businesses and working at the intersection of technology and brands to the TechSparks stage.
Mohit Bhatnagar
Mohit Bhatnagar is Managing Director at Peak XV. His work in venture capital spans investments across consumer, technology, and other sectors, giving him a view of founders building companies as well as investors backing them.
Kalavathi G V
Kalavathi G V is Executive Director and Head of the Global Development Center at Siemens Healthineers. The Bengaluru centre works on technology and R&D for the company’s global healthcare business.
Rahul Chari
Rahul Chari is Founder and CPTO at PhonePe. As co-founder, he has been closely involved in building the company’s technology and product functions as it has expanded its digital payments and financial services business.
Bharat Mandot
Bharat Mandot is Founder and Chairman of Stelcore Group. The group works across commerce and supply-chain businesses, with its operations spanning Stelcore Commerce and Stelcore Supply Chain.
Shweta Rajpal Kohli

articles.title: macOS: Apple führt neue Kontrollfunktionen ein, um mehr Schutz vor KI-Agenten zu bieten
articles.text:
Neue Kontrollfunktionen: Wie Apple deinen Mac gegen KI-Agenten absichern will
Sicherheitsvorfälle wie der Angriff auf Hugging Face haben bewiesen, dass sich autonome KI-Agenten der menschlichen Kontrolle entziehen und in fremde Systeme eindringen können. Inzwischen fordern sogar Anbieter wie OpenAI und Anthropic eine stärkere staatliche Regulierung ihrer Modelle, um die Risiken zu minimieren. Das allein reicht allerdings nicht aus, um sich vor ungewolltem Zugriff durch agentische KI zu schützen. Denn auch Systeme, die von Nutzer:innen freiwillig verwendet werden, können anders als beabsichtigt handeln. Apple hat deshalb jetzt neue Sicherheitsfunktionen für Mac-Nutzer:innen angekündigt.
KI-Agenten handeln selbstständig
Mehrere Berichte über Openclaw zeigten schon im Frühjahr, was passiert, wenn ein KI-Agent nicht wie gewünscht handelt. Einer davon stammte von Summer Yue, die als KI-Forscherin bei Meta tätig ist. Sie wollte ihr Postfach von einem Openclaw-Agenten verwalten lassen – stattdessen löschte dieser sämtliche E-Mails. Auch auf mehrfache Befehle per Smartphone, die ihn stoppen sollten, habe die KI nicht reagiert. Jetzt hat Meta selbst einen KI-Agenten auf den Markt gebracht – und auch hier scheint es noch Probleme bei Kontrolle und Transparenz zu geben. Laut Unternehmensangaben sei das System namens Muse in der Lage, das digitale Leben seiner Nutzer:innen zu managen und sogar den Wocheneinkauf für sie zu erledigen. Dabei sollen sie jederzeit die Kontrolle über ihre Daten und Apps behalten.
Der Tech-Kolumnist Jason Aten testete Muse auf seinem iPhone und seinem Mac. In einem Artikel für Inc. berichtet er, dass der KI-Agent nach einigen normalen Eingaben und Antworten begonnen habe, seine Nachrichten mitzulesen – obwohl er den Vollzugriff auf die Festplatte nach eigenen Angaben bewusst deaktiviert hatte. Sein Bericht ist nicht der einzige Vorfall, bei dem Muse den Nutzer:innen zufolge zu weit gegangen sei. So berichtete etwa der Youtuber Matt Robb, dass der Muse-Agent sich falsch verhalten habe. Er wollte ihn eigentlich zum Verkauf gebrauchter Gegenstände auf Facebook Marketplace nutzen. Der Agent habe allerdings seine Adresse ohne Zustimmung geteilt, woraufhin ein:e Käufer:in bei ihm aufgetaucht sei, als er gar nicht zuhause war.
Apple passt Zugriffseinstellungen an
Meta bestritt laut Techcrunch zwar, dass der KI-Agent ohne Erlaubnis gehandelt habe. Trotzdem bleibt die Skepsis groß. Nur wenige Tage nach diesen Vorfällen kündigte Apple zusätzliche Kontrollen für die Einstellung „Vollzugriff auf die Festplatte“ unter macOS an, um Nutzer:innen besser vor ungewollten Handlungen durch KI-Agenten zu schützen. Zusätzlich berichtete Wired, dass eine Sicherheitslücke in der Mac-App von ChatGPT Hacker:innen Zugriff auf sensible Daten ermöglichen könnte. Im Fall von Metas KI-Agent Muse können Nutzer:innen den „Vollzugriff auf die Festplatte“ optional aktivieren. Laut Apple erlaube diese Einstellung den Zugriff auf Dateien, E-Mails, Nachrichten und sogar auf den Browserverlauf.
„Einige Entwickler:innen nutzen den Vollzugriff auf die Festplatte auf eine Weise, die Nutzer:innen gefährden und alles auf ihren Systemen offenlegen könnte, ohne dass diese es vollständig wissen und verstehen“, erklärte Apple in dem kürzlich veröffentlichten Beitrag. Das Unternehmen kündigte deshalb neue Kontrollmechanismen an. „Es ist entscheidend, dieses Problem anzugehen. Da KI-Agenten immer leistungsfähiger und autonomer werden, werden die mit diesem Zugriffsniveau verbundenen Risiken erheblich zunehmen. Wir setzen uns dafür ein, dass Nutzer:innen diese Risiken klar verstehen, bevor sie einen solchen Zugriff gewähren, damit sie fundierte Entscheidungen über ihre eigenen Daten und ihre Privatsphäre treffen können“, so Apple.

articles.title: C'est le top départ des Jours Flash Prime sur Amazon : voici les meilleures offres Tech en DIRECT — Frandroid
articles.text:
Si vous connaissez le Prime Day, les Jours Flash Prime devraient vous sembler assez familiers. C’est la même recette, avec des milliers d’offres réservées aux membres Amazon Prime, mais juste pas le même nom. Notez d’ailleurs que l’événement dure seulement deux jours, il va donc falloir être assez réactif pour profiter des meilleures offres qui tomberont au compte-gouttes.
Si vous recherchez un nouveau smartphone, tablette, TV, PC portable, casque ou écouteurs sans fil, des objets connectés ou tout autre objet Tech à prix cassé, vous êtes au bon endroit. Cet article sera régulièrement mis à jour, au rythme des ventes flash, n’hésitez donc pas à revenir y faire un tour plus tard si vous ne trouvez pas votre bonheur la première fois.
Les meilleures offres des Jours Flash Prime sur Amazon
Philips 65MLED810
Pour un TV Mini LED de 65 pouces à ce prix, le Philips 65MLED810 est difficile à ignorer. Il procure une bonne immersion grâce à sa technologie Ambilight et ne coûte pas plus de 420 euros aujourd’hui.

Le Philips 65MLED810 passe à 418,57 euros chez Amazon au lieu de 999 euros.

Vous pouvez profiter de cette période de Prime Day pour acheter le Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra de 256 Go à 1 104,81 euros au lieu de 1 469 euros.

articles.title: Hace mucho tiempo que el buen altavoz no es solo el que se escucha bien. En 2026, esto es lo que más importa
articles.text:
Hubo un tiempo en el que comprar un altavoz consistía en fijarse siempre en el modelo más grande ¿te acuerdas de esos muebles con sistemas Hi-Fi con pletina doble, ecualizador, plato de discos...? Aquellos equipos de alta fidelidad han ido dejando paso a altavoces compactos y conectados, y el sonido ya no es lo más importante en todos ellos.
Por eso vamos a repasar los principales reclamos con los que los fabricantes de altavoces han intentado destacar frente a la competencia en lo que llevamos de 2026 porque el mercado cada vez está más saturado y la oferta es más amplia. La calidad de sonido sigue siendo un valor fundamental, pero no es el único.
Si nos fijamos en los anuncios de distintas marcas, la competencia entre los altavoces conectados está enfocándose en varios frentes: mejorar el sonido, sí, pero más aún facilitar el uso y conseguir que un mismo equipo tenga más utilidad dentro y fuera de casa.
Índice de Contenidos (7)
Altavoces más dinámicos
Uno de esos frentes consiste en convertir el altavoz en algo más que un dispositivo para escuchar música desde el móvil o en un lugar fijo en la habitación. Un buen ejemplo es como distintos fabricantes plantean algunos de sus modelos dando un paso más allá y los venden como complementos ideales para mejorar el sonido del televisor. Por ejemplo, Samsung lo hace con Music Studio y Q-Symphony, que permite combinar televisores, barras de sonido y altavoces compatibles. Es una idea interesante, ya que permite ampliar el equipo poco a poco sin tener que gastar demasiado dinero de golpe.
Es algo que también está en el catálogo de otras marcas. La posibilidad de combinar varios altavoces también está presente en Sonos, cuyo Sonos Play puede agruparse con otros Play o Move 2 incluso fuera de la red doméstica.
Una variante que también vemos en otras marcas es la posibilidad de montar una especie de hilo musical por toda la casa. JBL, por ejemplo, ha lanzado la serie Cove, que permite trasladar la reproducción a otro altavoz manteniendo pulsado un botón, sin necesidad de sacar el móvil.
¿Y cómo los hacen más polivalentes? Pues es algo que encontramos con altavoces que se olvidan de los enchufes como el Sonos Play, representante de modelos que no están pensados para quedarse en un lugar fijo. Gracias a su batería, permite escuchar música tanto dentro de casa como en exteriores. En este sentido, destacan la protección IP67 frente al polvo y al agua y la posibilidad de utilizar su batería para cargar el teléfono.
Sonido de calidad
Al final estamos hablando de un altavoz y eso es algo que no debemos olvidar: como en un teléfono, las llamadas, aquí sigue teniendo un papel importante el sonido, no lo olvidemos. La sensación de que el audio llega desde diferentes direcciones se está convirtiendo en otro argumento para vender altavoces de gama alta, y varias marcas están apostando por ella.
JBL, por ejemplo, incorpora Dolby Atmos en los algunos de sus modelos con la idea de ofrecer una escucha más inmersiva con equipos relativamente compactos. LG hace lo propio algunos de sus lanzamientos de este año como los LG Sound Suite M5 y M7. Estos modelos de la gama 2026 forman parte del sistema Sound Suite y utilizan Dolby Atmos FlexConnect, que adapta la reproducción a la posición de los altavoces y a las características de la habitación.
Otro ejemplo es Sony, que tiene en su catálogo los BRAVIA Theatre Rear 9 para añadir sonido trasero a sistemas de cine en casa. Por su parte, los ULT Tower 7 y Tower Max utilizan 360° Party Sound para repartir la música alrededor del altavoz en fiestas y reuniones.
Una IA pero de verdad
La inteligencia artificial también gana protagonismo, no solo como reclamo, sino como una herramienta para mejorar el audio mediante ajustes automáticos. Un buen ejemplo es JBL, que incorpora en el Xtreme 5 un sistema que identifica si estamos escuchando música o voz y adapta la configuración. A ello se suma el procesamiento del audio para controlar la distorsión a volúmenes elevados.
LG ha hecho algo parecido con los LG xboom Stage 501 y Blast, que ajustan el sonido según lo que escuchamos y dónde lo hacemos. Su tecnología AI Sound analiza el contenido y modifica automáticamente la ecualización para destacar las voces, la melodía o el ritmo. Y por el horizonte ya asoman rumores de un nuevo HomePod grande...
Asistentes que ahora sí son inteligentes
Los asistentes, por su parte, buscan entender mejor lo que queremos escuchar, porque seamos sinceros, hasta ahora dejaban mucho que desear. Ya hemos visto cómo Gemini ha reemplazado a Google Assistant en muchos altavoces de Google y cómo Siri AI apunta a los nuevos altavoces de Apple, sin olvidar Alexa+.
Los fabricantes quieren pasar página y dejar atrás aquellos asistentes que solo servían para subir el volumen o preguntar por el pronóstico del tiempo. Más allá de las tres grandes compañías mencionadas, otro ejemplo de este cambio es Sonos, que ha anunciado para este otoño un asistente capaz de interpretar peticiones relacionadas con el ambiente que buscamos o referencias a canciones cuyo título no recordamos.
Conectividad funcional
Conectados ya lo eran muchos, pero las marcas han dado un paso más y no se trata solo de poner WiFi o Bluetooth porque sí. En las propuestas más completas, el WiFi ahora permite acceder a servicios de música y organizar la reproducción en casa, mientras que el Bluetooth facilita la conexión directa con el móvil (muchas veces con dos al mismo tiempo) y ha mejorado para un menor consumo energético. A ello se suma la compatibilidad con AirPlay 2, Google Cast o servicios como Spotify Connect, Tidal Connect y Qobuz Connect.
Marcas como LG, Samsung o Sonos ofrecen distintas combinaciones de estas opciones en sus familias de altavoces. De hecho, muchas de ellas requieren una aplicación propia para sacar todo el partido a sus equipos.
El diseño también importa
Un buen ejemplo es Samsung, que, de la mano del diseñador Erwan Bouroullec, ha lanzado una nueva colección de altavoces, los Music Studio, con formas pensadas para integrarse en la decoración.
Queremos altavoces de calidad y funcionales, pero también que sean bonitos y encajen en casa. De ahí que aparezcan modelos con todo tipo de diseños y acabados. Bang & Olufsen y Harman Kardon son dos de los fabricantes que cuentan con altavoces de diseño distintivo.
