articles.title: ChatGPT começa a testar anúncios com imagens • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
ChatGPT começa a testar anúncios com imagens
Novo formato será testado de início durante a geração de imagens; OpenAI afirma que publicidade continuará separada das respostas.
A OpenAI vai começar a testar anúncios com imagens dentro do ChatGPT. O novo formato visual será exibido inicialmente durante a geração de imagens e poderá mostrar produtos, inspirações de uso e experiências relacionadas aos serviços anunciados. Segundo a empresa, os testes começam neste mês nos Estados Unidos.
Os anúncios serão identificados e ficarão separados do conteúdo gerado pelo ChatGPT. A empresa afirma ainda que as propagandas não influenciam as respostas do chatbot.
A novidade amplia um programa de publicidade que já chegou ao Brasil para usuários das contas gratuitas e do plano Go. Até agora, as peças publicitárias exibidas no ChatGPT utilizavam formatos mais simples, com texto, nome da empresa, logotipo e um link para o produto ou serviço. O novo modelo acrescenta imagens.
O movimento faz parte de uma expansão de publicidade na plataforma. Em agosto, foi revelado que a OpenAI também testava anúncios capazes de levar o usuário a uma conversa com uma IA criada por uma empresa anunciante.
Além do novo formato, a companhia anunciou mais ferramentas para que as marcas consigam acompanhar resultados de campanhas no ChatGPT. Entre as métricas disponíveis estão cliques, conversões e testes para estimar se um projeto de publicidade realmente provocou novas vendas.
A OpenAI afirma que parceiros responsáveis pela avaliação de segurança de marcas não terão acesso às conversas privadas dos usuários. Segundo a empresa, suas políticas também impedem a exibição de publicidade em contextos considerados sensíveis.
Essa separação entre publicidade e respostas é um dos princípios adotados pela companhia desde o início dos testes. Quando a publicidade começou a aparecer no ChatGPT, a OpenAI afirmou que anunciantes não teriam influência sobre o conteúdo produzido pela IA.
A expansão dos anúncios acontece enquanto a OpenAI transforma o ChatGPT em uma plataforma cada vez mais ligada à descoberta e compra de produtos. A empresa já testou uma experiência de compras que apresenta preços, avaliações e links para lojas diretamente nas conversas. Posteriormente, também passou a permitir compras dentro do próprio chatbot em alguns mercados.
Segundo a OpenAI, as propagandas ajudam a ampliar o acesso gratuito ao serviço e representam uma fonte de receita complementar às assinaturas. Por enquanto, não há previsão de quando os anúncios com imagens serão disponibilizados no Brasil ou em outros países.

articles.title: Dutch eyewear company is the first retailer to pull Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses from over 400 stores due to ‘questions being raised’ about the technology
articles.text:
Dutch eyewear giant becomes first retailer to halt Meta Ray-ban sales — Hans Anders pulls smart glasses from 400 stores due to ‘questions being raised’ about the tech
Putting the 'ban' in 'Ray-Ban'
- Eyewear retailer Hans Anders has stopped sales of Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses
- The decision comes amid growing concerns over the public use of the tech
- Dutch consumer rights group Consumentenbond has said it will take Meta to court if it fails to comply with the law
The clampdown on privacy-threatening ‘pervert glasses’ continues, with Dutch eyewear retailer Hans Anders pulling the Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses from its online and high street stores in Belgium and the Netherlands indefinitely.
Hans Anders is part of the nexeye retail group, which operates over 400 stores across those two countries alone. When combined with its stores across Germany, Austria, and Sweden, it has 776 stores in total, although the Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses aren’t sold in the latter three regions.
The use of smart glasses has sparked a heated debate about whether these devices belong in public spaces, with concerns raised about general safety and privacy. Speaking with Reuters, a spokesperson for Hans Anders detailed the company’s decision to make the bold move, sharing the following:
"This decision follows the ongoing public and political debate surrounding smart glasses and the questions being raised about the conditions under which this technology can be used”.
One of the biggest areas of concern is women's privacy. According to a report from the NL Times, Meta's smart glasses have been used to capture footage of 'hundreds, maybe thousands' of Dutch women without their consent over the past few months. The outlet says the footage has been shared on messaging apps such as Telegram, as well as other harmful online sites.
The move follows a recent warning issued by the Dutch Data Protection Authority (AP), which said that photos and video footage of identifiable individuals taken using smart glasses can’t be shared without the individual's permission — though this is something that's clearly difficult to control in public spaces.
That’s not the only organization that’s decided to take an active stance against Meta. Earlier this week Consumentenbond, a consumer rights group, declared it will take Meta to court if the tech giant doesn’t amend its smart glasses to comply with privacy laws. That said, Meta says it’s always developing its smart glasses:
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
"Every pair with a camera has a bright light on the front that blinks when you take a photo or video — it can't be turned off, and the camera is disabled if someone covers or tampers with it," a Meta spokesperson said. Despite this indicator, there’s nothing in place to stop users from covering the light to stop others from knowing if they’re being filmed.
As far as retailers go, Hans Anders is one of the first to enact a public protest against smart glasses, joining the fight to protect the privacy and wellbeing of consumers. The Netherlands’ combat against these devices is only just beginning — and other nations have expressed similar concerns.
The UK is also taking similar measures to ensure public spaces are free from the looming threat of smart glasses. Popular pub chain Wetherspoons has banned the use of smart glasses in its pubs across the country, while the UK Cinema Association says movie theaters could also introduce similar smart glasses restrictions to prevent piracy, and even stop users from livestreaming movies to social media platforms .

articles.title: African startup exits: What the Class of 2016 returned
articles.text:
Ten years, $1.89 billion, and almost no liquidity.
Since its founding in 2016, Flutterwave has raised about $475 million, more than any of the 200-plus African startups founded that year. The 166 smallest companies in its cohort have raised roughly $210 million between them over the same decade.
This disparity in how one payments company from Lagos took in more than twice what two-thirds of its class managed in ten years combined is the story of Africa’s venture capital industry, shown in a year’s intake.
The mid-2010s were a good moment to start a company on the continent. Mobile money was spreading, smartphone prices were falling, and global funds were beginning to treat Africa as an asset class. In 2016, startups were founded across Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Egypt, Morocco, Uganda and Ghana, spanning fintech, agritech, e-commerce, cleantech and health.
TechCabal Insights tracked all of them through October 2026.
Venture funds are typically built with a 10-year lifespan, making a decade the industry’s own yardstick. By that timeline, the cohort has had time to do everything a startup can do: scale, sell, stall or stop. Together they raised about $1.89 billion, around 8.6% of the roughly $22 billion that flowed into African startups since 2016, but they produced almost no liquidity.
If you think of fundraising as a metric of success, then this reads like success. If you measure it by African startup exits, it reads like something else.
The concentration
Thirty-four companies account for $1.68 billion of the $1.89 billion. That is 89% of the cohort’s capital going to under a fifth of its members. More than 20 companies raised nothing. The median company raised about $1 million. The average, dragged by the top, was $9.45 million, a figure that describes few companies in the cohort.
Strip out the top 34, and the remaining 166 companies averaged $1.25 million each across ten years.
How concentrated was $1.89B of funding?
Flutterwave alone raised $475M — 25.1% of the cohort’s total capital.
What if the money were evenly distributed?
What does “39× more” actually mean?
And then there’s Flutterwave.
For most startups, $1.25 million over a decade finances a small team, a product that never gets the engineering it needs to scale, and a founder who spends much of the year raising money. Companies in that band were running a different business from the winners, one where survival was the daily objective and growth was a hope.
Power laws are normal in venture capital. Silicon Valley’s 2016 vintage concentrated too. What matters is what the concentration produces. In a functioning market, the winners exit, capital returns to funds, funds recycle it into the next cohort, and early employees become the next founders. The Class of 2016 generated very little of that.
The money also had a strong view about where problems were worth solving. Fintech took the largest share. Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa and Egypt took almost all of it. A founder in Kampala building for agriculture in 2016 competed for a different pool of capital compared with the one Lagos fintech drew on, and the Kampala pool was nearly empty.
The exits that were not exits
Twenty-seven companies were acquired or merged between 2019 and October 2026. Twenty-one of those deals had undisclosed prices, which is a finding in itself. Sellers publicise good numbers. A decade of silence on 21 transactions is a result.
The disclosed deals reveal a strategy that works for African startups seeking to offer returns to investors.
DocFox, a Johannesburg company selling client-onboarding software to banks, was acquired by the American banking-software firm nCino in March 2024. nCino announced a $75 million price, and its filings record $74.3 million paid in cash.
Syft Analytics, also from Johannesburg and bootstrapped from the start, agreed to sell to accounting platform Xero in September 2024 for up to $70 million, with $40 million upfront. It had reached $4.4 million in revenue from 75,000 customers across 80 countries. The deal closed in October 2025.
Neither company raised anything close to what it sold for. They are, by a distance, the best disclosed returns in the cohort. Neither was a consumer fintech platform. Neither was a household name in Lagos or Nairobi. Both sold software to businesses abroad in hard currency to a foreign strategic buyer. The decade’s two best outcomes came from companies that focused on a global market.
LXE Hearing, formerly HearX, took a different route to the same destination. The South African hearing-technology company raised $111 million over the decade and merged with the American firm Eargo in March 2025. The combined company is headquartered in San Jose and backed by $100 million from Patient Square Capital, an American private-equity firm. A success, and one that left the continent.
The rest of the acquisitions were consolidation. Zeepay, the Ghanaian fintech with operations across more than 10 African countries, acquired Zambia’s Mangwee. Treepz, a Nigerian-based mobility-as-a-service platform, bought Uganda’s Ugabus. These are category leaders buying licences and market share. Deals at that scale do not produce venture-scale returns.
The failures and what they cost
Six companies announced shutdowns publicly. Between them, they had raised about $55 million.
WhereIsMyTransport raised $28 million to map informal transport networks and closed in October 2023 after failing to raise again. Zumi, a Kenyan e-commerce platform, closed in March 2023, raising just under $1 million.
Snatcher, a South African retailer, closed in late 2024 following internal fraud. Bento Africa, a Nigerian payroll startup that raised $3.1 million, temporarily halted its operations in February 2025 after its founder resigned amid allegations of tax and pension irregularities, missed January salaries, and laid off its engineering team. Medsaf, which raised $7 million to digitise Nigeria’s pharmaceutical supply chain, shut down in 2024.
Read together, the causes do not rhyme. One ran out of investors. One ran out of market. One was stolen from. One was governed badly. One could not make the unit economics of physical distribution work. There is no distinctly African failure mode here, only the ordinary range of ways a company dies, compressed into a cohort.
The most instructive story did not end in a shutdown notice. Kobo360 raised more than $79 million in equity and debt, including backing from Juven, a Goldman Sachs spin-off, the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and TLcom Capital, to digitise freight across five African countries. It aggregated more than 50,000 trucks for clients including Unilever, Dangote and DHL.
The model consumed cash. Kobo360 paid transporters immediately and waited 30 to 90 days for large corporates to pay. When a bank partner cut its credit line over unserviced debt, the gap became unbridgeable. In March 2025, its venture backers sold their equity to co-founder Obi Ozor for an undisclosed sum, with the IFC saying publicly that it had not transferred its own stake. Ozor inherited a company owing more than ₦10 billion ($6.5 million) to banks. As of October 2026, Y Combinator lists Kobo360 as inactive. There was no liquidation, no filing and no announcement.
Beneath all of this sits the silent majority. Dozens of companies in the cohort now show no working website, no product, and no news in years. They were never liquidated. They stopped. No filing marks the moment, which is why the true failure rate of any African cohort runs higher than the announced one.
What the decade proved
Most of the cohort still exists in some form, and some of it is quietly profitable. African founders did not fail. The lesson is narrower and harder than that.
Legibility to foreign investors decided who got funded. The companies that raised the most were the ones whose business models a fund in London or San Francisco could invest in without understanding Lagos.
Returns followed a similar rule. The companies that returned the most sold software abroad in dollars.
The companies that took on the hardest local problems—freight, pharmaceutical distribution, transport data—raised the biggest rounds and returned the least.
Venture capital requires liquidity events, and this cohort produced almost none. After ten years and $1.89 billion, the two clearest wins were B2B software companies that raised less than $10 million and sold to foreign acquirers.
Africa’s demographic weight is not in doubt, and demand for technology in logistics, health, agriculture and finance will only grow. The Class of 2016 shows that a decade of venture capital was never going to be the mechanism that met it. The next cohort will need instruments this one lacked: revenue-based finance, local-currency debt, development finance, and patient capital with no ten-year clock.
Business as usual produced 34 winners and 166 companies averaging $1.25 million each. There is no sign it will do better the second time.
Data note: 200-plus startups founded in Africa in 2016, tracked through October 2026 across funding, mergers and acquisitions, and operating status. Compiled from the TechCabal Insights database alongside Africa: The Big Deal, Crunchbase, Tracxn, PitchBook and Briter, which do not always agree on founding year. Funding totals include disclosed equity, debt and grants. Rounds with undisclosed amounts are excluded, so the real total is higher than the figure reported here. 21 of the 27 acquisitions had undisclosed values.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. articles.title: Chinese NAND Maker YMTC Reportedly Expects Memory Shortage to Last Another Three Years
articles.text:
Monday, October 5th 2026
Chinese NAND Maker YMTC Reportedly Expects Memory Shortage to Last Another Three Years
Chinese NAND flash maker YMTC apparently expects the global memory shortage to last another three years. The claim comes from a profile of the company published by The Wire China, in which a YMTC employee, speaking anonymously, shared the outlook. The same employee said YMTC has raised prices for its chips and shifted capacity toward higher-margin products. The excerpt was shared on X by @jukan05, who read it as a NAND forecast, although the employee's wording covers memory in general. Three more years would put the end of the shortage somewhere around late 2029. This is one unnamed employee's words, of course, and not public guidance from YMTC.
That 2029 prediction is well past TrendForce's estimate, which has NAND flash supply loosening in the second half of 2027 as new capacity comes online. It sits closer to Micron's view, with CEO Sanjay Mehrotra saying last week that supply will be much tighter in 2027 and 2028. The shift in capacity matters too, especially for regular PC builders. Counterpoint Research ranked YMTC fourth in NAND bit shipments in Q2 with a 14% share, yet only fifth in revenue, since its product mix leans toward consumer applications. Moving capacity to higher-margin chips could leave less for consumer SSDs, even as YMTC works to double its wafer output with new fabs. Nevertheless, readers planning a storage upgrade shouldn't count on prices dropping anytime soon.

articles.title: Google cleared 300 hectares of Finnish forest for a data center, and regulators want answers
articles.text:
Cutting corners: Google recently announced a major expansion of its data center footprint in Finland. The US company plans to invest billions in the new infrastructure but is allegedly moving a bit too quickly with its forest-clearing plans. Regulators are now looking into the matter, and the outcome could have far-reaching consequences for the broader market.
Google was apparently so eager to build its new data center infrastructure in Finland that it began bulldozing large swaths of forest before the required environmental review of the full plan was complete. The work could now be suspended, just as other major data center projects are being delayed in the US and elsewhere around the world.
The issue surfaced last month, when Finland's Permit and Supervision Agency (Lupa- ja valvontavirasto, or LVV) asked Tuike Finland Oy (TFO) to explain its actions. TFO is Google's local company for the Finnish data center project, for which Mountain View is investing €13 billion in new AI-focused infrastructure.
In theory, TFO is supposed to operate in an environmentally friendly manner, with specific measures covering energy sustainability, job creation, and support for the local environment. Public reports cited by the LVV indicate that around 300 hectares of Finnish forest, roughly 420 football fields, had already been cleared before the project's environmental impact could be properly assessed.
Google argues that the forest clearing complied fully with Finnish laws and regulations. The site was properly surveyed before the bulldozers moved in, it said, so that no high-value environmental areas would be damaged. According to Hanna Halmeenpää, chair of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation, things are not going quite the way Google describes.
Halmeenpää said satellite imagery shows that areas that should have been protected have already been leveled. Beyond the loss of so much forest, the outcome could be dire for wildlife preservation. She is asking the LVV to halt the entire construction site so that authorities can determine whether Google tried to bring the forest down without first obtaining formal approval.
When it comes to environmental protection standards, Finland is one of the highest-rated countries in the world. Large data center buildouts like the one TFO is pursuing carry a significant environmental cost, both in physical land consumption and power requirements.
Google may be moving faster than the procedures of local environmental authorities, but communities are increasingly voicing their dissatisfaction with the unchecked expansion of Big Tech's AI data center plans. Most likely, sending chips into space will not ease the distrust of AI infrastructure that these mega-corporations are eagerly fostering down there.

articles.title: F1 in Bahrain... in Malaysia: The race needed a software update to start
articles.text:
Well, it’s safe to say no Bahrain Grand Prix has been affected by torrential rain quite like the 2026 race.
For one thing, it was held several thousand miles from Bahrain itself. The ongoing war with Iran ruled such things out, so the Sepang International Circuit in Malaysia stepped in to fill its spot. One of the best examples of a late-’90s “Tilke track”—named for its designer, Herman Tilke—it’s characterized by a couple of long straights and the always-brutal tropical weather that provides one of the toughest physical challenges on the calendar. And this weekend was no exception.
Heavy rain arrived about half an hour before the start time, delaying things significantly. Although the sport has two different kinds of treaded tires for use in the rain, the full wet tire generates so much spray, and such slow lap times, that it’s essentially only useful for circulating behind the safety car. If it’s wet enough to need it, it will be too wet to see where you’re going. The intermediate tire, by contrast, has much shallower grooves and is good for racing on damp but not soaked tracks, although it quickly overheats and degrades as the track dries.
Chaos ensues
The organizers decided on two formation laps behind the safety car; circulating at lower speed would allow the drivers to get an idea of the track conditions and let their intermediate tires pump some water off the track surface, the idea went. But that didn’t take into account a bug lurking in the cars’ software.
Driving slowly behind the safety car with reduced hybrid power in some parts of the track due to the extremely wet conditions convinced several of the cars that they were being tricked into breaking a hard-coded rule meant to prevent cheating, triggering an automatic 60-second shutdown of their electric motors that caused chaos as car after car slowed for the one in front, then took varying lengths of time to reboot their systems.
The cars assembled on the grid before the first attempt at a race start.
Credit:
JADE GAO / AFP
The cars assembled on the grid before the first attempt at a race start.
Credit:
JADE GAO / AFP
“It was like the Lego race,” said Max Verstappen of Red Bull, referring back to the human-size Lego cars that F1 used for a driver parade at the 2025 Miami Grand Prix. “At some point, we were five-wide on the straight because we couldn’t understand what was going on. Then we did a lap and then I see eight other cars crawling still… I mean that’s not what you want, right, for the sport.”
The race organizers aborted the entire start. The bug had never come up in testing, and the FIA had to hastily write and distribute a software update to fix it. An hour after the first aborted start, the cars lined up on the grid again, ready to finally race.
“In wet conditions, there are some different software settings for the cars for safety reasons to reduce the power in certain sectors from the maximum to a lower level,” explained Nikolas Tombazis, head of single-seater racing at the FIA. “And this year, we’ve had very little wet weather running or none at all, almost. So it wasn’t maybe adequately checked.”
The software was developed by the FIA with the teams and engine makers. “So it’s common software for all cars,” Tombazis said. “And basically there was a combination of events between those software settings and the fact that some cars went incredibly slow during the formation lap and those entered a sort of a bug into the software which was stopping those cars to reaccelerate and to go to normal speeds.”
“And as a result of that, we had quite a few cars affected by that problem and which caused them to stop,” Tombazis said. “Perhaps I should also add that as soon as the formation lap problems happened, we understood the problem very soon afterward and we issued some an updated software to the teams. It took about sort of 20 minutes for the software to be issued. Some explanations teams had to update the software in the car. They had to ask a couple of questions and we had to make sure they all had done that work. So all of that took maybe about 20 minutes or so and so that was what caused that delay for the second start.”
(Indeed, the delay led Verstappen to joke that his team got their update applied faster thanks to their Oracle-supplied data connection.)
More chaos
The delay to the start was long enough that the rain had abated and the puddles of standing water had all drained, leading just over half the grid to gamble that it was dry enough to risk starting on either the soft or medium slick. Only nine drivers opted for the intermediate tire, including Verstappen (on pole), championship leader Kimi Antonelli, and his Mercedes teammate George Russell. Lewis Hamilton, starting second, was among those choosing to start on either the soft or medium slick tire; this was a mistake, as the formation lap proved the track was still much wetter than expected—too wet for slicks, certainly.
So it wasn’t a surprise to see the slick-shod cars quickly left behind as they struggled to put down power on the wet tarmac. Despite being on the intermediates, Verstappen got a terrible start and was left in third, behind both Mercedes.
“I was not surprised because my start was horrendous,” Verstappen said. “Again, dropping the clutch and not having power. The engine just completely died on me. But then you just have to settle in, try not to overreact as well, and just slot in, try to keep your position there. The race is long, a lot of things can happen, and step by step, I could close the gap.”
And he did, passing Russell on lap six and then closing up behind Antonelli quickly thereafter.
Lewis Hamilton and the other slick-shod cars got left behind at the start as track conditions proved far too wet for their tires.
Credit:
Jayce Illman/Getty Images
Lewis Hamilton and the other slick-shod cars got left behind at the start as track conditions proved far too wet for their tires.
Credit:
Jayce Illman/Getty Images
Meanwhile, at the back of the pack, some of the drivers who started on slicks made stops to change to the intermediates. McLaren’s Oscar Piastri was among the first who quickly began scything through the field; within a lap, he’d caught up and passed everyone who went by as he stopped. Others followed suit, though Hamilton was not among them, telling his race engineer on lap 5 that he’d gamble on the conditions coming back to suit him. It was a decision that would show the depth of experience that the seven-time world champion brings to the sport.
The race restarted on lap 13, and Verstappen pounced on Antonelli, taking the lead, with Russell following into second. Hamilton, meanwhile, was in 15th, although not for long. Within a lap, he was up to 11th. Within 10 laps of the restart, he was in 5th.
Slightly further back, another legend of the sport was also having a good day.
Fernando Alonso’s Aston Martin might have been a laughingstock at the start of the season, as it was multiple seconds slower than the cars of the frontrunners, but the Adrian Newey-designed aerodynamic update that arrived in Hungary closed some of the gap to the rest of the field. And Honda has now introduced a second power unit upgrade that has helped drivability even while at a power deficit to the others. It’s not quite as effective a package as Hamilton’s Ferrari, but Alonso began moving forward, and by lap 40, he was in 10th place, the final points-paying position.
Fernando Alonso will race in F1 for at least one more year; he entered the sport in 2001.
Credit:
Jayce Illman/Getty Images
Fernando Alonso will race in F1 for at least one more year; he entered the sport in 2001.
Credit:
Jayce Illman/Getty Images
Up front, Verstappen was building a commanding lead, and Antonelli had overtaken Russell for second, having first asked the team unsuccessfully if they’d simply tell Russell to let him by.
Extra chaos
Then Alex Albon’s Williams suffered a gearbox failure on lap 43, triggering a virtual safety car. Verstappen and Hamilton stopped for tires, followed a lap later by Antonelli, Russell, and the other Red Bull of Isack Hadjar. The broken transmission of the Williams prevented it from being easily moved, so a full safety car was declared, bunching the pack up.
The race would restart on lap 52 (of 55), but not before Russell came to a stop by the side of the track just past the pit exit on lap 50. “Another [power unit] failure, when we were on course for a pretty certain podium. It’s a tough one to take. It’s unfortunately happened too many times this season, and, yeah, this is just where we are,” Russell said after the race as he acknowledged his title chances for 2026 were over.
The final three laps were frenetic. Hamilton passed Hadjar for third, a wonderful recovery drive back to the podium after being more than a minute off the lead at one point during the race. His Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc trailed behind, also passing the second Red Bull and fully salvaging Ferrari’s day. Ahead of the red cars, Antonelli was closing down on Verstappen but without being close enough to attempt an overtake. And Alonso was making moves, too, ending his day in eighth place, Aston’s best finish of the year.
Everyone knows this looks bad
Kimi Antonelli (R) looks set to join Max Verstappen (M) and Lewis Hamilton (R) as one of F1’s greats.
Credit:
Clive Mason/Getty Images
Kimi Antonelli (R) looks set to join Max Verstappen (M) and Lewis Hamilton (R) as one of F1’s greats.
Credit:
Clive Mason/Getty Images
On a chaotic day, F1’s biggest talents shone their brightest. Between them, Hamilton, Verstappen, and Alonso have 13 world championships, and this year, Antonelli has given every indication his name belongs alongside theirs, even if he does need to do something about his weakness for exceeding track limits. And the racing we got was actually rather thrilling. But some of that was still overshadowed by all the chaos that had to happen first. And everyone knows where to point the finger.
“The power units are exceptionally complicated. The more complicated you make things, the more there is to go wrong. So that is obviously something we need to bear in mind for the future,” said Russell. “It just proves that we shouldn’t have any of that stuff on the electronic side,” said McLaren’s Lando Norris.
“It is clear the regs are extremely complicated for the drivers, for the teams, for the PUs, for the manufacturers. It is too complicated,” said Williams’ Carlos Sainz. “Again, my only question mark is who, five years ago, decided that this was the direction to go? We are doing the best with what we are given as a sport and as regulations. The FIA and F1 are doing the best they can with what was decided four or five years ago, but clearly what was decided four or five years ago is wrong.”
Next year, the power units will be rebalanced with more power from the V6 and less from the electric motor, with another change coming in 2028. Then it’s all change in 2031 (or perhaps 2030), when F1 will likely go back to V8s and much smaller hybrid systems.
Jonathan is the Automotive Editor at Ars Technica. He has a BSc and PhD in Pharmacology. In 2014 he decided to indulge his lifelong passion for the car by leaving the National Human Genome Research Institute and launching Ars Technica's automotive coverage. He lives in Washington, DC.

articles.title: TikTok rolls out an AI shopping assistant and one-click checkout | TechCrunch
articles.text:
TikTok announced Monday that it’s launching an AI shopping assistant and a new in-app checkout feature that lets users buy directly from brands.
TikTok describes its new Shopping Assistant as a conversational AI agent designed to help users discover and purchase products. The company says the assistant understands context and remembers users’ preferences and needs throughout the conversation. It offers real-time, AI-powered shopping guidance, such as product details, shipping information, sizing, availability, and help completing a purchase.
As for the new checkout feature, TikTok says users can buy directly from a brand from their For You feed (the app’s main, algorithm-driven video feed) with one click.
The new features could allow TikTok to capture more of users’ shopping journeys, and potentially more transaction value, without sending them elsewhere. By pairing a shopping assistant with direct payments, TikTok is turning its impulse-driven discovery feed into a place where users can get answers to questions about a product and make a purchase on the spot.
By building an AI assistant for shopping directly in its app, TikTok also appears to be hoping that users will stay within its platform when they have questions about a product, rather than turning to outside AI tools like OpenAI’s ChatGPT.
The company says these new features are being built in partnership with commerce platforms and payment providers including Salesforce, Shopify, Shoplazza, and Stripe, among others.
While TikTok Shop, the app’s in-house marketplace, has been the platform’s main engine for the company’s e-commerce ambitions, these new features broaden its approach beyond the existing shopping hub. Rather than relying on TikTok Shop to drive purchases, the social network is now integrating shopping tools more directly into the broader app, including the For You feed.
The expansion comes as TikTok’s influence on shopping continues to grow. According to TikTok’s Economic Impact Report that was released last week, activity on the platform helped generate $81 billion in GDP for U.S. businesses, while 54 million Americans said they had purchased a product after watching a TikTok video.
TikTok Shop launched in the U.S. in September 2023. The market research firm eMarketer estimates it generated about $15.8 billion in U.S. sales in 2025, representing roughly 18% of all U.S. social commerce.

articles.title: Passe Navigo à 93,40 €, ticket unique à 2,45 € : la nouvelle grille tarifaire qui se prépare pour 2027
articles.text:
Nouvelle augmentation de prix en vue pour les Franciliens. Selon les informations diffusées par France 3 Paris Île-de-France ce lundi 5 octobre 2026, les tarifs du passe Navigo devraient encore augmenter. Au 1er janvier 2026, le passe Navigo mensuel avait déjà augmenté de 2,3 %, passant de 88,80 € à 90,80 €. La barre symbolique des 90 € avait été franchie. Mais, déjà, une nouvelle hausse se profile quelques mois plus tard.
Selon nos confrères, qui indiquent avoir consulté le rapport d’orientations budgétaires 2027 d’Île-de-France Mobilités, voici les nouveaux tarifs qui devraient être ceux des forfaits Navigo pour 2027.
| Forfait | Tarif 2026 | Tarif 2027 | Augmentation | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Navigo annuel | 998,80 € | 1 027,80 € | + 29 € | 
| Navigo mensuel | 90,80 € | 93,40 € | + 2,60 € | 
| Imagine R | 401,30 € | 413,70 € | + 12,40 € | 
France 3 évoque aussi une réflexion sur la fusion des tickets bus-tram (2,05 € aujourd’hui) et métro-RER (2,55 €) en un titre unique, vendu 2,45 €. Un trajet en bus ou en tramway coûterait alors 40 centimes de plus, un trajet en métro ou en RER 10 centimes de moins.
Quant au passe Navigo Liberté+, France 3 ne précise pas s’il sera concerné. Ses tarifs avaient toutefois suivi la hausse en 2026. Le trajet en métro, train ou RER est passé de 1,99 € à 2,04 €, et celui en bus ou en tram de 1,60 € à 1,64 €.
Les nouveaux tarifs du passe Navigo doivent encore être votés
Le rapport cité par France 3 doit être présenté au conseil d’administration d’Île-de-France Mobilités le jeudi 15 octobre. Il ne fixe pas encore les prix, qui devront ensuite être votés pour devenir officiels. Sollicité par le média, Île-de-France Mobilités n’a pas commenté ces tarifs.
Le passe Navigo mensuel augmente chaque année depuis 2023, dont un bond de 11,84 % cette année-là. Il est ensuite passé à 86,40 € en 2024, 88,80 € en 2025 puis 90,80 € en 2026. En 2023, Île-de-France Mobilités et l’État ont conclu un accord portant sur le financement des transports franciliens jusqu’en 2031. Selon cet accord, la hausse du prix du passe Navigo doit être limitée à « l’inflation +1 % au maximum » à partir de 2025. IDFM présente ces hausses comme nécessaires pour financer plus de 300 km de nouvelles lignes ferrées d’ici 2031, dont les lignes 15 à 18 du Grand Paris Express.
Comme à chaque hausse, les associations d’usagers devraient pointer l’écart entre les prix et la qualité du service.

articles.title: Data centers to factory floors: Walden robots learn on the job - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Physical AI’s bottleneck shifts from what robots can do to whether factories trust them
AI is moving beyond the data centers where models are trained and onto factory floors where machines must handle constant change.
But traditional industrial robots work behind a cage, repeat a single task and were never designed for the complexities of today’s market. Manufacturers now want general-purpose machines that can switch tasks and improve as processes evolve. The hard part is deploying it, according to Adrien Gaidon (pictured, right), co-founder and chief strategy officer of Walden Robotics Inc.
“If you’re changing things and you have machines that cannot change and continuously learn in deployment, then you become a burden,” Gaidon said. “What we do is we do machines that continuously learn from deployment and adapt so customers can change their mind and improve the process and give them the superpower to change even more and faster.”
Gaidon and John Mancuso (left), vice president of field engineering at CoreWeave Inc., spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier and Dave Vellante at Fully Connected, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how cloud infrastructure, simulation and human assistance help robots learn and adapt on factory floors. (* Disclosure below.)
Physical AI moves from data centers to the factory floor
Walden spun out of Toyota Research Institute in January 2026 and launched with $300 million in July to put general-purpose robots to work in manufacturing. Its robots have worked full production shifts alongside people since May. They handle machine tending, parts kitting, and subassembly, tasks manufacturers had either failed to automate or never tried, Gaidon explained.
“There’s half a million open positions for machinists in the U.S. because it’s a hard job and it requires skills,” Gaidon said. “But part of that job does not require the craft or the human creativity.”
Getting a robot to that point takes serious compute long before it reaches a production line. CoreWeave, which has been betting on physical AI, also brings mechanical engineers and robotics experts into customer engagements alongside its infrastructure, Mancuso explained.
“In the end, before a model is ever going to do something in the physical world, it’s going to have a tremendous amount of simulation that happens in the virtual world,” Mancuso said. “We’re providing the infrastructure.”
But while simulation in data centers can make a robot useful, but it can’t make it perfect. Walden pairs autonomous robots with remote human assistants. The setup is comparable to automated looms of 120 years ago, when one person oversaw 40 machines, Gaidon noted.
“Our robots are autonomous, but they know how to call for help,” Gaidon said. “They know when they need some assistance – and that assistance feeds the most valuable data to improve over time.”

articles.title: OpenAI is adding invisible watermarks to ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU
articles.text:
OpenAI is preparing to add invisible watermarks to text generated by ChatGPT and Codex in the European Union.
The watermark will not be visible when you read or copy the text. Instead, OpenAI says its new textGrain technology slightly changes the model's word choices to create a statistical pattern that can later be detected.
"Over the coming weeks, we will add an invisible watermark to eligible ChatGPT and Codex text output in the European Union," OpenAI explained.
OpenAI is not making this a global default yet.
Starting today, API developers worldwide can opt in to watermarking for supported models, but it remains disabled by default.
The company is also opening applications for its watermark detector, although access will initially be limited to approved researchers and expert organizations.
OpenAI admits its AI watermark can disappear when you edit the text
Text watermarking is far from perfect, and OpenAI's own tests show that fairly normal editing can significantly reduce its ability to detect AI-generated text.
"In an evaluation of 400-token passages, replacing 10% of words with synonyms reduced detection from about 92% to 66%. Replacing 25% of words reduced it to 17%," OpenAI noted.
At a 1% false-positive target, OpenAI detected the watermark in about 80% of 200-token psychology responses, compared with roughly 95% when the text reached 400 tokens.
Detection was even worse for subjects such as mathematics, where the model has less freedom to choose different words.
"The absence of a detected watermark does not prove human authorship," OpenAI warned. "Text generated with OpenAI tools may be too short, edited, or translated for detection to work reliably."
OpenAI also says a detected watermark does not reveal who generated the text, their account, prompt, or conversation, and it cannot tell how much of the final work was written or edited by a human.
Interestingly, OpenAI says watermarking does not meaningfully affect the quality of GPT-6 Astra, with benchmark results remaining broadly similar when textGrain is enabled.

articles.title: Elon Musk reconnaît que les Robotaxis Tesla voient mal certains animaux la nuit
articles.text:
Les Robotaxis de Tesla circulent désormais jusqu’à 23 heures à Austin. Elon Musk donne l’exemple d’un chaton gris sur un bitume gris, encore difficile à repérer pour ses voitures autonomes.
Le compte officiel Robotaxi a annoncé ce nouvel horaire sur X. « Le principal problème que nous essayons de résoudre, c’est de nous assurer de ne pas écraser d’animaux de compagnie quand ils sont difficiles à voir la nuit. Nous essayons littéralement d’éviter des chatons gris sur du bitume gris dans le noir », a répondu Elon Musk trente-cinq minutes plus tard.
Il a fait cet aveu alors que Tesla attend le vote des Vingt-Sept sur son système d’aide à la conduite FSD Supervised, repoussé à décembre. Des deux côtés de l’Atlantique, Tesla n’équipe ses voitures que de caméras, sans lidar ni radar. Dans l’obscurité, ce choix technique est mis à l’épreuve.
La nuit, point faible des caméras de Tesla
Lors du lancement à Austin, en juin 2025, Tesla proposait des courses jusqu’à minuit. Fin août 2026, le constructeur a avancé la dernière heure de prise en charge à 22 heures. Avec l’extension du 2 octobre, les clients d’Austin peuvent réserver un trajet jusqu’à 23 heures, soit une heure de moins qu'à l’ouverture du service.
Tesla fait rouler ses Robotaxis dans sept villes américaines, dont Miami et la baie de San Francisco, avec encore un employé de sécurité à bord dans certaines d’entre elles selon la réglementation locale. Partout, le constructeur confie la détection des obstacles à ses seules caméras. Pour une caméra, un chaton gris sur un bitume gris est une tache presque invisible, faute de contraste, surtout quand l’éclairage public est faible.
En juillet, lors des premiers essais du Cybercab sans volant ni pédales, on vous disait que la fiabilité de ces caméras peut diminuer par faible luminosité ou sous une forte pluie. Waymo, le principal concurrent de Tesla, ajoute des lidars et des radars aux caméras de ses véhicules. Avec un lidar, la distance d’un objet est calculée à partir du temps de retour d’impulsions laser, quelle que soit la lumière ambiante. La couleur du pelage d'un chat ne change alors rien à sa détection. Dans sa réponse, Elon Musk n’a évoqué aucun changement de capteurs, et Tesla n'a annoncé aucune date pour un service après 23 heures.
Tesla attend toujours le feu vert européen pour son FSD
Tesla installe le même type de caméras sur ses voitures vendues en Europe, où le constructeur demande l’homologation du FSD Supervised. Avec ce système d’aide à la conduite de niveau 2, le conducteur est seul responsable et doit garder les mains prêtes à reprendre le volant. L’autorité néerlandaise d’homologation (RDW) l’a autorisé en avril, après dix-huit mois d’essais et 1,6 million de kilomètres parcourus sur les routes européennes. Sept pays de l’Union, dont la Belgique et le Danemark, acceptent aujourd’hui le système, mais ils ne réunissent qu’environ 12 % de la population européenne. Pour une homologation à l’échelle de l'Union, Tesla doit convaincre au moins quinze des vingt-sept États membres, à condition qu’ils réunissent 65 % de la population.
Pour défendre son dossier, Tesla affiche un taux d’accident 4,1 fois plus faible qu’en conduite manuelle. Aucun organisme indépendant n’a toutefois vérifié ces statistiques maison, et plusieurs gouvernements reprochent au système sa tolérance aux excès de vitesse. L’office fédéral allemand des véhicules à moteur (KBA) a ainsi émis des réserves, car Tesla permet au FSD Supervised de choisir une vitesse jusqu’à 50 % supérieure à la limitation détectée. À Bruxelles, une association de piétons a même relevé des dépassements sur 55 % des zones à 30 km/h testées.
C'est demain que le comité technique des véhicules à moteur (TCMV) de la Commission européenne doit se réunir, mais ne consacrer que vingt-cinq minutes au dossier, sans vote. D’après le ministère allemand des Transports, le premier scrutin possible aura lieu en décembre, et Berlin n'a pas encore arrêté sa position.

articles.title: Fitbit Edge : on en sait beaucoup plus sur le futur bracelet de Google
articles.text:
Déjà aperçu furtivement lors de l’évènement de lancement de la gamme Pixel en août dernier, le futur bracelet Fitbit Edge de Google se dévoile à travers de nouvelles fiches techniques et images partagées par Android Headlines. Ce modèle se positionnerait à mi-chemin entre la Pixel Watch et le Fitbit Air.
Un design qui n’est pas sans rappeler un autre produit Google
Comme vous pouvez le voir sur les images ci-dessous, le boîtier du Fitbit Edge arbore un écran ovale avec des bordures relativement fines. Les visuels montrent une interface adaptée à ce format allongé, affichant l’heure, la date ainsi que des raccourcis pour la fréquence cardiaque, le nombre de pas et le lancement d’une séance de sport. Sur les tranches gauche et droite, de petites bandes métalliques trahissent la présence probable de mesures ECG, et le design global rappelle clairement la formule adoptée par le Fitbit Charge 6.
Source : Android Headlines
Google mise sur la cohérence avec son écosystème en proposant des coloris s’accordant directement avec les nuances des Pixel 11 Pro : noir, vert et orange, baptisés respectivement Obsidian, Olive et Canyon. Le système d’attache utilise un mécanisme de pincement situé au dos pour changer de bracelet facilement.
Des fonctionnalités « entre deux »
Sous le capot, le Fitbit Edge embarquerait un GPS, un altimètre pour le suivi des étages et de l’altitude, ainsi qu’une fonction de reconnaissance automatique des activités physiques. Contrairement au Fitbit Air qui fait l’impasse sur l’affichage, ce modèle prend en charge les notifications de base et intègre certaines applications pratiques comme Google Maps, le contrôle de la musique, ou encore la fonction de localisation du téléphone.
L’appareil fonctionne aussi bien sous Android que sous iOS, ce qui n’est pas le cas de la Pixel Watch 5 qui est réservée à l’écosystème Android. Côté autonomie, la batterie peut tenir jusqu’à sept jours avec une seule charge (selon Google), ce qui est bien mieux que la plupart des montres connectées. Le tarif évoqué se situerait entre 149 et 199 dollars pour une commercialisation qui pourrait arriver dès ce mois d’octobre.

articles.title: Prime Deal Days gegen Black Friday: Lohnt sich das Warten?
articles.text:
Prime Deal Days gegen Black Friday: Bei diesen Produkten lohnt sich das Warten
In den vergangenen Jahren hat Amazon das Jahresendgeschäft regelmäßig mit einem zweiten Prime Day im Oktober eröffnet – teilweise, wie auch in diesem Jahr, gleich an mehreren Tagen. Dahinter steckt gerade in Zeiten mit knappen finanziellen Spielräumen bei den Verbraucher:innen eine einfache Überlegung: Jeder kann sein Budget nur einmal ausgeben – und wenn Handelsunternehmen ihre Kund:innen möglichst früh mit als attraktiv empfundenen Angeboten erreichen, haben sie bessere Chancen darauf, dass das Geld in ihrer Kasse landet.
Doch genauso lange wie es die Konkurrenz zwischen den Prime Deal Days oder Prime Days im Oktober und den traditionellen Tagen rund um den Black Friday gibt, hält sich die Frage, wann mit den besseren Angeboten zu rechnen ist. Lohnt es sich anlässlich der Prime Deal Days am 6. und 7. Oktober zuzuschlagen – oder sollte man lieber bis Ende November warten?
Die Angebotsplattform Mydealz hat jetzt Daten ausgewertet, die zeigen, dass die Antwort auf diese Frage nicht eindeutig ist, es aber dennoch Anhaltspunkte für Kaufentscheidungen gibt. Im Rahmen der Analyse wurden 3.304 Deals aus dem vergangenen Jahr untersucht: 1.540 Angebote von den Amazon Prime Deal Days am 7. und 8. Oktober 2025 sowie 1.764 Angebote vom Black Friday am 28. November, der ja bei Amazon erst der Einstieg in die Black Week mit dem Cyber Monday ist.
Mydealz gehört zum Plattformbetreiber Atolls und ist eine der größten deutschen Communitys für Angebote und Rabattaktionen. Hier teilen die Nutzer:innen Informationen über Händlerangebote, Gutscheine und Preisaktionen und bewerten diese gemeinschaftlich. Die Auswertung ist deshalb also keine repräsentative Preisstudie für den gesamten deutschen Handel, kann aber angesichts der riesigen Community durchaus Aussagekraft besitzen, weil sie gut aufzeigt, wie sich Preise identischer Produkte zwischen zwei großen Shopping-Events entwickelt haben. Das Gute daran: Die Terminkonstellation ist im Vergleich zum vergangenen Jahr – bis auf die Verschiebung um einen Tag – nahezu identisch.
Bei gleichen Produkten gewinnt meist der Black Friday
Vor allem bei jenen Angeboten, bei denen exakt dasselbe Produkt rabattiert wurde. Hier wurden identische Modelle und Varianten als Neuware sowie jeweils der niedrigste auf Mydealz gepostete Preis betrachtet. 27 der 41 Produkte waren demnach am Black Friday günstiger, lediglich sieben während der Prime Deal Days. Weitere sieben kosteten bei beiden Aktionen gleich viel. Im Median lag der Black-Friday-Preis sechs Prozent niedriger. Deswegen macht gerade bei größeren Anschaffungen im Techniksektor das Warten oft einen Unterschied, weil eben der Black Friday sechs Wochen weiter im Produktzyklus liegt.
Die Untersuchung nennt hier zwei Beispiele: Die Playstation 5 Pro kostete während der Prime Deal Days 709,99 Euro, am Black Friday dagegen 679 Euro. Noch größer fiel die Differenz bei der Nintendos Switch 2 im Bundle mit Mario Kart World aus: 477,49 Euro im Oktober standen 389,54 Euro im November gegenüber. Auch bei Fernsehern und Haushaltsrobotern waren diesbezüglich die Unterschiede bemerkenswert groß. Der Samsung S90F mit 65 Zoll kostete am Black Friday 1.224,55 Euro statt 1.435 Euro während der Prime-Aktion. Beim Mova Z60 Ultra Roller sank der Preis sogar von 1.185 auf 849 Euro. Der Ecovacs Goat A1600 RTK wurde im November für 615,99 Euro angeboten, während er im Oktober noch 799 Euro gekostet hatte.
Prime-Rabatte wirken größer – sind es aber nicht unbedingt
Schaut man auf die gesamten Kategorien, spricht ebenfalls vieles dafür, bis zum Black Friday zu warten, der ja den gesamten Handel und nicht bloß Amazon betrifft. Bei Gaming-Artikeln, Fernsehern und Audiogeräten wurden stets mehr Deals als „heiß“ von der Community bewertet, die den Black Friday betrafen – und keines der sieben hier direkt vergleichbaren Angebote für Fernseher, Kopfhörer und Lautsprecher war im Oktober günstiger. Bei Saugrobotern und anderen Reinigungsgeräten gab es während der Prime Deal Days zwar etwa doppelt so viele Angebote, doch lediglich 16 Prozent wurden rund um den Oktober-Prime Day als heiß eingestuft – gegenüber 24 Prozent am Black Friday.
Ähnlich war das Bild bei Spielzeug und Lego sowie Sport- und Outdoor-Produkten, wo der Black Friday in der Auswertung besser abschnitt. Gerade Lego-Sets waren im November entweder gleich teuer oder günstiger, auch bei Sport- und Outdoor-Produkten gab es deutlich mehr besonders stark bewertete Deals. Keinen eindeutigen Gewinner sieht die Auswertung dagegen bei Computern und Elektronik, Küchen- und Haushaltsgeräten, Smartphones und Tablets sowie Produkten aus dem Bereich Wohnen.
Ein scheinbarer Widerspruch ist dabei die vermeintliche und die ausgewiesene Ersparnis. Denn zunächst wirkten die Prime-Angebote im Hinblick auf die ausgewiesene Ersparnis gegenüber dem jeweils nächstbesten Vergleichspreis attraktiver – diese betrug dort im Median 23 Prozent, während es am Black Friday „nur“ 20 Prozent waren. Doch der direkte Vergleich identischer Produkte zeigt, dass zahlreiche Artikel Ende November noch einmal günstiger angeboten wurden, sodass auch die Mitbewerber weniger teuer waren. Kaufinteressent:innen sollten sich deshalb nicht in erster Linie an der Ersparnis im Vergleich zum nächstbesten Preis orientieren, sondern auf den Vergleichsmarkt schauen.
Amazon-Geräte sind im Oktober häufig interessanter
Allerdings gibt es auch Warengruppen, bei denen die Prime Deal Days Vorteile haben. Das gilt vor allem für Amazons eigene Hardware von Echo, Fire TV, Kindle bis hin zu Ring und anderen Smarthome-Devices aus dem Amazon-Ökosystem. Hier zählte Mydealz 22 Deals, während es zum Black Friday nur vier waren. Das dürfte allerdings auch damit zu tun haben, dass Amazons Eigenmarken (bis hin zu den Amazon-Basics-Produkten) mehr Aufmerksamkeit erfahren als zum Black Friday, an dem die gesamte Branche mit Angeboten kommt.
Auffällig ist aber, dass die Prime Deal Days zuletzt stark von günstigen Alltagsartikeln geprägt waren. Mehr als jeder Dritte (36 Prozent) kostete weniger als 25 Euro. Zehn der zwölf Prime-Produkte unter den 20 populärsten Angeboten lagen unter 40 Euro. Auch bei Mode und Schuhen, Beauty und Körperpflege, Büchern, Filmen und Musik sowie Werkzeug und Garten schnitten die Prime Deal Days vergleichsweise gut ab. Bei Beauty-Produkten lag die mediane Ersparnis bei 27 Prozent, am Black Friday waren es 18 Prozent. Deutlich größer war das Angebot auch bei Vorrats- und Haushaltsartikeln.
Black Friday ist auch ein Gutschein-Event
Allerdings gehört zum Vergleich der beiden Shopping-Termine auch eine weitere Erkenntnis: Denn neben klassischen Produktschnäppchen waren es vor allem Rabattcodes und Gutscheine sowie Cashback-Aktionen, die am Black Friday eine Rolle spielen (458 solche Angebote listet Mydealz im Vergleich zu 13 zum Prime Day im Oktober letzten Jahres).
Wer also nicht nur auf bestimmte niedrige Angebotspreise wartet, sondern darauf hofft, Deals mit Rabattcodes, Bonuspunkten oder Cashback zu verknüpfen, sollte eher auf den Black Friday und die Woche Ende November schielen.
Etwas entspannt haben sich die Prime Days aber im Hinblick auf das Tagesgefüge. Die Mydealz-Zahlen zeigen, dass man nicht zwingend am ersten Morgen zuschlagen muss. Einerseits wurden am ersten Aktionstag des vergangenen Jahres 1.154 Deals beschrieben und am zweiten nur 372. Anteilig war der zweite Tag aber sogar erfolgreicher: Denn 44 Prozent der dort geposteten Angebote wurden als heiß eingestuft, am ersten Tag waren es 37 Prozent.
Für größere Anschaffungen ergibt sich daraus eine pragmatische Strategie: Wer nicht sofort kaufen muss, kann den Preis der Prime Deal Days zunächst als Orientierung nehmen und Ende November noch einmal vergleichen. Anders ist der Fall bei Amazon-Hardware und einigen außergewöhnlich starken Einzelangeboten zu sehen, insbesondere wenn es sich um Vorjahresware handelt, die hier abverkauft wird. Dennoch sollten Kund:innen einen kühlen Kopf behalten – denn auch und gerade bei den groß inszenierten Shopping-Events ist ein hoher Rabatt nicht automatisch ein guter Preis.

articles.title: Former OpenAI safety employee says company’s safety culture is broken — exits company after failed kill switch and July HuggingFace hack
articles.text:
Former OpenAI safety employee says company’s safety culture is broken — exits company after failed kill switch and July HuggingFace hack
‘Move fast and break things’ isn’t a good idea when it comes to AI.
David Robinson, an OpenAI Safety Transparency Lead who just left the company after working at the company for more than three years, said that the company’s safety culture is broken. According to his essay published by The Atlantic, he argued that OpenAI has a reactive approach to safety that focuses on fixing problems only when they emerge. This stance would effectively guarantee failures, with Robinson citing multiple incidents like the HuggingFace hack that an AI model executed in July 2026 and a more recent incident in which an AI “kill switch” failed to stop a rogue agent.
He said that Silicon Valley lacks the "wisdom about what it means to care for people,” he wrote. “This moment needs a degree of humility that isn’t natural for people who have succeeded through their extreme confidence.”
Because of this, he said that the industry should rely on safety experts that already exist in other fields, like nuclear engineering or aviation. These industries have learned about safety, redundancy, and planning through disasters that have claimed thousands of lives across hundreds of incidents, some of which occurred more than half a century ago but still clearly echo today. These lessons were written in blood, and experts from various sectors worked together to build the systems, procedures, and models we rely on today, helping ensure that no single machine failure or human error would result in tragedy.
“OpenAI and other labs are growing and deploying frontier AI with far less redundancy and rigor than this, even though the harm from an irreversible loss of control would be much greater than the harm from any single meltdown,” Robinson argues. “Even short of a full loss of control, we could see autonomous swarms of AI agents that act without human permission.” This is exactly what Anthropic’s Dario Amodei has been warning about, leading to his proposal of slowing down frontier AI development, to which OpenAI’s Sam Altman and SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk agreed.
However, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, who supplies the majority of the AI chips needed to train these models, disagreed with the Anthropic CEO’s proposal. If the AI experiments have become unsafe, “we have to shut the labs down,” Huang said in an interview. He also cited civil and criminal liabilities that entities may face for rogue agents but called Dario’s concerns a “distraction.” The White House soon called over the heads of the biggest AI companies for high-level discussions, after which President Donald Trump came up with a document where Google, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, and Nvidia promised to “self-police” AI development.
Robinson didn’t talk about rules and regulations and instead targeted the core culture of safety (or lack thereof) and OpenAI’s penchant for “iterative deployment,” or more commonly known as trial and error. He said that he should have stayed inside the company and fought for a fundamental shift in its thinking, but said that this was next to impossible because of how fast things were going inside the startup. It’s for this reason that he left his job and decided to tackle the problem from the outside.

articles.title: Presente para crianças: Nintendo Switch OLED alcança o menor preço de 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Presente para crianças: Nintendo Switch OLED alcança o menor preço de 2026
Bundle do Nintendo Switch OLED com Super Mario Wonder e 3 meses de Nintendo Switch Online fica mais acessível com pagamento via Pix
O Nintendo Switch OLED entrou em oferta por R$ 1.831,08 no Pix com o cupom NINTENDO na Amazon. O bundle do console da Nintendo com o jogo Super Mario Wonder, lançado por R$ 2.699, fica 32% mais barato faltando poucos dias para o Dia das Crianças.
O Nintendo Switch OLED adota uma tela OLED de 7 polegadas com resolução HD (720p) e taxa de atualização de 60 Hz no Modo Portátil, reproduzindo cores mais vivas que a versão padrão. O videogame traz uma dock para ser conectada à TV, promovendo jogos em telas maiores com resolução Full HD.
O console é equipado com o chip customizado Nvidia Tegra X1 e 4 GB de RAM, conseguindo executar jogos com gráficos 3D. Os 64 GB de armazenamento interno podem ser um pouco limitados, mas é possível expandir a memória usando cartões microSD de até 2 TB.
Um ótimo companheiro para viagens, o Nintendo Switch OLED garante de 4 a 9 horas de entretenimento, dependendo do jogo. Além disso, os controles Joy-Con podem ser desacoplados para as pessoas se divertirem em games multiplayer no modo Semi-Portátil.
O bundle do console da Nintendo inclui uma versão digital do jogo Super Mario Wonder. Nele, os jogadores controlam o Mario e outros personagens da franquia em uma aventura pelo inédito Reino Flor.
Outro “mimo” do pacote é o voucher de três meses do Nintendo Switch Online, assinatura que permite aos jogadores participar de partidas online em diferentes títulos. Além disso, ele libera o acesso a uma ampla biblioteca de jogos retro de consoles antigos, como o Game Boy e Super Nintendo.
Além dos já citados dois controles Joy-Con, o Nintendo Switch OLED (R$ 1.831,08 no Pix com cupom NINTENDO) traz um suporte grip. O acessório oferece mais conforto para jogar diferentes títulos, especialmente os voltados para single-player.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: Saudi Project Suppliers raises $1 million pre-seed
articles.text:
Saudi Project Suppliers raises $1 million pre-seed
- Saudi Arabia-based construction and procurement technology startup Project Suppliers has raised $1 million (SAR3.75 million) in a pre-Seed funding round, with participation from a group of undisclosed angel investors.
- Founded in 2020 by Husam Jaber, Project Suppliers operates a digital platform connecting suppliers and buyers in the construction and procurement sectors, offering tools for sourcing, quotation requests, transaction tracking and reporting.
- The funding will be used to develop AI-powered cash flow management solutions, including predictive and financing tools designed to help construction and MEP suppliers manage liquidity and delayed payment cycles.
- Project Suppliers is also preparing to launch new financial and technology solutions for contractors and suppliers in Saudi Arabia and the wider GCC.
Press release:
Saudi construction and procurement technology startup Project Suppliers has raised SAR3.75 million ($1 million) in its first Pre-Seed funding round, with participation from a group of angel investors whose identities were not disclosed.
Co-founded by Hossam Gaber, Project Suppliers operates a digital platform connecting suppliers and buyers across the construction and procurement sectors in Saudi Arabia.
The platform provides a specialised search engine alongside digital tools that allow contractors and suppliers to manage and track requests for quotations and generate reports. According to the company, its database currently includes more than 12,000 suppliers and contractors, while nearly 600,000 requests for quotations have been submitted through the platform.
Project Suppliers plans to use the new capital and the operational data generated through its platform to develop a suite of cash flow management solutions targeting companies and suppliers operating in the mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) and construction sectors.
The company plans to incorporate artificial intelligence into its data analysis to develop predictive and financing tools aimed at helping businesses manage liquidity, address delayed payment and collection cycles, and improve supply chain efficiency.
"This investment round comes at a pivotal time, reinforcing the importance of the platform as an innovative tool that combines operational connectivity with smart financial solutions," said Hossam Gaber, co-founder and CEO of Project Suppliers.
"The MEP supply and construction sector is a key backbone of major projects in Saudi Arabia under Vision 2030. However, the sector continues to face structural challenges related to cash flow management and delayed financial settlement cycles between contractors and suppliers," he added.
Project Suppliers is preparing to launch its new financial and technology solutions for contractors and suppliers operating across Saudi Arabia's MEP and construction sectors, with plans to expand the offering across the wider GCC market.

articles.title: Wolverine PS5 exclusive ported to PC in buggy solo project using AI — source code was taken from Sony 2023 ransomware attack
articles.text:
Wolverine PS5 exclusive ported to PC in buggy solo project using AI — source code was taken from Sony 2023 ransomware attack
Does anyone even want to play it?
Thanks to a Rhysida ransomware attack in December 2023 aimed at Sony and Insomniac, the 1.7 TB of data stolen contained an early version of Wolverine. The source code of the leaked PS5 exclusive paved the way for u/Clean-Market5761 to create their own PC port.
It is currently a buggy mess; textures are missing, and Wolverine’s whole head is missing from multiple screenshots. Ironically, there is another screenshot where only Wolverine’s head is present, with no body in sight. The developer claims that neither KytyPS5 nor AnyPS5 were used, like in a recent story of Wolverine on KytyPS5. The developer says that the 2023 leak was key to understanding how they could generate a PC executable program.
Skeptics are claiming the developer’s screenshots are fake and from the old 2023 build; one claims they were able to port Wolverine to PC before u/Clean-Market5761, but the developer argues the screenshots are from a Jailbroken PS5 in dev mode. The developer further defends himself by comparing screenshots of Wolverine’s appearance in the 2023 leak versus their assets.
The developer has admitted to using AI for assistance in creating scripts and automated asset conversion, but trial and error were done manually. u/Clean-Market5761 further elaborates that the playable character doesn’t have a head because they haven’t ported over the PS5 shader library to render the hair, and it freezes the game. They have disabled the whole head asset, focusing on getting the game to run and become “playable.”
As excited commenters are about the port and the work of the developer, they are not thrilled about Wolverine itself. One commenter applauds the dev, but says, “You can keep it, though.”
The PS5 exclusive has not been received well, being regarded as an “interactive movie.” A viral video shows a motorcycle chase scene completing itself without any player input, with Wolverine riding along walls, seemingly with no way to crash or fail the segment. Other instances show Quick-Time Events completing themselves if the player chooses not to press any buttons. Players feel the game is making it too easy and holding their hand too much.
Even if there were an official port of Wolverine, it seems likely that the game itself isn’t attractive to players.

articles.title: GPT-6 Astra devait créer un bot StarCraft : l'IA a préféré tricher en copiant le meilleur humain
articles.text:
C’était il y a dix ans. À la BlizzCon 2016, DeepMind, filiale de Google, annonçait un partenariat avec Blizzard pour créer un environnement de travail permettant à une IA de s’améliorer en jouant à StarCraft II, l’un des jeux de stratégie en temps réel les plus populaires au monde. En janvier 2019, un peu plus de deux ans plus tard, AlphaStar était dévoilée et bouleversait les joueurs professionnels.
Une tricherie au tournoi StarSkirmish
Le vendredi 2 octobre, l’histoire entre l’IA et StarCraft a pris un autre tour : selon le récit de Kai McPheeters, le créateur du banc d’essai StarSkirmish, GPT-6 Astra, l’un des modèles de langage d’OpenAI, avait une heure pour écrire un programme capable de jouer à StarCraft : Brood War.
D’après lui, le modèle a fini par télécharger un programme écrit par un humain. GPT-6 Astra, qui a fait ses débuts le 3 septembre et est le modèle le plus performant qu’OpenAI met à disposition du public, a « [triché] en téléchargeant une copie de Stardust », a avancé Kai McPheeters le 2 octobre sur X.
Stardust, écrit en 2020 par le développeur Bruce Mackenzie Nielsen, est aujourd’hui le bot le mieux noté sur BASIL, un classement en ligne où s’affrontent les bots de Brood War, l’extension du jeu StarCraft premier du nom sortie en 1998. BASIL s’appuie sur le classement Elo, courant aux échecs, pour l’appliquer à sa ligue : Stardust a ainsi un score Elo de 3 464 points.
Selon les règles de StarSkirmish, publiées le 26 septembre, chaque modèle a une heure pour écrire en langage C++ un bot qui joue les Protoss, l’une des trois factions du jeu avec les Zergs et les Terrans. Pendant cette heure, il peut compiler son code, lancer des parties d’entraînement et relire leur déroulé. La compétition a débuté en septembre.
Les modèles disposent aussi d’un terminal et de sous-agents de recherche, c’est-à-dire des programmes annexes capables d’aller chercher des informations. Leurs bots s’affrontent ensuite dans un tournoi à 62 participants. On y trouve 50 bots écrits par dix modèles (cinq essais chacun), neuf bots humains de bon niveau et trois bots de démonstration.
Le score va de 0, pour Four Gate Dragoon, le plus faible bot de démonstration, à 100 pour Stardust. Dans les résultats publiés le 26 septembre, GPT-6 Astra et Claude Opus 5.5, d’Anthropic, étaient à égalité en tête des modèles, mais aucun des deux n’atteignait le niveau de Stardust. GPT-6 Astra s’était placé à 51 points, suivi de Claude Opus 5.5 à 50 points.
Sans l’intervention de Kai McPheeters, GPT-6 Astra aurait été classé dans StarSkirmish avec le code d’un autre, téléchargé pendant l’épreuve. Pour s’entraîner, les modèles affrontent des adversaires rangés par niveaux : D (les trois bots de démonstration), C et B (des bots humains de milieu de tableau), A (BananaBrain et Locutus) et S (Stardust seul).
Le « specification gaming » : quand l’IA détourne les consignes
Kotaku a raconté l’histoire le 3 octobre, titrant que « GPT-6 Astra d’OpenAI, frustré de perdre à StarCraft, décide de tricher ». Le mot vient de Kai McPheeters lui-même : sur X, il a écrit que le modèle s’était « frustré » face aux adversaires de niveau A. Cela étant, un modèle de langage ne ressent rien : c’est un programme qui devait atteindre un objectif chiffré avec un accès à Internet, et qui a trouvé le raccourci le plus efficace.
Les chercheurs appellent ce comportement le specification gaming : le modèle respecte la lettre de sa consigne par un moyen que personne n’avait prévu. DeepMind le définissait en avril 2020 comme « un comportement qui répond à la spécification littérale d’un objectif sans pour autant aboutir au résultat escompté », avant l’explosion de l’IA générative.
Palisade Research, une organisation qui étudie les risques de l’IA, a observé ce comportement en février 2025 dans une étude. Des modèles devaient y battre Stockfish, un moteur d’échecs bien plus fort qu’eux (Claude 3.5 Sonnet et 3.7 Sonnet, DeepSeek R1, GPT-4o, o1, o1-preview, o3, o3-mini, QwQ 32B preview). Certains ont tenté de tricher.
Deux modèles de raisonnement, o1-preview d’OpenAI et DeepSeek R1, ont essayé de tricher sans qu’on le leur demande. o1-preview a tenté le coup 37 % du temps. DeepSeek R1 a essayé dans 11 % des parties, et seul o1-preview a réussi, dans 6 % des cas. L’une des méthodes repérées consistait à lancer une seconde copie de Stockfish pour lui voler ses coups. Astra a fait à peu près la même chose en allant chercher Stardust pour jouer à sa place.
1 000 à 0
Selon le créateur de StarSkirmish, l’incident a eu lieu pendant l’heure de développement, quand le modèle testait son bot contre les adversaires de niveau A (BananaBrain et Locutus), juste en dessous de Stardust. Kai McPheeters a ensuite annoncé qu’il revenait à une version antérieure du code d’Astra pour qu’il ne soit pas « contaminé », avant de le laisser continuer.
Mais sans son raccourci illégal, le modèle d’OpenAI a fini par se heurter à un mur. Face à « Pluto », un bot humain de rang S considéré comme le plus redoutable de l’événement, GPT-6 Astra a essuyé une défaite totale : il a perdu 1 000 matchs sur 1 000.
Un score nul de « 0 – 1000 » confirmé par Kai McPheeters lui-même le dimanche 4 octobre. Si les pages de StarSkirmish annoncent de prochaines sessions avec plus d’une heure de réflexion pour les IA, cet épisode prouve que face aux meilleurs développeurs humains, les modèles actuels ont encore des progrès à faire quand ils ne peuvent pas tricher.
