articles.title: Akka Tests Spec-Driven AI Delivery Across 65 Open Source Projects
articles.text:
Akka used 65 open source projects to test a spec driven workflow for AI assisted software porting, measuring specification structure, context, model and effort selection, automated validation, token consumption, and runtime performance. The initial tranche took 99.3 hours and consumed 9.41 billion tokens, with Akka reporting a lines of code or performance improvement in 57 of the 65 ports.
The experiment used two tranches. Akka analyzed all 65 projects, generating specifications and implementing up to 10% of each project's surface area, then selected 10 for complete implementation based on system characteristics and measurable results. The delivery harness cycled through discovery, specification, porting, benchmarking, and improvement. Discovery analyzed code, models, schemas, and runtime behavior, while Claude with Akka Specify handled implementation, testing, and review. A common benchmark runner compared tests, code size, and latency.
Akka delivery harness workflow(Source: Akka Blog Post)
Akka found that structured specifications with claims, evidence, and typed behavior improved first-pass implementations, while gaps in context files remained around cross-component decisions. Follow-up areas include interface enumeration, test ingestion, provenance tracking, differential testing, and adversarial testing.GitHub Spec Kit similarly structures coding agent workflows around specification, planning, tasks, implementation, and convergence. In Akka's experiment, Sonnet averaged 61 minutes per port versus 120 minutes for Opus, while Opus used about 40% fewer tokens. Higher effort settings increased consumption without consistently improving efficiency.
The finding prompted discussion among engineers following the research. Aaditya, commenting on Tyler Jewell's CEO of Akka LinkedIn post, wrote
Smaller model's behavior matched modernization work he had observed, where the small model follows the spec while a larger model may improvise.
Aaditya also questioned
Whether reductions in lines of code resulted primarily from dead code removal or from differences in the target language.
Rick Bryce, Head of Marketing at Avahi, raised a related point in the same discussion and suggested that constraints could influence the result. The comments add questions around whether model capability, specification constraints, or both account for differences in porting efficiency.
Cheaper model giving the tighter port is the finding worth chasing
Akka model and effort efficiency chart (Source: Akka Blog Post)
Validation used the original unit and integration tests alongside auditors checking serialization, security, error handling, PII, idempotency, and architectural boundaries. Akka added guardrails as failures exposed new issues, while reporting that additional exit conditions increased porting costs. Performance varied by project: applications, frameworks, and libraries generally improved, while infrastructure and tooling showed median degradation. Akka reported a 143,333 times improvement for Dify, but noted that the compared workloads differed, while Netflix Metaflow was approximately 100 times slower.

articles.title: RTX 5090 modder claims to have solved melting power connectors with auxiliary 8-pin board
articles.text:
Something to look forward to: A hardware modder has shared a promising fix for Nvidia's RTX 5090, a GPU with a documented history of power-related issues. Best yet, the workaround is said to be "relatively affordable" and would even come with a warranty.
Over on Reddit, user DallasGrave outlined the approach taken when developing the mod. In short, the fix utilizes a pickup PCB soldered to the contacts of the original 12VHPWR header that feeds an auxiliary dual eight-pin board. This effectively spreads the load across three sets of cables, which significantly reduces power draw and temperature.
According to the user, the modded card was tested at full load for 48 hours (at 550W), and cable temps never climbed above 40 degrees Celsius. Even the joints stayed nice and cool, we're told.
Tom's Hardware notes that the user, DallasGrave, appears to be affiliated with Grave PC, a company that specializes in CPU / GPU cooling and compact system design. In the Reddit thread, DallasGrave said they are working on a "relatively affordable" service to convert existing cards – complete with warranty. In another reply, the user says they are a PNY partner and that eventually, customers will be able to buy a PNY card with a similar mod directly from them – again, with a full warranty.
Asked about specifics of the mod, DallasGrave said they could have replaced the header with a higher current model but that does not fix the cable. "12VHPWR is simply rated too high," he said, adding that it never should have been approved beyond 350-ish watts.
This is not the first attempt we've seen to address the issue of melting connectors, but it does appear to be one of the cleanest solutions yet. Over the summer, YouTube channel TecLab shared a fix that involved connecting power wires directly to the GPU's PCB. It seemed to work, but it wasn't all that aesthetically pleasing. DallasGrave said their solution would be more of a universal option that could work across multiple GPU brands.

articles.title: Java News Roundup: JobRunr 9, OpenXava 8, Quarkus, LangChain4j, JNoSQL, Introducing Lathe
articles.text:
This week's Java roundup for September 28th, 2026, features news highlighting: the GA releases of JobRunr 9.0 and OpenXava 8.0; point releases for Quarkus, Micronaut, LangChain4j, Eclipse JNoSQL; ADK for Java and ADK for Kotlin; and introducing Lathe, a new Java language server.
OpenJDK
JEP 544, Ahead-of-Time Code Compilation, has been elevated from Proposed to Target to Targeted for JDK 28. This JEP proposes to improve application startup and warmup time such that it is instantly available with optimized native code when the HotSpot JVM starts. This enables applications to achieve peak performance more quickly and to sustain peak performance.
JDK 28
Build 18 of the JDK 28 early-access builds was made available this past week featuring updates from Build 17 that include fixes for various issues. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
For JDK 28, developers are encouraged to report bugs via the Java Bug Database.
Jakarta EE
In his weekly Hashtag Jakarta EE blog, Ivar Grimstad, Jakarta EE Developer Advocate at the Eclipse Foundation, provided an update on Jakarta EE 12, writing:
For Jakarta EE 12, the vote for including Jakarta Authorization in Jakarta EE Web Profile is ongoing. It makes perfect sense to group it together with the other security specifications there. On request from the steering committee, the timeline for Jakarta EE 12 was discussed and firmed up in the platform call this week. The timeline for Jakarta EE 12 will look like this:
- December 1 - Jakarta EE 12 Core Profile
- March 31 - Jakarta EE 12 Web Profile
- May 15 - Jakarta EE 12 Platform
One specification I, personally, really want to see included in Jakarta EE 12 Web Profile is Jakarta NoSQL. Simplifying and standardizing access to NoSQL datastores is a great feature when integrating artificial intelligence in enterprise applications. Particularly, support for vector databases for RAG is something that will be very useful. If you agree with me, or have an opinion about including Jakarta NoSQL in Jakarta EE 12, please do let us know on the mailing list or in the platform calls. The voice of the community matters!
Eclipse JNoSQL, the compatible implementation of Jakarta NoSQL was recently elevated from an incubating project to an Eclipse Enterprise for Java (EE4J) project. It has been an Eclipse project since 2017 and has been included in Eclipse GlassFish since Jakarta EE 11 as part of support for Jakarta Data.
JobRunr
The release of JobRunr 9.0.0 delivers notable changes such as: a new Chart tab in the History section of the dashboard that shows the life of a job, in Gantt chart format, with a row per state and a row per durable step; support for Micronaut 5 and Quarkus 3.40; and the addition of a warning when a serialized job is too large that will trigger an unwrap of the StepExecutionException. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes and this version 9 launch webinar. InfoQ will follow up with a more detailed news story.
OpenXava
The release of OpenXava 8.0.0 ships with bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: OpenXava built on Spring Boot; support for some Jakarta EE 11 specifications; and a more modern look-and-feel. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Quarkus
The release of Quarkus 3.34.0 provides bug fixes and notable changes such as: improvements to the AeshLauncher interface that hardens the signal protocol and timeout diagnostics; and an elimination of an unnecessary warning from the ResteasyReactiveJacksonProcessor class when an endpoint returns void. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes for version 3.40.1 and version 3.40.0.
Micronaut
The Micronaut Foundation has released versions 5.2.1 and 5.2.0 of the Micronaut Framework (announced here and here, respectively) based on Micronaut Core 5.2.11 and 5.2.8. Along with bug fixes and updates to many of the Micronaut ecosystem modules, new features include: experimental support for Micronaut for Python, for processing of Python source code at compile time; and a new Micronaut Jakarta EL module that serves as an implementation of the Jakarta Expression Language specification. More details on these releases may be found in the release notes for version 5.2.1 and version 5.2.0.
LangChain4j
The formal release (along with the thirty-first beta release) of LangChain4j 1.21.0 delivers bug fixes, dependency upgrades and introduces new, experimental decision models. This includes a new API consisting of the DecisionModel interface, and DecisionServices, RoutingChatModel and DecisionRouterPlanner classes. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes and tutorials for Decision Models and Decision Services.
Eclipse JNoSQL
The release of Eclipse JNoSQL 1.19.0 ships with new features such as: support for ScyllaDB; database drivers updated for Neo4J 6.3.0, InfluxDB 1.11.1, DynamoDB 2.55.7, and MongoDB 5.13.0; and improved lifecycle logging that include the Oracle NoSQL and Jakarta Persistence extensions. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Google Agent Development Kit
The release of ADK for Java 1.11.0 provides bug fixes, documentation improvements and new features such as: a new rewindBeforeInvocationId() method, added to the EventActions class, for rewind compatibility with ADK for Kotlin; and new thread-safe methods, immutableEvents(), addEvent(), and addEvents(), added to the Session class, to replace the now deprecated events() method. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Similarly, the release of ADK for Kotlin 1.3.0 delivers bug fixes and new features such as: a new @ExperimentalLiveApi annotation that marks a live bidirectional streaming API; and a change from null to an empty string in the initialization of the author attribute in the Event class. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Lathe
Alexey Gavrilov, Senior Software Engineer at Telenor Linx, has introduced a new Java language server, Lathe, an implementation of the Language Server Protocol (LSP). Lathe eliminates the difficulties with traditional project import and classpath or module-path configuration. It works in any editor compatible with LSP and its model comes from a Maven build such that everything remains synchronized. Lathe ships with a Neovim client and an MCP server for AI coding agents. The latest release, available this past week, is version 0.1.14.

articles.title: Connecting AI agents to enterprise knowledge
articles.text:
Sponsored
Connecting AI agents to enterprise knowledge
A strong structural foundation that links data and agents is key for context-rich agentic AI that scales.
In partnership withNeo4j
For all the data that AI systems continually amass and analyze, enterprise AI agents often suffer from a curious shortcoming: a lack of knowledge. More than data, knowledge is the understanding of what the data means in the context of individual organizations. AI agents need this understanding to reason about situations, make decisions, and ultimately take actions. Without sufficient knowledge, agents are prone to making flawed and unreliable decisions.
A lack of knowledge, our research finds, is a major reason agentic AI use cases never make it to production. Competitive pressure is making it urgent to address this. Organizations need to deploy and scale more of their agentic projects to capture the efficiency gains AI promises. Falling short risks wasting the investment already sunk into these projects, and it cedes ground to rivals already putting their agents to work more effectively.
The purpose of this report, which is based on a survey of 300 data, AI, and other technology executives, is threefold. First, it seeks to gauge organizations’ agentic knowledge capabilities (i.e., their ability to give AI agents a full contextual understanding of the data they ingest) across semantic knowledge, episodic memory, and procedural knowledge.
Second, the report probes the challenges organizations face in improving access to knowledge and ultimately to getting more agent use cases into production. Third, it explores the measures organizations are taking to overcome these challenges.
The key findings include the following:
Data and knowledge weaknesses consistently stall AI agent progress. On average, only around a third (34%) of organizations’ agentic AI projects make it into production. Even high-tech firms struggle with this. Legacy data systems, security and privacy concerns, and a lack of knowledge and context are the key points of failure.
Strong knowledge capabilities correlate with agent success. A small group of production leaders (organizations where on average 61% of agentic projects advance beyond pilot) have stronger knowledge capabilities than the rest, especially when it comes to semantics. This advantage tracks closely with their higher production rate.
Fragmented data hugely complicates knowledge access. Data fragmentation (the inadequate sharing of data across systems) was most commonly cited as a top challenge to expanding agents’ access to knowledge (cited by 55%). Production leaders, by contrast, are more likely to see security and privacy concerns as a major concern (cited by 72% of this group).
Most firms aim to strengthen the link between data and agents. Among steps that can yield higher quality agent decisions, executives expect the biggest impact to come from strengthening the structural foundation between the organization’s data and its AI agents. The experts we interviewed see a knowledge layer as a prime way to achieve this.
Investment priorities to boost knowledge range from pipelines to knowledge graphs. To expand agent access to knowledge, organizations will prioritize investments in retrieval technologies, like ingestion pipelines, AI-ready APIs, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG); in AI evaluation agents; and in knowledge graphs.
This content was produced by Insights, MIT Technology Review’s custom content arm, not its editorial staff. It was researched and written by humans, with any AI tools that may have been used limited to production processes under human oversight.

articles.title: Gemini vai ficar mais limitado para usuários de contas gratuitas • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Gemini vai ficar mais limitado para usuários de contas gratuitas
Gemini gratuito deixará de oferecer os modelos Flash e Pro, ficando limitado ao Flash Lite. Também haverá mudanças no Google AI Plus.
Se você usa o Gemini por meio de uma conta gratuita, atente-se para uma mudança nos recursos oferecidos: a partir da próxima sexta-feira (09/10), usuários não pagantes deixarão de ter acesso aos modelos de IA Flash e Pro, restando apenas o Flash Lite.
A mudança também afeta usuários que assinam o Google AI Plus, que custa R$ 24,99 por mês no Brasil. Esses usuários deixarão de ter acesso ao modelo Pro, mas poderão continuar usando as opções Flash e Flash Lite.
Com isso, somente usuários que assinarem o Google AI Pro ou o Google AI Ultra terão acesso a todos os principais modelos de inteligência artificial do Gemini. Como “bônus” para quem aderir ao primeiro, o Google oferecerá acesso ao Deep Think, modo de raciocínio avançado até então disponível somente no Google AI Ultra.
As mudanças nos recursos do Gemini serão aplicadas em escala global. De acordo com esta página de ajuda do Google, os usuários do Google AI Plus serão avisados das alterações em seu plano por e-mail, com elas podendo ser aplicadas de modo progressivo (e não necessariamente no dia 09, portanto).
Apesar de a mesma página destacar que as mudanças envolvem os aplicativos para Android e iOS do Gemini, elas também afetarão a versão web do serviço.
Em resumo, ficará assim:
| Plano | Flash Lite | Flash | Pro | Preço mensal | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gemini gratuito | Sim | Não | Não | – | 
| Google AI Plus | Sim | Sim | Não | R$ 24,99 | 
| Google AI Pro | Sim | Sim | Sim | R$ 96,99 | 
| Google AI Ultra | Sim | Sim | Sim | R$ 779,90 (inicial) | 
A companhia destaca ainda que todos os modelos passam a permitir que os usuários configurem níveis de esforço (baixo, médio ou alto), ou seja, definam o grau de aprofundamento e raciocínio de cada modelo na execução de tarefas.
Recentemente, o Google anunciou o Gemini 4 Argon para tarefas complexas e de segurança. Contudo, o acesso a esse modelo está limitado a “testadores confiáveis” neste momento.

articles.title: Qualcomm Licenses Huawei's LogicFolding, 5G, and Other Technologies
articles.text:
Monday, October 5th 2026
Qualcomm Licenses Huawei's LogicFolding, 5G, and Other Technologies
Qualcomm announced today that it is officially licensing technology from Chinese technology giant Huawei. In a deal estimated to be worth $6.9 billion upon completion, Qualcomm will license various technologies from Huawei to integrate across its product portfolio. According to official releases, these technologies include computing, AI, networking, and more. Bloomberg reports that the deal also covers Huawei's latest LogicFolding silicon design. This is a significant win for Huawei, whose R&D teams have spent years designing a way to bypass sanctions and overcome manufacturing technology limits. By stacking silicon vertically across two sheets, LogicFolding dramatically reduces the distance between compute elements, increases efficiency, and significantly improves transistor density. The result is a 55% increase in transistor density and a 41% boost in power efficiency.
Since Huawei lacks access to manufacturing its silicon using EUV lithography, it uses DUV machines with LogicFolding to work around this limitation. Even so, the company claims that LogicFolding on its domestic node production will achieve a transistor density equivalent to a 1.4 nm node by 2031. For Qualcomm, whose access to advanced lithography is unrestricted, this means the company can potentially surpass Moore's Law by stacking multiple sheets of cutting-edge silicon, achieving massive boosts in transistor density and power efficiency.This agreement will be completed after regulatory approvals are secured. Huawei sees it as a way to collaborate with the industry and share its technology under fair, reasonable, and non-discriminatory (FRAND) principles. For other technologies, Huawei's development and contributions to 4G and 5G standards are so advanced that they lead in some areas, such as near-physical-limit signal transmission technology using polar codes. Qualcomm will utilize these technologies in building its own modems and designs, selecting only what best suits its use cases.

articles.title: 'KB5124010 was a disaster on one of my Windows 11 PCs': latest update has a bug that breaks games, or worse still, the entire system going by some reports
articles.text:
Windows 11's latest update has a game-breaking bug — and there's no fix yet
New glitch is making the lives of gamers a misery
- Microsoft has admitted there's a bug in the latest Windows 11 update
- The September preview update causes some games and apps to crash
- According to some reports, this patch is also leading to sluggish performance, or even boot failures, so tread very carefully
Windows 11's latest update has a bug that's causing havoc with some PC games and apps, or worse still, according to reports that have found the upgrade breaking their entire system.
Windows Latest highlighted a post on the Windows health dashboard where Microsoft admits there's a problem with September's optional update, which was released almost two weeks ago now.
Bear in mind that this patch (KB5124010) is a preview update, then, but there certainly seem to be quite a few issues for gamers here based on some of the feedback on social media. These problems affect Windows 11 26H2 and 25H2 users, as well as those still on 24H2.
Microsoft tells us that: "Some applications which require the decoding of AC-3 (Dolby Digital) audio might close unexpectedly."
The company adds: "Affected applications may vary and can include games, media players, and certain productivity applications."
The bug may cause the game or app to completely fail to launch, or it might crash, and in some circumstances things could be fine until certain features are used, notably playing music.
At least Microsoft assures us that "many modern applications do not use Windows for this type of encoding and therefore will not encounter this issue," but clearly there are problems here.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
There are reports on Reddit from gamers expressing their displeasure at witnessing crashing with, for example, Fallout: New Vegas, Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion and Wardogs. In all cases, players found that the problems started after installing the September preview patch, and ceased when the update was removed.
What's more worrying is that some of the affected gamers are reporting more serious issues that include the system ending up broken with boot failures, or very slow performance for booting or shutting down the PC. Other complaints include general sluggishness on the desktop.
As one Redditor observes: "KB5124010 was a disaster on one of my Win11 25H2 PCs. It caused boot issues, very slow shutdown/search, and after uninstalling it the machine got stuck at the Asus logo and stopped booting. Clean reinstall in the end."
Another agrees: "I thought I was going insane with slow boot up. File Explorer issues. Just big grey boxes taking forever."
Analysis: this needs a quick fix
Microsoft says: "We are working on releasing a resolution for this issue in a future Windows update. We will provide an update when more information is available."
Well, this is a nasty one by all accounts, so Microsoft better muster all its bug squashing powers pretty swiftly. After all, while this is a preview update now, it becomes the full October update for Windows 11 a week tomorrow – so that's not far away at all.
Also, there are some folks who may have wanted to grab this optional update straight away because it packs a fix for a previous bug in the September (non-preview) update which broke a backup feature in Windows 11. So, they could have downloaded KB5124010 and been happy to receive this particular fix, only to find that their games or apps are suddenly in hot water (or worse). Sadly this kind of situation is all too common with Windows 11 these days.
Furthermore, this is a warning to be careful around preview updates, because seemingly the only cure for the bugs here is to uninstall the patch – there's no workaround. Also be aware that if you have selected the option to 'Get the latest updates as soon as they're available' in Windows 11 then you will get all these preview updates automatically, and possibly be hit by bugs like these.
That's why I'd be cautious about exercising this right, even if you are very keen to receive new Windows 11 features as soon as possible.

articles.title: AI glasses face their first major government crackdown
articles.text:
Norway has become the first major country to propose a temporary ban on the use of AI glasses in selected public places amid growing privacy concerns over wearable technology.
The rich Scandinavian country’s center-left government said on Monday that it would introduce a law to parliament soon on a temporary ban for places such as parks, beaches, schools, and kindergartens. It will also set up an expert group to propose permanent national rules.
“I am concerned about the introduction of powerful new technology where people risk being photographed, filmed, or recorded without their knowledge,” said Torgeir Micaelsen, Norway’s digitalization minister. A temporary ban “will give us time to conduct a thorough assessment and hold an informed debate that can lay the foundation for permanent regulation,” he said.
Governments around the world are grappling with how to regulate AI glasses—including those from Facebook owner Meta and cheaper copycat devices—amid worries that they are being used to film people without their consent, including children and women in settings such as changing rooms.
Parts of Norwegian society have already reacted with their own bans, including schools in the capital Oslo and the country’s biggest company, oil and gas major Equinor, which has banned them from its offices and offshore facilities.

articles.title: Es begann mit der Alge: Wie drei Forscher die Optogenetik begründeten
articles.text:
Nobelpreis für Medizin: Pioniere der Optogenetik ausgezeichnet
Der diesjährige Nobelpreis für Medizin und Physiologie geht an drei Forscher: Karl Deisseroth vom Howard Hughes Medical Institute und der Stanford University, Peter Hegemann von der Humboldt-Universität Berlin und Georg Nagel von der Universität Würzburg. Die Auszeichnung ehrt ihre Entdeckungen, die den Zweig der Optogenetik überhaupt erst möglich gemacht haben. Das Verfahren kommt in heutigen Laboren weltweit zum Einsatz und bringt wortwörtlich Licht in die Vorgänge in unserem Gehirn. Dies lieferte einen wesentlichen Fortschritt in der Neurowissenschaft.
Ein neuer Weg für die Neurowissenschaft durch die Optogenetik
Optogenetik ist ein Kunstwort und eigentlich kein besonders gutes. Zwar braucht man Genetik, um das eigentliche Ziel zu erreichen: Zellen einen Schalter zu verpassen, den sie von Natur aus nicht haben. Aber es geht nicht um Vererbung, sondern darum, Zellen, stimuliert durch Licht, an- und auszuknipsen und zu schauen, was passiert.
Hegemann als Biophysiker und Nagel als Biologe entdeckten dazu in der Alge Chlamydomonas reinhardtii das Protein namens Kanalrhodopsin. Der Einzeller ist nur wenige Mikrometer groß, zählt zu den Grünalgen und sieht putzig aus, wie eine Erbse mit zwei Fühlern. Aber es sind Geißeln, mit denen die Alge schwimmt. Im Verhältnis zu ihrer Größe ist sie zwölfmal schneller als der US-Schwimmer und 18-malige Olympiasieger Michael Phelps.
Wie die Alge das Licht „sieht“
Wie alle Pflanzen macht auch sie Photosynthese. Das geht nur mit Licht, deswegen schwimmt sie immer dorthin, wo es hell ist. Mehr als 15 Jahre lang hatte Hegemann Chlamydomonas erforscht, weil er wissen wollte, wie die Alge das Licht sieht. 2002 endlich entdeckte er den Mechanismus. Zusammen mit seinem Kollegen Nagel fand er ein spezielles Protein in ihrem Augenfleck. Es ist dem menschlichen Sehfarbstoff Rhodopsin erstaunlich nah verwandt. Die beiden tauften es Kanalrhodopsin.
Das Molekül funktioniert wie eine Schleuse: Fällt Licht darauf, klappt ein molekularer Schalter um und öffnet einen zum Molekül gehörigen Kanal in der Zellhülle. Geladene Teilchen strömen ein und geben so das Lichtsignal ans Innere der Zelle weiter. Die beiden Forscher ahnten sofort: „Kanalrhodopsin könnte ein mächtiges Werkzeug sein.“ So schrieben sie es 2002 in der Veröffentlichung. Dafür müsste man nur das Kanalrhodopsin-Gen in das Erbgut von Nervenzellen einschleusen.
Wie der optogenetische Schalter eingesetzt wird
Die Arbeit von Karl Deisseroth knüpft an diese Erkenntnisse an und verwandelte das Protein in einen lichtgesteuerten Schalter für Nervenzellen. Zunächst gelang ihm das bei Ratten, deren Nervenzellen auf blaues Licht reagierten und das er in einer Arbeit 2005 beschrieb. 2007 konnte er den lichtgesteuerten Schalter bei Nervenzellen im Gehirn von lebenden Mäusen demonstrieren.
Die Methode der Steuerung per Licht überholte bisherige mühselige und eher grobe Verfahren, wenn Forscher:innen Zellen im Gehirn stimulieren wollten. Neurowissenschaftler:innen piksten zum Beispiel Elektroden ins Gehirn, jagten Strom hinein und schauten, was das für Folgen hat. Oder sie beeinflussen Nervenzellen chemisch, mit Psychopharmaka beispielsweise. Aber: Chemische Stoffe wirken nur langsam und auf große Bereiche. Und auch Strom trifft immer mehrere Zellen auf einmal.
Optogenetik löst andere Verfahren ab
Durch Licht stimulierte Nervenzellen boten einen präziseren Weg. Auf diese Weise lassen sich die neuronalen Schaltkreise aufdecken, die bestimmte Erinnerungen, Gefühle oder Verhaltensweisen bei uns auslösen. Zudem hilft diese Technik auch, neuronale Erkrankungen wie Parkinson und Epilepsie besser zu verstehen und vielleicht eines Tages Patient:innen mit Licht behandeln zu können.
Der Medizin-Nobelpreis geht nun zu gleichen Teilen an die Forscher. Er ist dotiert mit zwölf Millionen schwedischen Kronen, das entspricht etwa einer Million Euro. Am 6. Oktober folgt die Vergabe des Nobelpreises für Physik, am 7. Oktober folgt der Nobelpreis für Chemie. Im vergangenen Jahr erhielten drei Immunforscher:innen den Medizin-Nobelpreis.

articles.title: China stockpiled 343 immersion DUV tools for advanced chipmaking — report claims 270 ASML scanners can produce 7nm processors without sanctioned EUV tools
articles.text:
China stockpiled 343 immersion DUV tools for advanced chipmaking — report claims 270 ASML scanners can produce 7nm processors without sanctioned EUV tools
China, apparently, has significant immersion DUV capability.
Chinese chipmakers have accumulated an estimated 343 immersion DUV lithography chipmaking tools from 2012 to early 2026, many of which can be used to make chips using 7nm-class process technologies, according to a report from the Centre for Technology & Statecraft (CTS). The Washington-based group asserts that this equipment gives Chinese fabs considerable potential to produce sophisticated processors despite their inability to procure ASML's more advanced EUV systems. While the total number of ArFi tools owned by Chinese chipmakers seems plausible, some other estimates look questionable.
China has been particularly aggressive in procuring wafer fabrication equipment in recent years as the U.S. government has been busy imposing various curbs on its semiconductor industry. Since 2012, Chinese chipmakers, including logic and memory makers, have imported 343 immersion DUV lithography scanners from ASML, excluding imports to multinational fabs located within China.
The authors of the report claim that the existing export controls leave an important gap because lithography equipment originally acquired for less advanced process technologies can potentially be reassigned for more sophisticated process technologies, such as 7nm-class nodes (which the industry adopted in 2018 – 2019). This happens at a cost, but if no other options are available, Chinese chipmakers have no choice. They propose to prohibit exports of all immersion DUV systems to China and restrict replacement components and maintenance services for machines installed at advanced fabs, a proposal consistent with the bipartisan MATCH Act introduced in April.
CTS claims that 270 of these immersion DUV tools are ASML's Twinscan NXT:1980i scanners featuring a 38nm resolution and a 2.5nm matched-machine overlay capability crucial for multipatterning for 7nm-class nodes, which can be used to make chips using 7nm-class fabrication technologies. In addition, CTS claims that Chinese fabs own 22 NXT:2050i and six NXT:2000i systems. It is unclear how many of the 296 advanced immersion DUV scanners shipped to China are currently operational.
Dutch authorities introduced licensing requirements for exports of ASML's NXT:2000i and more capable immersion DUV scanners in September 2023, which effectively prevents their shipment to China. As a result, Chinese chipmakers had to opt for the least capable NXT:1980i. CTS now estimates that Chinese fabs purchased approximately 90 NXT:1980i scanners in 2024 and another 89 units in 2025, spending more than $13 billion during the two-year period. While the Netherlands expanded export controls to the NXT:1980i in September 2024, individual exports of this model can still receive approval. Furthermore, ASML can also potentially sell its NXT:1965Ci systems to clients in China, though we are not sure it has all the components needed for these outdated scanners.
ASML's own results reflect unusually high demand from China: the country represented 41% of its net system sales by shipment destination in 2024 and 33% in 2025. That share subsequently declined to 19% in Q1 2026 and 14% in Q2, which is something that ASML had warned about before.
One should keep in mind that the CTS numbers — ~90 NXT:1980i systems in 2024 and 89 in 2025 — cannot be independently reconstructed from ASML's published financial data. At most, ASML's disclosures provide a useful sanity check: China was indeed an exceptionally large destination during precisely those years, while ASML sold 129 and 131 ArFi systems globally in 2024 and 2025, respectively. If CTS' numbers are correct, then Chinese chipmakers bought the lion's share, 70% and 68%, of ASML's immersion DUV tools output in 2024 and 2025 despite export controls introduced in 2024. Meanwhile, the NXT:1980Di systems are readily available on the secondhand market.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
*The source mentions the NXT:1980i machines, which probably include the original 1980Di and newer 1980Fi featuring higher productivity. We will use the 'NXT:1980i' name in this story for consistency, even though ASML has never produced a scanner named NXT:1980i.

Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Gemini Call for Me might tell your mom you’re running late
articles.text:
Google may be expanding its “Call for Me” AI feature beyond business calls so you can use it to send messages to friends and family. Android Authority reports finding a “Gemini Calling” introductory screen in an APK teardown with examples that include “Call Mom and tell her I will be 15 minutes late” and “Call John and ask if he is coming for dinner.”
Gemini Call for Me might tell your mom you’re running late
A rumored Android update would automate personal phone calls with Gemini AI.
Based on those examples, even with this expansion, Gemini would likely be limited to basic, text message-like calls. While Google’s AI might not automate an entire catch-up phone call with your relatives, it could deliver quick messages to people who prefer a phone call, miss texts often, or even still have a landline phone.
Android Authority also says it found “granular permissions” for Gemini actions in individual apps, including what appear to be settings for phone call permissions. These settings would allow users to pick and choose which app capabilities they want to allow Gemini to access, potentially giving users an option to opt out of receiving incoming automated calls from Gemini. However, as Android Authority notes, it’s also possible Google might not publicly release this expansion or the granular Gemini app settings.

articles.title: Hot Girl Hotline is like 'Dear Abby' for the AI era | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Women throughout history have always sought out relationship advice, whether from newspaper columnists like “Dear Abby,” letters to Cosmo, or just chatting with girlfriends. In the social media era, you can instead post anonymously on Reddit relationship forums or look to social media creators who discuss the topic.
Now, two sisters are launching a startup for young women, Hot Girl Hotline, which focuses on bringing AI into these conversations.
I know what you may be thinking: With all the advances in AI technology, founders are building something for women to talk about their dating woes? Well … yes!
The reality is that people have already been turning to large language models (LLMs) via apps like ChatGPT for this type of advice, and the team believes this type of activity should be handled more carefully.
Unfortunately, as we’ve seen, chatting with a general-purpose chatbot about personal topics can sometimes lead to disastrous effects — especially for those who were already mentally fragile. ChatGPT, for example, has faced a wave of lawsuits over its alleged manipulative conversation tactics that plaintiffs say contributed to negative mental health effects, including, in some cases, suicide.
The idea behind Hot Girl Hotline is to reach young women who are looking to have these sorts of private conversations while navigating dating life and relationships, but in a safer way.
“We’re not trying to be an AI companion,” explained Baila Mudgil, formerly a social media consultant, who co-founded the startup with her sister Sumrin (“Sumi”), who studied computer science at Stanford. “A companion is really going after solving loneliness, escapism, boredom — and you can rely on a lot of emotional dependency from that AI companion.”
Baila says the startup’s approach is to focus on offering quality advice grounded in behavioral science, but in a way that makes it feel like you’re chatting with a trusted friend or big sister. The conversation is often Socratic, with the AI asking you questions to help you arrive at the answer yourself.
“This is not to replace speaking to a human. This is not clinical advice, and we have a lot of safeguards in place … we take safety really seriously,” Baila said. If conversations raise flags, for instance, the user is referred to resources such as the crisis hotline 988.
“We believe the key to quality advice is not just knowing what to do next; it’s understanding why you’re doing it. So that’s a big piece of it,” added Sumi.
Notably, the AI also knows when to end the conversation; it doesn’t keep asking follow-up questions to drag you further down a rabbit hole. Instead, it pushes users to go take action out in the real world rather than ruminate on the problem.
The sisters believe there’s room for an app like this because not everyone wants to post on the web for advice, and there are times when you don’t want to bring up a personal, dating, or relationship-focused issue with a friend.
Friends can bring their own biases into the conversation, or the user may not want to put their partner on blast for something they did before they determine whether they’re going to work through it or end the relationship.
“It doesn’t mean you’re replacing your friend — you’re just trying to get another perspective,” says Baila of the hotline.
The app also personalizes its advice for each user to reflect their values, goals, identity, and tastes.
Under the hood, the startup relies on a mix of AI models and encrypts users’ data in transit and at rest. It doesn’t sell or train on the data, either. When it uses a third-party AI model, it follows a zero-data-retention policy there as well.
Hot Girl Hotline plans to monetize through a $9.99 per month subscription, which hundreds of its most active users are already paying for. Later, it may incorporate ads, too.
Relationship advice is just the beginning of how the company wants to cater to young women. It also plans to expand into other areas, like beauty and lifestyle.
New York-based Hot Girl Hotline is currently bootstrapped and will be participating in the Startup Battlefield 200 at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, taking place October 13-15 in San Francisco. It’s available on iOS and the web.

articles.title: Kenyan court orders e-commerce company Copia into liquidation - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
A Kenyan High Court has ordered Copia Kenya, the e-commerce company that raised over US$120 million to serve consumers outside the country’s major cities, into liquidation after more than two years of administration failed to revive the business.
Launched in 2013, Copia combines technology and a network of local agents to offer a broad product offering and efficient, reliable delivery to “base of the pyramid” consumers. Its service enables rural households to access goods that would otherwise be difficult to obtain without travelling to a major city.
The company raised more than US$120 million in capital, with its most recent raise being a US$50 million Series C, and expanded into new markets, but in May 2024 entered administration after failing to secure the necessary capital to continue operations.
In a September 17 ruling, the Kenyan High Court found no realistic path for Copia to return to operating as a going concern, meaning extending the administration would only add delay and costs. Copia will now go into liquidation, with its remaining assets estimated at KES206.6 million (US$1.6 million) as of February.
“I am satisfied that the Joint Administrators have demonstrated, on a balance of probabilities, that the objectives of administration have been exhausted,” Justice Rhoda Rutto wrote in the ruling.
Copia’s existing administrators, Julius Mumo Ngonga and Anthony Makenzi Muthusi of KPMG, have been appointed as joint liquidators.

articles.title: Why finance teams need to think in systems
articles.text:
Why finance teams need to think in systems
As financial workflows become more connected, finance teams are taking a greater role in designing processes that reduce manual work, improve visibility, and scale with the business.
Finance has always had a role beyond recording transactions. It is involved in planning, controls, treasury, risk, and decision-making. What is changing is the extent to which finance teams are also involved in the systems through which financial activity takes place.
A customer's payment information can now move through a website or app, a payment system, an invoicing platform, a bank account, and an accounting system before it appears in a financial report. If those systems do not communicate, someone has to fill the gaps: checking transactions, moving data, downloading reports, and matching records manually.
As businesses grow, it becomes harder to manage.
Finance teams are becoming more involved in how these processes are designed. They are looking at where data comes from, where it needs to go, which steps can be automated, and how different systems should work together.
Finance remains responsible for financial control, visibility, and decision-making. But fulfilling that responsibility increasingly requires an understanding of the systems behind the numbers.
From recording transactions to designing workflows
Consider a typical payment. A customer pays an invoice online. The payment needs to be recorded, the invoice updated, the money sent to the right bank account, and the transaction eventually reconciled with the accounting records.
When each step sits in a different system, finance teams can end up doing much of this work manually.
The same applies as businesses add subscriptions, recurring payments, payment links, marketplaces, or physical locations. Finance may also have to manage refunds, disputes, settlements, payouts, and multiple banking relationships.
So payments are becoming part of a wider financial workflow, not a series of individual transactions.
Technology can take some of the repetitive work out of this process. More importantly, it lets finance teams look at the workflow as a whole. Can a successful payment automatically update an invoice? Can payment information move into accounting without being entered again? Can a failed transaction trigger the next step without someone having to monitor it?
These are questions about how financial processes should work, and technology can help make them happen.
Finance starts thinking in systems
Accounting and financial controls remain at the centre of the function, but finance professionals also need to be comfortable with data, digital systems, and the way information moves between them.
A 2025 Wolters Kluwer survey of 100 senior finance executives in India found that 74% ranked digital transformation as a top priority, while 66% prioritized workflow automation. The survey also identified fragmented systems and data silos as challenges for finance teams.
Finance professionals do not need to become software developers. But they do need to understand what a system can do, where a process is breaking down, and what should happen when two systems need to exchange information.
As routine work becomes more automated, finance teams can spend more time on analysis, planning, problem-solving, and working with other parts of the business. That also brings them closer to decisions about how processes are built, how different systems connect, and where technology can improve them.
Connecting financial systems
An API allows different software applications to exchange information and interact with each other. For finance teams, this means that payment information related to payments does not have to stop at the payment platform. Transaction information can move into systems handling invoices, accounting, orders, or customer records.
For example, once a customer completes a payment, that transaction information can pass to another application, which can update the relevant financial record or trigger the next step in the workflow.
Zoho Payments provides REST-based APIs that allow businesses to incorporate payment functionality into their applications. It also supports webhooks, which can send real-time notifications when events such as successful or failed payments, refunds, and payouts take place.
For finance, the value is in what these connections let the business do. Payment collection, invoicing, and reconciliation can become one workflow, instead of separate activities that require moving information between systems.
Building finance operations that can scale
A process that works when a business handles a few dozen transactions can become a bottleneck as the number of customers, invoices, payment methods, and bank transactions grows. More manual work also creates more opportunities for errors and mismatches.
Connected systems can help businesses handle more volume without increasing manual work at the same rate. They can reduce the need to move information between systems manually, limit mismatches, and give finance teams better visibility into financial activity.
Zoho Payments is one example of this connected approach.When used with Zoho Books, payment information can flow into the accounting workflow, helping businesses record collections, track settlements, and reconcile transactions. For businesses with more specific requirements, APIs provide another way to connect payment functionality with existing applications and workflows.
The aim is to make payments, invoices, and reconciliation work together rather than treating them as separate tasks. This can give finance teams more control over how financial information moves through the business, while reducing the amount of manual intervention as transaction volumes grow. The finance team will still close the books, manage cash, and oversee reporting. But it is also likely to have a greater role in deciding which systems connect, which tasks should be automated, and how financial data moves from one part of the business to another.
Finance isn’t becoming IT. But understanding the numbers increasingly means understanding the systems that move them.

articles.title: IQVIA fined $7.8 million for failing to properly anonymize health data
articles.text:
Italy's Data Protection Authority (GPDP) has fined IQVIA €7 million ($7.8M) over poor data-processing practices that the agency says could have put roughly one million patients at risk of data exposure and de-anonymization.
IQVIA is a multinational company that provides healthcare data analysis, technology, and clinical research services. The company claims on its website that it operates in over 100 countries and handles 68 petabytes of data and 1.2 billion patient records.
Italian authorities investigated IQVIA's data-processing practices in April 2025, and last month decided that the company did not provide adequate health-data anonymization warranties, despite its claims.
GPDP has found that IQVIA's Italian division had created a database containing the health information of roughly one million patients by aggregating data from 800 general practitioners.
While the company used a unique code instead of patients' names in those records, the data protection agency found they could be used to track and de-anonymize patients over time.
"The code associated with each patient made it possible to track them over time,” explained GPDP in an announcement published late last week.
“Combined with a very detailed set of information (year of birth, sex, diagnoses, symptoms, prescriptions, tests, vaccinations, as well as location data), it made it possible to single out individual patients and, using reasonable means, reidentify them.”
In addition, IQVIA processed data without an appropriate legal basis and without informing patients, which violates the GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation).
Finally, IQVIA allegedly did not establish or follow any data retention periods, with the GPDP finding records dating back as far as 2001.
For a subset of 3,300 patients in IQVIA's database, the company also included names, tax identification numbers, addresses, and contact details.
In addition to the $7.8 million fine, Italian authorities also ordered the company to bring its practices into compliance within 120 days.
BleepingComputer has contacted the firm with questions about the fine, and a spokesperson sent us the following statement:
"IQVIA is committed to the responsible use of data and information and continues to cooperate with the Authority. Protecting data is a core priority for IQVIA, and we maintain robust safeguards, including the use of pseudonymization and encryption, to support responsible data use in healthcare.
IQVIA acknowledges the decision adopted by the Italian Data Protection Authority and reserves the right to appeal. The dataset to which the Italian Data Protection Authority's decision relates is not used by IQVIA in conduct of clinical research services and does not relate to the conduct of clinical trials on behalf of the sponsors.
We have engaged constructively with the Italian Data Protection Authority throughout this process and have already taken steps to adopt the measures necessary to ensure full alignment with the Authority's guidance."

articles.title: La reputación de la IA está en entredicho. La solución de la industria: cambiar el discurso a la "superinteligencia"
articles.text:
El Gobierno de EEUU quiere cambiar el relato. Los incidentes que han protagonizado durante las últimas semanas varios modelos de inteligencia artificial (IA) de frontera, como el ataque a Hugging Face, y la posibilidad de que esta tecnología en el futuro represente una amenaza existencial para el ser humano han dañado la reputación de la IA. La Administración Trump está decidida a resolver de una vez por todas la crisis de confianza a la que se enfrenta esta industria, y su forma de hacerlo es cuando menos peculiar.
El primer paso que ha dado persigue intentar cambiar la forma en que se habla de la IA impulsando la adopción del término 'superinteligencia' en vez de 'inteligencia artificial'. El destierro del adjetivo 'artificial' y la llegada del prefijo 'super' intentan que los usuarios dejemos atrás la posible desconfianza que despierta una tecnología que todavía genera inquietud y la sustituyamos por una percepción mucho más ambiciosa: la de una herramienta capaz no solo de imitar nuestras capacidades, sino de superarlas.
No obstante, esto no es todo. El Gobierno estadounidense se ha ganado la complicidad de varios laboratorios de IA y compañías de tecnología, como Anthropic, Meta, Nvidia o Google. El pasado 29 de septiembre Donald Trump y varios ejecutivos de la industria de la IA, como Dario Amodei, Mark Zuckerberg, Jensen Huang o Sundar Pichai, presentaron un acuerdo que propone que las compañías adopten varias medidas de seguridad adicionales, como controles internos y auditorías independientes.
Esto es más una campaña de marketing que un mecanismo efectivo de seguridad
El problema de fondo que plantea la estrategia de la Administración Trump para 'lavar la cara' a la IA consiste en que el acuerdo de seguridad es voluntario. Los laboratorios no tendrán la obligación legal de llevar a cabo unos determinados controles internos y aceptar auditorías independientes; lo harán solo si quieren hacerlo, por lo que no están sujetos a mecanismos de cumplimiento equiparables a los de una regulación. En un ámbito tan delicado no parece una buena idea dejar la seguridad de los modelos de IA de frontera al amparo solo de la buena voluntad de las empresas de IA.
Al Gobierno de EEUU y los laboratorios no les va a resultar fácil cambiar a corto plazo la forma en que los usuarios percibimos la IA
Con toda probabilidad, al Gobierno de EEUU y los laboratorios no les va a resultar fácil cambiar a corto plazo la forma en que los usuarios percibimos la IA, sobre todo si nos ceñimos a aquellas personas que desconfían de esta tecnología. Y es que la crisis de confianza no ha sido desencadenada únicamente por la posibilidad de que en el futuro pueda llegar una superinteligencia peligrosa para el ser humano; muchas personas están preocupadas por el impacto que la IA ya está teniendo en el mercado laboral.
Otras preocupaciones inmediatas son la amenaza que la IA representa para la privacidad de nuestros datos, los contenidos generados automáticamente, el consumo energético de los centros de datos y el poder acumulado por las grandes compañías de tecnología. Dario Amodei, el director general de Anthropic, ha sido certero al reconocer que la crisis de confianza a la que se enfrenta la IA la han desencadenado estos problemas.
Por este motivo, más que cambiarle el nombre a la IA o pedir a los laboratorios que se comprometan voluntariamente a hacerla más segura, probablemente será necesario demostrar con hechos que esta tecnología puede desarrollarse sin ignorar sus riesgos. La confianza de los usuarios no parece que vaya a recuperarse simplemente cambiando las palabras; probablemente se recuperará respondiendo a las preocupaciones que ya existen y estableciendo mecanismos de control capaces de garantizar que las promesas de la industria no dependerán únicamente de su buena voluntad.

articles.title: Free Mobile a une nouveauté pratique pour ses abonnés, mais il y a une condition
articles.text:
Free Mobile permet désormais de transférer directement son eSIM, la carte SIM dématérialisée qui porte la ligne, entre un iPhone et un Google Pixel, dans les deux sens, sans repasser par son espace abonné. Pour un abonné qui en a déjà une, l’opération ne coûte rien de plus. En revanche, seuls les Pixel sont concernés pour l’instant côté Android. Free indique que d’autres marques Android pourront l’être « prochainement », sans liste ni date.
Plus besoin de générer une nouvelle eSIM
Jusqu’ici, changer de téléphone avec une eSIM Free pouvait obliger à passer par l’espace abonné : supprimer l’eSIM du premier appareil, puis l’activer sur le second, avec une connexion Internet pendant les deux opérations. Le transfert se fait désormais directement dans les réglages d’iOS et d’Android. L’opérateur l’a annoncé sur le compte Free_1337 : le transfert entre iPhone et Pixel, et inversement, est « simplifié » et reste « sans frais supplémentaires si vous avez déjà une eSIM ». Sur le Pixel, l’option propose de récupérer une SIM depuis un iPhone ou un iPad. Sur l’iPhone, elle apparaît sous le nom « Transférer à partir d’Android », à côté du transfert entre deux iPhone.
 Du nouveau chez @Free !
Le transfert de SIM/eSIM entre les iPhones et les Google Pixel (et inversement) est désormais simplifié 📱✨
Le transfert entre les différents OS reste fluide et sans frais supplémentaires si vous avez déjà une eSIM🔄
D’autres marques Android pourront également être compatibles prochainement 🚀
— Free 1337 (@Free_1337) October 2, 2026
Les conditions à réunir
Free Mobile figure désormais dans la liste des opérateurs français référencés par Apple, avec Orange et SFR. Selon cette page d’assistance, il faut un iPhone 11 ou plus récent sous iOS 26 ou une version ultérieure, et un smartphone Android sous Android 16 ou plus récent. Les deux appareils doivent aussi être connectés à un réseau Wi-Fi, avec le Bluetooth activé.
Pixel uniquement, pour l’instant
Free ne parle pas de n’importe quel smartphone Android : seuls les Google Pixel sont cités. Samsung, Xiaomi, Honor et les autres ne sont donc pas concernés pour le moment, et les générations de Pixel compatibles ne sont pas précisées. D’autres marques comme Samsung et Xiaomi prennent bien en charge la fonction de leur côté, mais l’opérateur doit aussi l’intégrer, ce qui explique la limite actuelle. Par ailleurs, la documentation de Google sur le transfert d’un iPhone vers un Pixel cite Orange et SFR, mais pas encore Free. Mieux vaut donc vérifier la compatibilité de son appareil avant de changer de téléphone.
Quant aux abonnés Bouygues Telecom, ils peuvent aussi transférer leur eSIM entre iPhone et Android, mais la procédure est plus longue : elle passe par l’espace client.

articles.title: Les Nothing Ear (3) perdent 65,95€ sur Amazon avant les Jours Flash Prime : notre avis avant d'acheter
articles.text:
Les Nothing Ear (3) misent sur un boîtier en aluminium doté de micros pour les appels, une idée que notre test a trouvée pratique. Leur son nous a en revanche moins convaincus, ce qui change la manière de lire cette baisse à 113,05 €.
Sortis en septembre 2025 à 179 euros, les Nothing Ear (3) sont les écouteurs à réduction de bruit de Nothing positionnés au-dessus des Ear (3a), avec codec LDAC et certification IP54. Ils sont actuellement proposés à 113,05 € au lieu de 179 € sur Amazon, soit 37 % de remise. Leur particularité tient dans le boîtier : deux micros et un bouton Talk le transforment en micro déporté pour les appels ou les notes vocales.
Cette offre s’adresse surtout à celles et ceux qui téléphonent beaucoup en déplacement et apprécient un objet soigné. Pour la musique, notre test a été plus sévère, et mieux vaut le savoir avant d’acheter.
Les écouteurs Nothing Ear (3) en noir sont affichés à 113,05 € sur Amazon, contre 179 € à leur lancement, avec leur boîtier Super Mic.
Pourquoi choisir les Nothing Ear (3) ?
- Des appels plus clairs grâce au boîtier : avec les seuls écouteurs, notre test a relevé une voix étouffée ; en parlant dans le boîtier, la captation devient bien plus naturelle. Un vrai plus pour un appel dans la rue ou une note vocale.
- Une finition qui se remarque : la base en aluminium anodisé du boîtier donne une vraie sensation de montée en gamme, au prix d’un poids de 71,4 g, contre 51,9 g pour la génération précédente.
- Une application complète : Nothing X propose un égaliseur paramétrique à 8 bandes, un test auditif et un test d’ajustement des embouts. De quoi adapter le rendu et la tenue à vos oreilles.
Le téléphone avant la musique
Au quotidien, les Ear (3) se montrent compacts, légers et stables, avec quatre tailles d’embouts fournies, même si la plus grande reste un peu petite. Le Bluetooth 5.4 multipoint permet de basculer entre ordinateur et smartphone, et la portée s’est révélée excellente dans notre test des Nothing Ear (3). La certification IP54 protège écouteurs et boîtier des éclaboussures et de la poussière, et la recharge sans fil Qi est de la partie. Comptez environ 5 h 45 d’écoute avec réduction de bruit, et 2,5 recharges supplémentaires dans le boîtier.
Ils conviendront aux actifs qui enchaînent les appels hors du bureau et à ceux qui veulent des écouteurs au design distinctif. La réduction de bruit atténue bien les basses fréquences, mais laisse passer les haut-médiums, comme les voix. Ils sont moins indiqués pour les mélomanes : nous avons trouvé leur son en V très radical, spectaculaire mais fatigant, et l’égaliseur ne corrige que partiellement ces excès. Le mode transparence, qui néglige presque les aigus, et le réglage du volume par appui long déçoivent aussi.
Face aux Ear (3a), un écart difficile à justifier pour la musique
Les Ear (3) se distinguent d’abord par leur boîtier en aluminium et son Super Mic. Sur le plan sonore, notre test les juge en recul face aux Nothing Ear de 2024, et la comparaison est cruelle face aux Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless 4 ou aux Huawei FreeBuds Pro 4, vendus dans la même gamme de prix. Les Ear (3a), que notre comparatif des meilleurs écouteurs sans fil retient comme bon rapport qualité-prix sous les 100 euros, offrent un bon équilibre dans les médiums et les aigus, même si leurs basses sont trop en avant par défaut. Si le téléphone n’est pas votre priorité, ce sont eux qu’il faut regarder en premier.
✅ Les points forts
- Boîtier en aluminium anodisé et Super Mic efficace pour les appels
- Puissance sonore et basses fréquences bien isolées
- Application Nothing X complète, avec égaliseur 8 bandes
- Écouteurs confortables et stables, certifiés IP54
- Multipoint, LDAC et recharge sans fil
❌ Les limites
- Son en V fatigant et peu naturel, noté 5/10 dans notre test
- Isolation perfectible sur les voix et mode transparence décevant
- Réglage du volume lent et peu intuitif
- Autonomie limitée à 3 h 45 en LDAC avec réduction de bruit
Si le Super Mic répond à votre usage, les Nothing Ear (3) sont à 113,05 € chez Amazon, soit 65,95 € de moins que leur prix de lancement.
À 113,05 €, les Nothing Ear (3) deviennent plus faciles à défendre qu’à 179 €, sans changer de nature pour autant. Notre test leur a attribué 6/10 : ils brillent par leur boîtier, leur confort et leurs appels via le Super Mic, beaucoup moins par leur restitution sonore. Ils s’adressent donc à ceux qui passent plus de temps au téléphone qu’à écouter attentivement de la musique.
Si vous cherchez avant tout un son agréable sur de longues sessions, tournez-vous plutôt vers les Ear (3a) ou les références de notre comparatif. Si c’est le design qui vous séduit, prévoyez quelques minutes avec l’égaliseur pour calmer les basses et les aigus. Vous limiterez ainsi la fatigue que nous avons ressentie lors des écoutes prolongées.
Pour profiter du Prime Day, n’oubliez pas de devenir membre Amazon Prime. Vous bénéficiez d’un essai gratuit de 30 jours, c’est donc le bon moment pour tester.

articles.title: Fast and Furious : Vin Diesel lâche enfin l'info que tous les fans attendaient
articles.text:
Quand un filon pèse plus de 7 milliards de dollars au box-office mondial, la notion d’« adieux » relève du pur marketing. La nouvelle est tombée jeudi 1er octobre par l’intermédiaire du média américain Deadline : Universal et sa plateforme de streaming Peacock préparent une série Fast & Furious en prise de vues réelles.
L’objectif est clair : installer la franchise à la télévision dès 2028, une année stratégique où sortira également au cinéma Fast Forever (le 11e et théoriquement dernier film de la saga principale, calé au 17 mars 2028).
La bénédiction (intéressée) du patriarche Vin Diesel pour Fast and Furious
Pendant dix ans, l’idée de décliner la franchise Fast and Furious à la télévision a été balayée d’un revers de main. Il a fallu une réorganisation au sommet d’Universal pour faire sauter le verrou. Lorsque Donna Langley, patronne emblématique du studio cinéma, a également pris les rênes du pôle télévision de NBCUniversal, Vin Diesel a subitement trouvé à l’idée toutes les vertus du monde.
Présent lors des présentations d’NBCUniversal à New York, l’interprète de Dominic Toretto, qui occupera le poste de producteur exécutif sur la série, s’est fendu d’un discours à la tonalité très « Toretto » :
« Depuis dix ans, les fans en veulent toujours plus. Ils veulent voir l’univers s’étendre autour des personnages historiques et de leurs histoires. C’est à partir du moment où Donna Langley a repris la télévision que j’ai su que l’intégrité des personnages, l’aura internationale et ce sentiment de ‘famille’ seraient préservés. »
Derrière la rhétorique du gardien du temple, il y a un calcul industriel limpide : au moment où le grand écran ferme son chapitre principal, Universal cherche à verrouiller ses abonnés sur Peacock. Pas folle la guêpe.
Un commando de showrunners habitués aux gros bras
Pour tenir le volant de cette adaptation sérielle, Universal a recruté un duo rodé aux récits d’action rugueux et à la testostérone télévisuelle :
Mike Daniels, passé par les salles d’écriture de Sons of Anarchy et Shades of Blue.
Wolfe Coleman, vétéran de 9-1-1: Lone Star.
Tous deux feront office de co-showrunners, scénaristes du pilote et producteurs délégués. Ils seront entourés de la garde rapprochée historique de la franchise cinématographique : Neal H. Moritz, Chris Morgan, Jeff Kirschenbaum et Sam Vincent. Aucun détail n’a filtré sur l’intrigue, le casting ou une éventuelle apparition de Vin Diesel à-l’écran, mais l’équipe de production est en place.
Universal entend dupliquer la méthode Disney/Marvel ou Lucasfilm : transformer une saga cinématographique vieillissante en un univers étendu tentaculaire, alimenté par le streaming.

articles.title: „Da wurde ein Fehler gemacht“: Wie schnell Blogs unter Druck der US-Regierung verschwinden
articles.text:
Digitale Souveränität: Wie schnell Blogs unter Druck der US-Regierung verschwinden
„Autistici/Inventati schließt. Bleibt menschlich“, so liest sich das letzte digitale Lebenszeichen der italienischen Hacktivisten-Gruppe. Mit der Domain „autistici.org“ bot die Plattform eine Heimat für Blogs, Websites, E-Mail-Konten und Mailinglisten. Doch Ende August stufte die US-Regierung diese Gruppe als „global-agierende Terroristengruppe“ ein. Laut einer offiziellen Veröffentlichung liefere sie eine „digitale Infrastruktur für gewalttätige Antifa-Zellen und andere extrem linke Militante in aller Welt“. In der Folge sperrte die italienische Banca Etica das Konto von A/I und schließlich nahm die Gruppe, die auf Spenden von Nutzer:innen angewiesen ist, die Domain offline.
Im deutschsprachigen Raum machte dies Anne Roth publik. Ihr Blog „annalist“, den sie bis dahin unter der zugehörigen Domain NoBlogs.org seit 19 Jahren betrieben hatte, war damit im Netz auch nicht mehr auffindbar. Sie hatte ihn ursprünglich begonnen, um sich dort mit politischen Themen, staatlicher Kontrolle und Überwachung zu befassen und hatte daher eine Domain gesucht, die das Tracking und Weitergeben von Daten ausschloss. Im Fediverse auf Mastodon machte Roth auf die Sperrung der Domain aufmerksam, mit der mehr als 20.000 Blogs nicht mehr zugänglich sind. Auch beruflich setzt sie sich mit Netzpolitik auseinander, als Referentin im Bundestag für Die Linke. Als Betroffene einer solchen Sperrung berichtet sie über das Gefühl und welche Nachteile unserer Internet-Architektur das zeigt.

articles.title: Six months on, Koko's carbon credits still have no buyer
articles.text:
Koko Networks (UK) Limited, the British arm of insolvent Kenyan clean-cooking company Koko Networks, has failed to find a buyer for its carbon credits at a fair price, leaving creditors expecting little or no recovery as the company winds down.
The trouble began in Kenya when Koko Networks Limited, the operating company that served more than one million households with subsidised cooking fuel, laid off more than 700 employees in January and entered administration on February 1. The Kenyan government had declined to issue the Letter of Authorisation needed to sell carbon credits into international compliance markets, cutting off revenue that helped keep the fuel affordable.
The carbon credits are the UK arm’s main asset, as Koko Networks (UK) Limited sold them and guaranteed group debts. Without a sale, FirstRand Bank, which is owed $60 million, and other unsecured creditors owed about £126 million ($167 million) expect to recover nothing. The administration is expected to cost close to £880,000 ($1.16 million), excluding administrators’ fees.
“We do not anticipate that the bank (FirstRand) will be repaid in full from the company’s assets,” PwC, the accounting firm appointed administrator of Koko Networks (UK) Limited on February 19, said in a progress report dated September 17.
The sale process began on July 17, when PwC started marketing Koko’s assets as part of the insolvency process. It initially sought buyers for the wider business, including its technology, manufacturing operations and fuel distribution platform, in deals worth more than $15 million.
According to the report, PwC held talks with three potential purchasers and five brokers before appointing a broker to market the credits. Offers have since arrived, but the administrators said they “do not consider that these offers would generate a meaningful return to the estate.” PwC will continue marketing the credits.
The report did not disclose how many credits Koko holds, what type they are, or their value on the company’s books.
Creditors fund the wind-down
With little cash coming in, creditors are financing the closure. Koko UK received about $659,000 during the period from the administrators of the Kenyan business. The report said the money comes from certain creditors under a wider group arrangement.
The funding carries interest and is treated as an administration expense, meaning it must be repaid ahead of unsecured creditors, those with no security over company assets.
The administrators project costs of about £880,000 ($1.19 million), before their own fees. Lawyers are the largest expense, led by DLA Piper UK, the law firm advising on the case.
Creditors will also be asked to approve about £181,000 ($245,000) of unpaid costs from before the appointment, most of it PwC’s own time. The company has not yet approved its remuneration.
Against that bill, there is very little to recover, as the company holds under £280,000 ($379,000) in cash.
Koko’s largest receivable, a debt of about £1.1 million ($1.49 million) from Koko Rwanda, the group’s Rwandan business, is not expected to be repaid because that company is itself insolvent.
The biggest creditor is FirstRand Bank, acting through its Rand Merchant Bank division, the South African lender’s investment banking arm.
The bank’s collateral does not include the company’s main assets, so administrators do not expect it to recover anything. Other unsecured creditors are also expected to receive nothing, as is His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs (HMRC), the UK tax authority.
The administrators are also assessing possible legal claims with their counterparts in Kenya and the group’s Mauritius company and are seeking outside funding to pursue them. The report did not state who the claims would target. It warns that if they go ahead, “significant costs will arise” on top of the current estimates.
Koko’s failed carbon-credit model
Koko Networks was founded in 2014 as a clean-cooking company focused on replacing charcoal and other polluting fuels with subsidised bioethanol cooking fuel. The company sold the fuel to about 1.3 million Kenyan households and relied on carbon revenue to keep prices low.
Its Kenyan operating company, Koko Networks Limited, entered administration on February 1 after the government declined to issue the authorisation letters needed to sell credits into international compliance markets. The UK company, which commercialised the credits generated in Kenya, entered administration on February 19.
PwC expects to send its next report in about six months, or at the end of the administration if that comes sooner.
