articles.title: OpenAI will show visual ads in ChatGPT while you generate images
articles.text:
OpenAI is expanding ads in ChatGPT, and one of the first new formats will show visual ads while you're generating images.
The company says it will begin testing the new ad format later this month in the U.S. with an initial group of advertisers.
According to OpenAI, these ads could use images to show product inspiration, how a product is used, or experiences associated with a service, which gives advertisers a more visual way to promote themselves inside ChatGPT.
"Initially, we'll test this new ad format during image generation in ChatGPT. Ads will be clearly labeled, and remain separate from the image being created," OpenAI explained.
OpenAI also reiterated that ads do not influence ChatGPT's answers.
The company says ChatGPT now reaches 1.2 billion people every week, and advertising is becoming another way for OpenAI to make money from users who may not pay for a subscription.
OpenAI is also getting more serious about measuring ChatGPT ads
Alongside the new visual format, OpenAI is adding more tools that allow advertisers to measure whether ChatGPT ads actually lead to purchases or other conversions.
It's integrating with Hightouch, Tealium, and LiveRamp for conversion data, while attribution partners now include AppsFlyer, Adjust, Branch, Triple Whale, Kochava, and several others.
OpenAI is also working with DoubleVerify and Integral Ad Science on brand suitability, which is particularly important for ChatGPT because ads appear around conversations rather than a traditional webpage.
The company says its safeguards are designed to prevent ads from appearing in emotionally vulnerable, sensitive, or otherwise unsuitable conversations.
OpenAI also says these independent partners will not get access to private user conversations while evaluating whether its advertising safeguards are working as intended.
For now, the visual ad experiment is limited to the U.S., but OpenAI clearly sees ads becoming a much larger part of ChatGPT as it tries to monetize its 1.2 billion weekly users.

articles.title: Gracias a la IA, Amazon ha pasado de tener uno de los flujos de caja más holgados del mundo a un reguero de pérdidas
articles.text:
Las grandes tecnológicas llevan tres años pagando la IA con su propia caja, y esa caja ha cambiado de dueño. Un gráfico de a16z lo resume perfectamente: desde 2022, el flujo de caja libre de los hiperescaladores –las grandes tecnológicas que operan centros de datos a gran escala– ha pasado de unos 275.000 millones de dólares a prácticamente 0. Cero.
El de los fabricantes de semiconductores, en cambio, ha saltado de 50.000 a 400.000 millones.
Por qué es importante. Este es uno de los primeros rastros nítidos que deja el dinero de la IA. Porque hasta ahora casi todo eran promesas en torno a la implementación empresarial de los agentes, la multiplicación de la productividad y la esperanza de mayores ingresos futuros.
Lo único medible a gran escala ha sido una transferencia. Sale de las cuentas de Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon y Meta, y llega a las de NVIDIA, TSMC o los fabricantes de memoria.
- Justo ayer hablábamos del fenómeno financiero de Micron, que ha multiplicado por doce sus beneficios trimestrales de un año para otro.
- En 2025 eran comparables a los de Cisco y en 2026 ya superan los de Apple.
En cifras.
- 275.000 → 0. Flujo de caja libre aproximado de los hiperescaladores entre 2022 y hoy. En miles de millones de dólares.
- 50.000 → 400.000. El de los fabricantes de chips en el mismo período.
- 700.000 millones. El gasto en capital que los cuatro grandes hiperescaladores preveían para 2026.
- 76%. Peso de las tecnológicas en el crecimiento de beneficios del S&P 500 este año, según a16z.
Entre líneas. Flujo de caja libre y beneficio son cosas distintas.
- Beneficio es lo que queda tras restar a los ingresos los gastos del año. Una inversión grande no lo hunde de golpe, porque su coste se reparte en varios ejercicios.
- Flujo de caja libre es el dinero que de verdad entra en la empresa menos el que sale para invertir. Si compras servidores por 100.000 millones, salen hoy, enteros.
Las cuatro grandes generan más efectivo que nunca, pero sale por la puerta en forma de servidores, naves y contratos eléctricos casi en cuanto entra. Eso las convierte en algo que nunca habían sido: empresas intensivas en capital, más parecidas a una eléctrica que a una firma de software.
UN VISTAZO A...
En primer plano. Amazon ya está ahí. En los últimos doce meses sus operaciones han generado 161.400 millones, pero ha gastado 169.000 millones netos en inmuebles y equipos. El agujero es de 7.600 millones, el primero desde 2023.
Lo más llamativo está en su previsión: Andy Jassy ha subido el gasto de este año de unos 200.000 a unos 220.000 millones por el encarecimiento de la memoria. La subida de precios nos afecta a los consumidores pero también a los proveedores.
- Amazon no está sola: Alphabet ha registrado un flujo de caja libre negativo de 5.900 millones en el segundo trimestre.
- Dicho eso, en doce meses sigue teniendo un flujo positivo de más de 53.000 millones...
- ...lo cual no quita que este haya sido su primer trimestre con un flujo de caja negativo desde que salió a bolsa en 2004.
Y ahora qué. El hueco solo se cierra de dos formas:
- Con ingresos, que van lentos. En abril, apenas un 2% de los hogares estadounidenses pagaba por algún servicio de IA.
- O con deuda, que Amazon ya ha avisado al regulador de que podría emitir.
Mientras tanto, el reparto no cambia. NVIDIA cobra al contado, pero Amazon, Google y Meta cobrarán a cinco años vista, si cobran.

articles.title: Microsoft's fix for shader compilation wait is coming to Nvidia, Intel, and Qualcomm GPUs
articles.text:
Something to look forward to: Microsoft is preparing to expand its Advanced Shader Delivery service to PCs with Intel, Nvidia and Qualcomm graphics hardware, a move aimed at cutting down the lengthy shader-compilation process that can hold up a game's first launch. The service has already appeared in the PC version of Gears of War: E-Day, but it currently works only with AMD Radeon GPUs. Microsoft says support for more Windows devices is coming later in October.
Advanced Shader Delivery, or ASD, distributes compiled shaders from the cloud instead of having each player's PC compile them locally before play. Microsoft says that can reduce the process from "several minutes" to "just a few seconds," with a 95% reduction in burn time overall.
Shader compilation is now a familiar issue for PC players, especially in large games with demanding graphics systems. Shaders are small programs used by the GPU to render lighting, surfaces, effects and other visual elements. A game may need to compile them for a particular PC setup before it can run smoothly.
This process often happens when you launch a game for the first time. In some cases, it also takes place during gameplay as new areas, effects or assets load. When that happens, you can notice stuttering, even on high-end hardware.
Microsoft's approach is meant to move more of that work away from the player's machine. Instead of requiring the PC to prepare all of the shader data locally, ASD delivers precompiled shaders through the cloud. The goal is to reduce both the initial wait and the risk of shader-related hitches once a game is running.
Wendy Ho, a DirectX program manager at Microsoft, said in a company blog post that the service will soon support "additional Windows devices powered by Intel, Nvidia and Qualcomm."
Broader GPU coverage gives ASD a better chance of becoming a practical option for major PC releases rather than a feature tied to a narrower group of systems. Nvidia remains a major presence in PC graphics, while Intel has expanded its Arc GPU lineup and Qualcomm is pushing further into Windows devices.
The first implementation also highlights the scale of the problem Microsoft is trying to address. Gears of War: E-Day has had a substantial shader-compilation step at startup. Microsoft reports Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is the next game scheduled to support the technology.
The service will not automatically improve every PC game. Developers must build ASD support into their titles, and there is no indication that it will become standard across the industry in the near term. Some games will continue to compile shaders locally, while others may use different caching or precompilation methods.
Still, shader compilation has become one of the clearest weak points in the PC gaming experience. Players can spend heavily on fast processors, modern graphics cards and solid-state storage, then face several minutes of waiting before a new game reaches its menu. If ASD works as Microsoft describes, it could speed up first launches and reduce one of the most common sources of PC game stutter.

articles.title: Edmonton mayor hints at upcoming support for entrepreneurs as city’s Startup Week kicks off | BetaKit
articles.text:
Downtown Edmonton was abuzz with founders, investors, innovators, and entrepreneurs this evening as the city gathered to officially kick off Edmonton Startup Week.
Spearheaded by Edmonton Unlimited, the annual celebration runs from Oct. 5 to 9. This year’s run of shows includes 30 events at Edmonton Unlimited’s headquarters, and an additional 49 events happening throughout the city.
Events include workshops on the fundamentals of building a startup, panels exploring everything from AI to defence to fundraising, an entire day platforming Edmonton’s burgeoning deep tech ecosystem, and a whole lot of networking.
Opening remarks honed in on the importance of Edmonton’s startups to the growing profile of the city’s entrepreneurial community.
Mayor Andrew Knack, who during his remarks issued an official proclamation from the City denoting this week as Edmonton Startup Week going forward, called the event an opportunity to work on some of the biggest problems facing the world.
“We know the days ahead will feature critical conversations about some of the most complex challenges we’re facing in our world,” he said before adding that the health and vitality of Edmonton’s entrepreneurial class is an indicator of the city’s vitality overall.
RELATED: Edmonton Unlimited unveils 10 companies to watch ahead of Startup Week
“Ninety to 95 percent of businesses in Edmonton are small- and medium-sized businesses. If you’re not thriving, this city is not thriving,” he said.
Knack also teased the City’s upcoming four-year budget, telling a packed auditorium that it was poised to include support for entrepreneurs in the city.
“You will see for the first time in a long time that the city will be heavily invested in not through words, but actions,” Knack said to applause.
13th annual event
This year marks the 13th iteration of Edmonton Startup Week, with the event doubling down on last year’s theme of “step in, step up, step forward.” Over its tenure, Startup Week has grown into a cornerstone gathering for entrepreneurs and investors, with the event routinely drawing attendees from Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, and abroad.
This year’s kickoff featured a swath of local leaders, as well as a series of pitches from 10 companies chosen earlier this year as Edmonton Unlimited’s 10 companies to watch in 2026.
Edmonton Unlimited CEO Tom Viinikka touted a “big announcement” on Wednesday, Startup Week’s day showcasing deep tech. Viinikka also spoke to the growth the ecosystem has seen over the last year, telling the crowd that during the innovation corporation’s previous deep tech day last June, nearly 80 investors, including 66 from out of town, to local founders, connected with local founders, ultimately leading to investments into deep tech startups like Zero Point Cryogenics and Aqtiva.
“Investors are coming here, seeing what is being built, and investing,” he said.
Viinikka also cited critical milestones taken by companies moving through Edmonton Unlimited’s programming as indicative of the broader ecosystem’s accelerating momentum. A critical step is, according to Viinikka, a “milestone that must happen for a business to keep moving forward and to achieve specific goals.” Examples include benchmarks like creating a minimum viable product, developing a prototype, completing a first domestic sale, or receiving first patents and investment. Edmonton Unlimited has recorded 461 of those milestones this year.
“Collectively, they’re a measure of the entrepreneurial momentum of our ecosystem,” he said. “Imagine what we could do if we had 10 times those numbers … Startup Week is an opportunity to add to those numbers.”

articles.title: Germany just built the world's tallest wind turbine — engineers hail 'overwhelming moment' as structure prepares to generate 3.8 megawatts of power
articles.text:
Germany just built the world's tallest wind turbine — the 365-meter tower will generate 3.8 megawatts from high-altitude winds
But we don't yet know how well it will work
- The world's tallest wind turbine has been built in Germany
- It's designed to catch higher, stronger, more consistent winds
- An 'inside out' construction process was deployed to build up
There's a new milestone to report in the field of wind energy engineering: German company Gicon just completed construction on the tallest wind turbine in history, standing 365 meters (1,198 feet) tall near the town of Schipkau in Brandenburg.
According to the official press release (via Interesting Engineering), the structure is now the second tallest in Germany, as well as the tallest wind turbine in the world. The official commissioning of the towering electricity generator is set for November.
The reason for the extra height is simple: a higher altitude means stronger and more reliable winds. However, experts won't know if the additional power generation is worth the extra costs and engineering efforts until the new turbine has started operating.
This first super-tall turbine will have a rated output of 3.8 MW, with future builds expected to hit 7 MW. That's fairly modest by turbine standards, but it's expected that the new structure will hit peak capacity more often and more consistently, ultimately achieving twice the energy yield of a conventional wind turbine with the same rotor diameter.
A new approach to construction
"This is an overwhelming moment for our entire team," says Gircon CEO Prof. Dr. Jochen Großmann (via Google Translate). "What was long a challenging idea and then an equally challenging construction project now stands as a globally unique facility in Schipkau... we at Gicon are extremely proud of this."
The engineering team used a special 'inside out' approach to constructing the tower, using what's known as a strand jack system to lift the higher sections through the center of the base of the turbine before fixing them in place.
And there's another promising aspect to all this: Gicon says current wind farms can be retrofitted with the taller structures, meaning (in theory) more power from existing turbine plots without the need for more land development.

Once the world record turbine is running, we'll be able to see just how effective it is at harnessing the faster, more consistent winds at higher altitudes. If it proves a success, expect to see wind turbines getting a lot faster in the future.

articles.title: OpenAI is adding text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex
articles.text:
An invisible, machine-readable watermark in text output is rolling out to ChatGPT and Codex, but only for users in the European Union at first.
OpenAI is adding text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex
It’s launching textGrain watermarking in the EU, but OpenAI says it won’t be the ‘global default’ yet.
OpenAI says its textGrain watermarking “matched or exceeded” other approaches like Google DeepMind’s SynthID for text, which is also the basis for the watermarking Anthropic announced in August. Like OpenAI, Anthropic made the move to meet the requirements of the EU’s AI Act; however, not everyone was happy to learn about the addition.
OpenAI also included scores from AI benchmarks showing similar performance from watermarked and unwatermarked text. But it notes that textGrain “does not guarantee reliable detection,” and says text watermarks don’t verify accuracy, determine who owns the text, measure how much a human contributed, or prove human authorship.
Rolling out text watermarking in the EU. Over the coming weeks, we will introduce text watermarking to eligible ChatGPT and Codex users across all plans in the EU only. We are not making text watermarking a global default at launch. This regional approach gives us room to learn from real-world use and feedback.
Enabling opt-in watermarking for API customers. Starting today, API customers around the world will be able to opt in to watermarked text outputs for select models. This lets customers decide how watermarking fits their transparency obligations and the experiences they provide to users. We are also working with cloud partners to make watermarking available for OpenAI model outputs accessed through their services in the coming weeks.
Providing detector access to researchers and expert organizations. Approved researchers and expert organizations can apply starting today. In accordance with the Code of Practice, access will be initially granted on a case-by-case basis to support evaluation and improvement of text provenance. The tool will report whether it detects an OpenAI watermark, without identifying the user or revealing their prompts or conversations. Given the risk of missed watermarks and false positives, we are not making it publicly available at launch.

articles.title: Russia's uncrewed robot tank fails during debut military display in front of President Putin — vehicle repeatedly lost control links and eventually got stuck in the mud despite the switch to a human driver
articles.text:
Russia's uncrewed robot tank fails during debut military display in front of President Putin — vehicle repeatedly lost control links and eventually got stuck in the mud despite the switch to a human driver
Russia’s new Shturm uncrewed tank failed during its debut display at Tsentr-2026, a Russia-led strategic military exercise held from September 28 to October 3, 2026, losing its command-and-control (C2) link and eventually getting stuck in the mud. According to an October 3 Defense Blog post, the tank repeatedly lost its C2 radio link with its separate command vehicle, forcing organizers to abandon remote operations and switch to a human driver-mechanic for a demonstration in front of President Vladimir Putin.
Despite manual human control, the vehicle eventually got stuck in a muddy ditch beside a dirt track, with its tracks and front hull buried in the soil. The Shturm is a Russian heavy robotic, uncrewed assault tank system designed by Uralvagonzavod, a Russian machine-building company and the world’s largest tank manufacturer by output, primarily for urban combat
It is built on modified Soviet-era T-72 and T-90 tank chassis and features a shortened 125mm D-414 main gun, or alternative configurations such as twin 30mm 2A42 automatic cannons and thermobaric rocket launchers. Its defining feature — and the primary source of failure during its debut demonstration — is its control system, which allows the tank to be remotely operated from a separate crewed command vehicle within a radio link range of roughly 3 kilometers. It also has provision for a manual, on-board human driver.
According to Defense Blog, the Russian Defense Ministry initially said on Oct. 2 that Putin had been shown the new uncrewed combat vehicles, and that they provided fire support to assault units during the main stage of the drills. Reports of the failure emerged afterward. The vehicle has “several technical flaws, including an engine compartment and turret roof that are almost unprotected, areas drones most often target when attacking armored vehicles in Ukraine,” according to a Russian armor expert cited by Defense Blog. “The idea of this vehicle seems unsuccessful to me: dependence on a command post that has to be 3 to 4 kilometers away and in direct line of sight. Without proper communications like Starlink, or something similar, there is no point in such a vehicle,” he added. Starlink had earlier blocked russian drones from using its services in the country's ongoing four-year war with Ukraine.

articles.title: El uso de la IA que nunca te hubieses imaginado ya es una realidad. Te va a encantar lo que ha hecho Telefónica
articles.text:
¿Irías a escuchar una orquesta sinfónica donde la inteligencia artificial tuviese un gran protagonismo? La respuesta, si te gusta la música clásica y valoras a quien la toca, probablemente sea no. La buena noticia es que la IA no solo se puede utilizar para sustituir músicos, y Telefónica ha dado un buen ejemplo de cómo mezclar el mundo de la tecnología y la música clásica sin ofender a nadie ni menospreciar a los integrantes de la orquesta. De hecho, la intención de su última hazaña era la de mejorar la experiencia del público.
Pero, ¿cómo se mezcla IA y música clásica en directo sin llevarse por delante el arte? Telefónica cuenta con varias de las redes más sofisticadas para poder acceder a nuevas tecnologías basadas en inteligencia artificial y comunicaciones, y ha colaborado con la Escuela Superior de Música Reina Sofía. Su orquesta ha sido la protagonista, y la IA, junto con el público, ha tomado un nuevo rol en el espectáculo.
¿El objetivo? Involucrar a la IA y el público en el desempeño de la obra. ¿Cómo lo han conseguido? A través de sus smartphones, los más de mil asistentes han podido tomar decisiones en directo, contestando preguntas sobre sus emociones para que la IA pudiese analizarlas en tiempo real y comunicarse con el director de la orquesta, Josep Pons.
La idea es plasmar la sensación colectiva en el escenario de una forma única, permitiéndole a la propia orquesta conocer cómo se sienten los espectadores en tiempo real y actuando en consecuencia. Todo, con ayuda de un proceso que sería imposible realizar sin la IA de forma tan rápida y eficaz.
En este caso concreto, la inteligencia artificial puede realizar las preguntas necesarias, analizar todas las respuestas e interpretar cómo está reaccionando el público para trasladar esa sensación a la propia orquesta.
Telefónica ha demostrado que coger el móvil durante la actuación no es síntoma de aburrimiento, a la vez que ha conseguido mezclar dos mundos antagónicos que llevan años enfrentados por culpa de su naturaleza: la mayoría de músicos no están muy a favor de que la IA se entrometa en su mundo.
Ahora la cosa cambia, permitiendo, gracias a la tecnología, hacer de la IA un complemento muy potente para realizar tareas y sumar experiencias que, hasta el momento, eran impensables.
Con esta propuesta, Telefónica ha conseguido conectar ideas, personas y sensaciones a través de la tecnología en una experiencia tan tradicional como lo es una orquesta sinfónica, un hito que pone sobre la mesa una colaboración más viable entre el arte y la IA.

articles.title: Researchers are tracking a Chinese AI 'agent fleet' | TechCrunch
articles.text:
A new fleet of AI agents is making its presence felt on the internet. On Sunday, a group of independent researchers posted preliminary findings about the agents, observing that they seem to be running on Tencent’s infrastructure and targeting Alibaba’s map service, Amap.
Researchers, however, resisted the term “swarm,” noting that there seems to be little coordination between their different queries. “‘Agent fleet,’ not ‘swarm:’” one researcher wrote in the preliminary report, “many parallel agents on the same kind of task, with no sign of communication between them.”
The agents were discovered by monitoring traffic to the domain-scanning service urlquery, a technique that previously revealed long-running activity by OpenAI agents. AI agents often use urlquery to load websites that they cannot access directly, leaving a record of their activities that can be valuable to researchers.
In this case, the record showed queries to Alibaba’s Amap service, seeking directions to different entrances of various public places, including a park, a zoo, and a hospital.
The research is ongoing and so few details are available, but the behavior shows how persistent AI agent activity has become on the internet. In the wake of the Hugging Face incident, many researchers are actively monitoring for rogue agent activity on the internet. Much of that activity has been easy to find because agents tend to use the same techniques and make little effort to conceal themselves.
In this case, the agents don’t seem to have been doing anything more nefarious than side-stepping Alibaba’s API rules — but we may not always be so lucky.

articles.title: Another Historic Cipher Falls to AI - Schneier on Security
articles.text:
Another Historic Cipher Falls to AI
This one is from 1809, written by Napoleon’s nephew.
Jammy • October 5, 2026 10:00 AM
What happens now?
Clive Robonson • October 5, 2026 10:27 AM
@ Bruce, ALL,
We talk about security by obscurity
But not with encryption systems.
Now AI is getting to the point older codes and ciphers are getting broken we should think that “obscurity” is not the right word to use for codes and ciphers.
People should ask a question about both codes and ciphers especially of the older styles.
“What can not change through the whole process?”
And the answer is the “statistics” of the plaintext and ciphertext, otherwise you would not be able to decipher the ciphertext back to plaintext.
What we know is that Current AI LLM systems are built around so called “Digital Neural Networks”(DNNs) that are in reality just glorified “Digital Signal Processing”(DSP) systems configured as “adaptive filters”.
The thing about filters is they are very good at “lifting signals out of the noise”. Adaptive filters are very good at lifting signals out of background noise that changes constantly but in a predictable way.
Keytext in older ciphers often had a period the same length as the password/phrase used to generate the Keytext. And due to the failings of humans this was often quite short and mostly either around ten characters or less in length or a well known phrase. This remained true up untill and through WWII and was still used via hand ciphers by spys or simple mechanical machine ciphers up untill the 1980’s when the first microcontrollers with sufficient grunt became available.
Thus as plaintext has recognisable statistics even when combined with a keytext of recognisable ststistics (see chi-squared test).
We can expect Current AI LLM’s in an agenetic framework to basically pull out the desired signals.
Thus the only cipher systems we should expect to have some security are those where there is either no periodicity in the key text or the workload is many orders of magnitude greater than even large teams of humans can perform.
In short Current AI LLMs are going to be “on desktops” in the not to distant future, and with them your own “Pocket SigInt Agency”.

articles.title: Row-Parallel DRAM Computing Cuts Data-Reorganization Overhead (Syracuse, FAU, TU Dresden)
articles.text:
Researchers at Syracuse University, Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, and TU Dresden published a technical paper titled “RAPID: Row-Parallel Arithmetic Processing in DRAM.”
Abstract Excerpt: “Processing-using-memory (PUM) architectures perform computation directly within DRAM to reduce costly data movement between memory and processors. Because charge-sharing operations are confined to individual bitlines, existing DRAM-PUM architectures reorganize data into column-oriented, bit-serial representations. This organization is fundamentally incompatible with the row-oriented, word-parallel layouts used by conventional processors and accelerators, requiring expensive data-layout transformations whenever computation transitions between PUM and conventional execution. In this paper, we present RAPID, a Row-parallel Arithmetic Processing-In-DRAM architecture. RAPID augments the DRAM subarray with two lightweight extensions: migration cells that enable localized horizontal data movement between neighboring bitlines and inversion cells that provide efficient in-array logical inversion. These primitives enable RAPID to operate directly on row-parallel, bit-parallel data, preserving CPU-compatible layouts while exploiting the massive parallelism of the DRAM subarray.”
Find the technical paper here. October 2026.
Tegge, William C., João Paulo Cardoso de Lima, Shouzhi Fang, Jeronimo Castrillon, and Alex K. Jones. “RAPID: Row-Parallel Arithmetic Processing in DRAM.” arXiv preprint arXiv:2610.02502 (October 2026). https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.02502

articles.title: Sennheiser HD 480 Pro Plus professional monitoring headphones review - comfort and high quality - Tech Guide
articles.text:
- RATING
The Sennheiser HD 480 Pro Plus headphones are the go-to choice for audio professionals but also pack a punch for audiophiles who just want to enjoy the superior audio quality.
The Sennheiser HD 480 Pro Plus are professional monitoring headphones which means they must produce great sound so they can be used to judge the audio quality for professional recording.
And they do.
The Sennheiser HD 480 Pro Plus are closed back earphones which means they have sealed outer earcups so no outside noise can interfere with what you’re listening to.
And they keep the sound in as well.
For Tech Guide’s review we mainly used the Sennheiser HD 480 Pro Plus to record and edit our podcasts and used them to listen to music through our smartphone.
DESIGN
The Sennheiser HD 480 Pro Plus has thick plush velour ear pads and a matching headband padding.
It has a metal adjustable headband and plastic earcups and weigh 282g without the cable attached.
So we can confirm they are light and they are comfortable.
Comfort is an important feature because you are potentially wearing them for hours at a time.
That’s what we did recording and editing our podcasts and interviews and we never ever felt they were too heavy or bulky.
The cups are large and deep and easily cover our ears while the clamp force that keep the headphones on your hear is exactly right so you can move your head around easily without them slipping off.
Same deal if you are using them to listen music to music and bopping along to the songs.
And we were also wearing our reading glasses while we were wearing the headphones and it did not reduce our level of comfort.
Now these are wired headphones only – no Bluetooth here – hearing audio through a cable offers higher quality lossless uncompressed sound with zero latency.
Considering what the headphones were made for, the quality required is non-negotiable.
The headphones come with a 3m mini XLR to 3.5mm/6.3mm audio plug coiled cable.
And you also get the choice of which each ear cup to connect the cable at the mini XLR end so you can direct the cable so it won’t get in your way.
The Sennheiser HD 480 Pro Plus headphones come with a hard case for easy and transport.
SOUND
The Sennheiser HD 480 Pro Plus not surprisingly sound remarkable – we expected nothing less from this respected audio brand.
Now because they are closed back headphones there is no active noise cancellation but through the enveloping ear cups and solid clamp force this kept most of the ambient sounds and noises out.
But don’t expect them to block out louder noises like ANC headphones would.
Considering where these headphones are designed to be used, this is not an issue.
We never took the headphones outside and where we use them in our office was relatively quiet anyway so they still offered an impressive sound.
Under the hood, 38 mm dynamic drivers that have a different frequency response that make them ideal for recording and listening.
For listening to and recording vocal audio, like podcasts, the Sennheiser HD 480 Pro Plus made every syllable crisp and clear but this wasn’t much of a stretch for the headphones.
It’s when you’re listening to music that they really come into their own.
It’s really easy to hear the separation between the instruments and the vocals in tracks that have a lot going on.
And when it comes to bass, the Sennheiser HD 480 Pro Plus provided sumptuous levels without going over the top.
Listeners will enjoy a textured and detailed sound quality within an expansive soundstage which is an achievement for closed-back headphones.
The midranges are clear and full-bodied with enough room left to hear vocals clearly.
Treble was the real hero here with a solid middle ground without a trace of sibilance so it could sound smooth and even no matter what type of music you’re listening to.
And while the headphones are designed for professional monitoring, they are also popular with audiophiles who want to enjoy high-quality sound without spending hundreds of dollars more on headphones with ANC and Bluetooth connectivity.
The Sennheiser HD 480 Pro Plus headphones are available now and are priced at $739 but we have seen them as cheap as $641.
VERDICT
The Sennheiser HD 480 Pro Plus headphones are the go-to choice for audio professionals but also pack a punch for audiophiles who just want to enjoy the superior audio quality.

Ear coupling: circumaural
Transducer principle: dynamic
Transducer diameter: 38 mm
Frequency response: 3 to 28,700 Hz (-10 dB)
Sensitivity: 107 dB SPL (at 1 kHz/1Vrms); 98 dB (at 1 kHz, 1 mW)
Max. SPL: 130 dB (1 kHz, 5% THD)
THD: <0.5% (at 1 kHz, 100 dB SPL)

Temperature range: 0°C to +50°C for operation; -25°C to +70°C for storage

articles.title: Windows 11 : l’Explorateur de fichiers va enfin prendre en charge ce raccourci indispensable
articles.text:
La dernière build de Windows 11 déployée par Microsoft auprès des membres de son programme Insider apporte plusieurs améliorations à l’Explorateur de fichiers. Parmi celles-ci, Microsoft va enfin autoriser l’utilisation du tilde (~) pour accéder instantanément aux répertoires personnels ainsi qu’à ceux des données d’applications. Une excellente nouvelle puisque cette prise en charge permettra de s’affranchir de la saisie des chemins d’accès pouvant parfois être complexes.
Un raccourci pour accéder rapidement aux dossiers personnels
Jusqu’à présent, pour accéder à un dossier personnel ou à un répertoire de données d’application, la seule solution consistait à naviguer manuellement jusqu’à ceux-ci, ou bien de connaître le chemin d’accès direct pour le saisir dans la barre d’adresse de l’Explorateur de fichiers. Deux méthodes pas franchement intuitives et surtout pas particulièrement rapides, d’autant plus pour la seconde.
Mais Microsoft vient d’intégrer dans la dernière build de Windows 11 une nouvelle fonction dédiée à la touche tilde dans la barre d’adresse de l’Explorateur de fichiers. Comme cela existe sur d’autres systèmes d’exploitation, notamment sur macOS, Windows 11 va désormais pouvoir utiliser le tilde ~ pour créer un raccourci vers le dossier racine de votre profil utilisateur, habituellement au format C:\Utilisateurs\VotreNomDutilisateur.
Concrètement, cela signifie qu’à présent, vous pourrez accéder directement à votre répertoire utilisateur en saisissant ~ dans la barre d’adresse de l’Explorateur de fichiers. Par extension, vous pourrez accéder rapidement à vos répertoires personnels, comme le dossier contenant vos téléchargements, en saisissant ~\Téléchargements dans la barre d’adresse de l’Explorateur de fichiers. Vous pourrez même accéder au répertoire caché AppData en saisissant ~\AppData, ou encore atteindre directement les dossiers de données d’applications locales ou liées à votre profil en tapant ~\AppData\Local ou ~\AppData\Roaming.
La prise en charge de ce raccourci, qui permet de s’affranchir de la saisie du début du chemin d’accès vers le répertoire racine devrait largement simplifier la tâche aux utilisateurs. Et pour cause, Windows 11 a pris la mauvaise habitude de renommer le dossier personnel de l’utilisateur en n’utilisant que les cinq premiers caractères de l’adresse e-mail associée au compte Microsoft. Un nom tronqué que bon nombre oublie et qui rend la saisie manuelle d’un chemin d’accès vers un répertoire plus fastidieuse.
Cette nouvelle fonctionnalité, pour l’heure encore en cours de test auprès des Insiders devrait être déployée dans les semaines à venir pour le reste des utilisateurs.
D’autres nouveautés à venir pour l’Explorateur de fichiers
Outre l’arrivée prochaine de ce nouveau système de raccourci, l’Explorateur de fichiers va également profiter d’autres nouveautés intéressantes. Microsoft a en effet optimisé celui-ci pour qu’il conserve vos préférences de tri et de taille d’icônes. L’Explorateur de fichiers prend par ailleurs en charge les chemins d’accès entourés de guillemets. Vous n’aurez donc plus besoin de « nettoyer » un chemin d’accès copié dans le presse-papiers de Windows avant de le coller dans la barre d’adresses de l’Explorateur de fichiers.
À noter également que Microsoft a entrepris un travail d’harmonisation visant à remplacer progressivement les anciennes boîtes de dialogue héritées de Windows 95 par des fenêtres développées avec WinUI. La prise en charge du mode sombre est également élargie pour couvrir davantage de boîtes de dialogues dans l’Explorateur.

articles.title: Looking for the perfect gaming TV in time for GTA 6? This LG OLED TV is my pick, based on my real-world testing
articles.text:
I test TVs for a living, and this 48-inch LG OLED TV is the ideal pick for gaming if you want to upgrade ahead of GTA 6
Big savings on LG's budget 2026 OLED
Thinking about upgrading your gaming TV in time for GTA 6? While there are tons of great options, you can't really go wrong with LG's OLEDs — and I've found some great deals ahead of Prime Day.
If you're in the US, you can pick up the LG B6 48-inch for $699.99 (was $1,199.99) at Best Buy. A perfect-sized TV for bedroom gaming, the B6 is packing everything you need for the best gaming experience.
If you're in the UK, today's LG B6 deals aren't as good, but the excellent LG C5 48-inch is available for £819 at PRC Direct. Crampton & Moore had this TV for £99 earlier, but the price has gone back up: PRC Direct now has the best price. This is a great price for what was easily one of 2025's best TVs.
Today's best 48-inch gaming OLED TV deals
The LG B6 is a brilliant OLED TV, delivering colorful, contrast-rich picture quality along with full gaming features and an intuitive smart TV platform. The 48-inch model is down to $699.99 at Best Buy, which is an excellent price if you're looking for a bedroom-sized TV or gaming display.
One of 2025's very best TVs, the LG C5 is the total package. Showcasing awesome picture quality and carrying every feature you could need, especially for gaming, the C5 is a tough TV to beat in terms of value. While stock of the C5 continues to thin out, the 48-inch model is available at PRC Direct for £819 (use code AUTUMN10 at checkout).
Top-notch gaming OLEDs
LG's OLEDs are among the best gaming TVs each year, as each model comes packed with all the features you could need.
While the LG B6 may be the entry-level model in the 2026 LG OLED lineup, it still offers four HDMI 2.1 ports, which support 4K 120Hz, full VRR, Dolby Vision gaming and ALLM. With a measured 8.9ms input lag time, performance on the B6 is excellent. While playing Battlefield V, I found the B6's response times to be razor-sharp, delivering smooth performance that never faltered, even in intense shootouts as I tried to dodge enemy fire.
The B6 is brighter than its predecessor, the B5, offering roughly 150 nits more peak brightness. This means HDR highlights have more punch, resulting in richer picture quality. Colors are vibrant, black tones are inky and contrast is strong: the B6 delivers a great picture that's perfect for movies and games.
The LG C5 may be one of last year's models, and while this year's LG C6 is an improvement, the C5 is still a fantastic TV, especially for gaming. It too has four HDMI 2.1 ports that support 4K 144Hz, full VRR, ALLM and Dolby Vision gaming, and its measured 9.2ms input lag time mean performance is smooth. Again while playing Battlefield V, the C6 did a phenomenal job handling fast-paced action as I tried to navigate chaotic battles.
The C5 also has brilliant picture quality ideal for movies and gaming. Colors really pop on screen, detail is refined with 3D-like textures, it offers rich contrast with dazzling bright tones and deep dark tones and it has razor-sharp motion handling.

If you own an Apple device, it's likely that you have — or want — a set of AirPods. Sure, you can pair any old set of Bluetooth earbuds with an iDevice, and they'll probably work fine. articles.title: Agentic retrieval with LangChain and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Agentic retrieval with LangChain and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
When a user asks the support assistant, a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) application built with LangChain to compare two products across three dimensions, they’re effectively posing six questions simultaneously. Similarity search uses a single query vector to encapsulate all the intents. The retriever then generates the best approximation of the average of those intents. The resulting answer comes back concise. The search executes without errors. The relevance scores look reasonable. Yet the retrieved chunks, while topically relevant, only cover a fraction of what the question actually asked.
In this post, we showcase a RAG application on Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base with LangChain. We run the same multi-part question through standard and agentic retrieval, and read the trace events to see the plan the model produced. We also cover what the two retrieval paths cost and when the cheaper one is the right choice.
Agentic retrieval is available on Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base. Instead of one search, Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base plans the retrieval. It breaks the question into sub-queries, runs them, judges whether it has enough evidence, and searches again if it doesn’t. The langchain-aws package exposes both agentic and standard retrieval, so you can use either from a LangChain application.
Solution overview
Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base, the fully managed RAG capability in Amazon Bedrock, removes the self-managed vector store, embeddings, and re-ranking models from the RAG architecture. You configure a data source, and Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases handles chunking, embedding, storage, and retrieval. This walkthrough uses Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3).
Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases provides two APIs. We briefly discuss those differences in this post. The Retrieve API runs one hybrid search and returns scored chunks. The AgenticRetrieveStream API runs a planning loop and streams the steps back to you as trace events. In the langchain-aws package, the first is a standard LangChain retriever you can drop into a chain. The second is a function retrieval directly from a knowledge base.
The following diagram shows the solution architecture. The application queries Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases using either the Retrieve API (standard, single-shot) or the AgenticRetrieveStream API (multi-step planning loop). Both paths return document chunks from the knowledge base, which the application then uses to generate a grounded response.
Implementation walkthrough
The following sections walk you through creating a knowledge base, querying it with both retrieval methods, and reading the trace events the agentic planner produces.
Prerequisites
To follow along you need:
- An AWS account with access to Amazon Bedrock in a Region where Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases and agentic retrieval are available. This walkthrough uses the US East (N. Virginia) Region (us-east-1), and the code assumes it throughout. Check the AWS documentation for other Regional availability and support.
- Two AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) identities, described in the next section: a service role the knowledge base assumes, and permissions on the identity you call the APIs from.
- Python 3.12 or later.
- An S3 bucket holding the sample documents. The corpus needs several documents that cover overlapping topics so that a comparative question has somewhere to go. A single flat document cannot demonstrate query planning.
Install the packages. The Boto3 version matters: agentic_retrieve_stream did not exist before 1.43.32.
Permissions
Two identities are involved and separating them is worth doing deliberately. The knowledge base assumes a service role to read your documents and call the embedding model. Your application uses an AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) caller identity to query. Neither needs the other’s permissions.
Amazon Bedrock creates the service role for you if you let it. To supply your own, give it a trust policy that lets Amazon Bedrock assume it. Scope it with aws:SourceAccount and aws:SourceArn so that another account can’t use it as a confused deputy:
The service role also needs s3:ListBucket on your bucket and s3:GetObject on its contents, both conditioned on aws:ResourceAccount. Scope the knowledge-base/* wildcard character down to specific knowledge base IDs after you have created them.
The AWS STS caller identity needs a different set. bedrock:AgenticRetrieveStream and bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream can’t be scoped to a knowledge base Amazon Resource Name (ARN). bedrock:Retrieve and bedrock:GetDocumentContent can:
bedrock:GetDocumentContent is often overlooked. Agentic retrieval calls it when a FullDocumentExpansion step decides a passage lacks the context to answer. A policy with only bedrock:Retrieve works until the planner reaches for a whole document and then fails partway through a query.
To create and manage the knowledge base itself, the calling role additionally needs bedrock:CreateKnowledgeBase on *, and the GetKnowledgeBase, UpdateKnowledgeBase, DeleteKnowledgeBase, StartIngestionJob, GetIngestionJob, and ListIngestionJobs actions on knowledge-base/*. If you’re using guardrails, add bedrock:GetGuardrail and bedrock:ApplyGuardrail.
Running this walkthrough might incur costs for document storage and ingestion in the knowledge base, retrieval calls, and foundation model (FM) inference.
For more information about pricing, see the Knowledge Bases section of Amazon Bedrock pricing.
Delete the resources when you complete this experiment.
Creating and populating the knowledge base
Create the knowledge base with a managedKnowledgeBaseConfiguration. Setting embeddingModelType to MANAGED uses the service-managed embedding model.
There’s no storageConfiguration in that request. For a self-managed knowledge base you would pass one describing your vector store. Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base does not take one, which is the clearest signal in the API that Amazon Bedrock owns the storage layer.
Attach the S3 bucket as a data source, then start an ingestion job. Ingestion is asynchronous, so poll until the job reaches a terminal state rather than sleeping for a fixed interval and hoping.
The full data source configuration and error handling are in the sample repository.
Querying with the LangChain retriever
AmazonKnowledgeBasesRetriever wraps the Retrieve API and behaves like any other LangChain retriever. For Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases, pass managedSearchConfiguration. This is the part that trips people up: vectorSearchConfiguration is the previous path for knowledge bases where you run your own vector store. It is what most existing examples show.
Each result comes back as a LangChain Document. The relevance score is in metadata["score"], and the source document’s own metadata is under metadata["source_metadata"], renamed so it does not collide. If you want to drop low-confidence results, set min_score_confidence on the retriever instead of filtering afterward.
For a question with one clear intent, this is the right tool. It is one call. The latency is the lowest of the two options, and you keep full control of how the answer gets generated. Most of the queries a production assistant sees are this shape, and reaching for a planning loop to answer them wastes money and time.
Where single-shot retrieval runs out
Now give the same retriever a question with several parts:
Five chunks come back, ranked by hybrid score against one embedding of that whole question.
That question contains six intents: two services across three dimensions. Scoring the retrieved text for evidence of each one gives a concrete measure of what a single embedding recovers.
| numberOfResults | Chunks | Share of corpus | Sub-intents covered | Missing | 
| 5 | 5 | 10% | 4 of 6 | checkout on-call, inventory restore | 
| 10 | 10 | 19% | 6 of 6 | none | 
At five results, one embedding standing for six intents misses two of them. At ten it covers all six, with visible waste: two sub-intents are covered twice and one chunk carries none.
The retriever did its job. The limitation is structural: one vector cannot represent six intents, and there is no step in the process that asks whether the returned evidence is enough to answer the question.
Running agentic retrieval
Agentic retrieval is not a LangChain retriever, but a feature of Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases. The langchain-aws package exposes it as a standalone function, agentic_retrieve, because the underlying API streams its results and doesn’t fit the synchronous BaseRetriever interface. There’s no flag on AmazonKnowledgeBasesRetriever that switches it on.
With generate_response=True, the service returns a grounded answer and citations alongside the retrieved chunks, so you get an answer without wiring up a separate model call. The function works only against Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base.
Internally, the service plans, retrieves, evaluates whether the evidence is sufficient, and iterates if it isn’t. The helper hides all of that and hands back the final chunks, which is convenient and means you can’t see the plan.
Reading the trace events
To watch the model decompose the question, call agentic_retrieve_stream on the bedrock-agent-runtime client directly. This is the one place in this walkthrough where we step around langchain-aws, because the helper discards trace events and doesn’t expose maxAgentIteration or a custom planner model.
Set generateResponse to False when you only want the retrieval behavior. The API generates a grounded answer by default, which costs an extra model call you may not need while you are inspecting the plan.
A trace event’s step tells you where the planner is. SpeculativeRetrieval runs before the first plan to cut latency and doesn’t count against your iteration budget. Planning is where the model reads the question and prior results and emits sub-queries. Retrieval fires once per sub-query. FullDocumentExpansion appears when the model decides a passage lacks the context to answer and pulls the whole document instead. Each carries a status of IN_PROGRESS, SUCCEEDED, or FAILED, plus a human-readable message.
The final chunks arrive separately. The result is its own event type rather than a fifth step, and it holds the deduplicated chunks from every iteration along with the grounded answer when response generation is on. Branch on the event key, as the preceding loop demonstrates, rather than expect a terminal step value.
The sub-query text is the part worth logging. It sits in attributes.actions[].retrieve.inputQuery.text, not in the top-level trace fields, so a handler that reads only step and status shows you that planning happened without showing you what it decided.
The following diagram shows the agentic retrieval planning loop, including the speculative retrieval, planning, sub-query retrieval, evaluation, and optional re-planning steps.
Two details are worth knowing before you build on this. Deduplication applies only to the result event, so a chunk retrieved by three sub-queries appears once at the end but three times across the traces.
The second is about scores. A Retrieve response gives each chunk a typed score field holding its relevance to the query. Agentic retrieval results carry content, metadata, and sourceRetriever, with no equivalent typed field. Code that reads result["score"] after switching APIs gets nothing. If you rank or filter relevance, plan for that difference.
In production, use Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to enforce content policies and grounding checks on generated responses. Both retrieval paths support guardrails. Agentic retrieval supports guardrails through policyConfiguration.bedrockGuardrailConfiguration rather than the guardrail_config argument the LangChain retriever takes, and supports BLOCK mode only. If you rely on MASK mode, that is a reason to stay on the Retrieve API.
maxAgentIteration accepts two through ten and defaults to five. Leave it at the default. At two or three the planner runs one cycle, emits no sub-queries, and returns what the speculative retrieval step already found. This is single-shot behavior at the agentic price. Decomposition begins at four. The planner often stops early when it judges the evidence sufficient, so the ceiling is a bound rather than a target.
Comparing the two retrieval paths
For context on how this behaves at scale, AWS evaluated agentic retrieval on MuSiQue, a public multi-hop benchmark. The evaluation showed improved recall over single-shot retrieval, with the largest gains on the hardest questions. Single-hop questions saw gains under five points. That last figure matches the shape of the trade-off: decomposition helps when there is something to decompose.
Building the RAG chain
For the standard retriever, the usual LangChain Expression Language (LCEL) composition works directly:
format_docs matters more than it looks. Passing Document objects straight into a prompt renders their repr, and the model gets metadata noise mixed into the context.
To put agentic retrieval in the same position, wrap it in a RunnableLambda, since it is a function rather than a retriever:
Note that generate_response is off here. The service can generate the answer itself, but inside a chain you usually want your own prompt and model, so you take the chunks and generate downstream. Use the service generation when you want one call and less code, and the wrapped version when the prompt is yours to control.
Choosing between standard and agentic retrieval
Use Retrieve for short, well-scoped questions. It is cheaper, faster, works against self-managed knowledge bases, and returns scores in the results. Most production traffic looks like this.
Use AgenticRetrieveStream when questions are multi-part, comparative, or exploratory, or when the evidence spans more than one knowledge base. It registers up to five knowledge bases in one request and routes sub-queries using a natural-language description you attach to each. The other API cannot do this at all. It costs more per call, makes several model invocations, and has the higher latency of the two.
Routing on query shape rather than picking one for everything is the pattern we recommend. A classifier or a heuristic on the question can send most traffic down the cheap path and reserve the planner for questions that need it.
Clean up resources
Delete the knowledge base, its data source, the S3 objects and bucket, and the IAM role that you created. A knowledge base with documents in it continues to incur storage charges.
The repository includes a cleanup script that also empties the bucket and removes the role.
Conclusion
We showed how to build a RAG application on Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with LangChain, and how agentic retrieval handles multi-part questions that single-shot retrieval answers poorly. We also showed the friction in the current integration. Agentic retrieval is a function rather than a LangChain retriever, so it needs a RunnableLambda to sit in a chain. The trace events that show the query plan require a direct boto3 call.
Agentic retrieval trades higher per-call cost for improved recall on multi-hop questions, using a built-in model for query planning. The next useful step is measuring your own query mix before you route everything through a planner.
To get started, see the Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases documentation and the accompanying sample code. For help applying this to your own workload, contact your AWS account team.

articles.title: French cybersecurity startup Fleuret AI raises €4 million to automate penetration testing with AI agents | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Fleuret AI, a Paris-based cybersecurity startup automating penetration testing with agentic AI, has closed a €4 million pre-Seed round to hire AI, software engineering, and offensive security talent and accelerate platform development.
The round was led by RAISE Ventures, with participation from Auriga Cyber Ventures, Wind Capital, Better Angle, and leading business angels from the cybersecurity world, including Jules Veyrat, co-founder and CEO of Stoïk; Alexandre Andreini, Chief Risk Officer of Stoïk; Eric Fourrier, CEO of GitGuardian; Georges Lotigier, co-founder at Vade; and Olivier Pantaleo and Jean-François Aliotti, the co-founders of Almond.
“AI has changed the nature of cyberattacks by putting powerful tools within everyone’s reach, often for free. Organisations have to test their security against every attack technique, including the newest. Fleuret built its platform to evolve continuously and stay a step ahead of attackers, with a team that puts AI to work for deep offensive expertise. We are convinced Fleuret can become the reference in offensive security in Europe,” said Thibaut Schlaeppi, co-head of RAISE Ventures.
Founded in 2026 by Yanis Grigy (CEO) and Augustin Ponsin (CTO), Fleuret combines AI and offensive expertise to make pentesting accessible, continuous, and sovereign. The platform is built to move penetration testing from a one-off audit to continuous security across five pillars: know the exposed systems, identify vulnerabilities, prove they can be exploited, help fix them, and verify they are fixed.
According to the company, companies change their systems every day while security requirements keep rising. It highlighted that under NIS2 in particular, a growing number of organisations have to demonstrate how robust their security is. However, penetration testing still relies largely on one-off audits, which include a snapshot of a system at a given moment, even though a new deployment a few days later can already have changed its attack surface.
Fleuret claims to automate the pentester’s work with two AI agents, Emile and Champollion. They map a company’s environment, explore its applications, APIs and infrastructure, then try to exploit the vulnerabilities they find. It notes that every finding includes a proof of compromise demonstrating how it can be exploited. The platform then keeps watching the attack surface and can trigger new tests as the system changes.
The French startup further notes that, beyond finding vulnerabilities, it is building tools to see them through to resolution: prioritisation by exploitability, integration with the tools engineering teams already use, automatic re-testing, and reports that verify a vulnerability has been fixed.
“We do not simply want to automate penetration testing as it exists today. Our ambition is to build the offensive security layer that will keep companies secure all year round, whatever their size. This round gives us the means to accelerate that vision and to build a platform designed for enterprise environments from day one,” said Grigy, CEO and co-founder of Fleuret.
The company currently employs about ten people and counts several customers, including Brevo, Stoïk, and Yogosha. “From the start, the ambition is European: make offensive security accessible to every company, including those that cannot afford regular penetration tests,” the company said.

articles.title: Gemini: Diese Modelle könnt ihr ab dem 9. Oktober nicht mehr gratis nutzen
articles.text:
Gemini: Welche Modelle ihr weiterhin gratis nutzen könnt – und welche künftig Geld kosten
Für zahlreiche Nutzer:innen von Googles KI-Tool Gemini ändert sich in dieser Woche etwas. Google weist auf einer aktualisierten Support-Seite auf die bevorstehenden Änderungen beim Zugriff auf die Gemini-Modelle hin. Was sich konkret ändern wird?
Google beschränkt kostenlosen Zugriff auf neueste Gemini-Modelle
Bislang hat Google den Nutzer:innen des kostenlosen Gemini-Tarifs freien Zugang zu seinen neuesten Gemini-Flash-Modellen gewährt. Ab dem 9. Oktober wird dieser Zugang allerdings auf zahlende Kund:innen beschränkt.
Inhaber:innen privater Konten ohne kostenpflichtiges Abonnement haben ab Stichtag nur noch Zugriff auf das Modell „Gemini Flash-Lite“. Die Modelle „Flash“ oder „Pro“ stehen ihnen nicht mehr zur Verfügung. Auch Nutzer:innen kostenpflichtiger Tarife sind betroffen: Abonnenten von „AI Plus“ – Googles günstigstem KI-Tarif – verlieren ab dem 9. Oktober den Zugriff auf das „Pro“-Modell.
Nur „AI Pro“ und „AI Ultra“ erhalten Zugriff auf verschiedene Gemini-Modelle
Die Änderungen erfolgen nur wenige Monate nachdem Google auf ein nutzungsbasiertes Modell (basierend auf der Rechenleistung) umgestellt und Limits für die Nutzung eingeführt hatte. Zuvor wurde die Nutzung von Gemini anhand der Anzahl der Prompts berechnet.
Nur Abonnent:innen der Tarife „AI Pro“ und „AI Ultra“ erhalten zukünftig Zugriff auf verschiedene Gemini-Modelle. „AI Pro“-Abonnent:innen können dann auf die Option „Deep Think“ zugreifen, die laut Google „maximale parallele Schlussfolgerung“ (maximum parallel reasoning) ermöglicht. Diese Funktion war bisher nur „AI Ultra“-Abonnent:innen vorbehalten. Ähnlich wie bei Claude und ChatGPT wird Google laut Android Police auch für Gemini verschiedene Stufen für den Rechenaufwand bei der Modellverarbeitung einführen. Unabhängig vom Modell kann man dann zwischen drei Stufen wählen: niedrig, mittel oder hoch.
Gemini 4 Argon wirft wohl seine Schatten voraus
Die Nutzungslimits der Tarife bleiben unverändert. „AI Plus“-Abonnent:innen erhalten auch in Zukunft das Doppelte des Standard-Nutzungslimits, „AI Pro“-Abonnent:innen das Vierfache. „AI Ultra“-Abonnent:innen verfügen je nach Tarif über das Fünf- oder Zwanzigfache des Standardlimits.
Google nimmt diese Änderungen laut Bericht wohl vor, um Ressourcen für die öffentliche Einführung von Gemini 4 Argon freizusetzen: seinem nach eigenen Angaben bislang leistungsstärksten und fähigsten KI-Modell.

articles.title: Microsoft: Windows KB5124010 update crashes some games and apps
articles.text:
Microsoft confirmed over the weekend that some games and applications using AC-3 (Dolby Digital) audio decoding will crash after installing the September 2026 KB5124010 Windows 11 preview update.
KB5124010 is an optional update that requires users to click the "Download and install" link, which should reduce the number of potentially affected Windows users. However, it installs automatically on devices running Windows 11 24H2, where the "Get the latest updates as soon as they're available" option is toggled on.
"In some cases the application can fail to launch, or close without warning. In other cases the application will work normally until certain features are used, such as playing music," Microsoft said in a Friday update to the Windows release health dashboard. "Affected applications may vary and can include games, media players, and certain productivity applications."
However, the company added that many modern apps don't use Windows for this type of encoding and aren't affected. Additionally, the code component that triggers these crashes is most commonly used in legacy applications that still use the Windows built-in audio decoding, while modern apps that use the legacy AC-3 codec often include their own audio decoding components.
Although it didn't provide an estimated timeline for a fix, Microsoft is working to resolve this issue and said it will share more information in a future update.
Last month, Microsoft released emergency updates to fix another known issue causing USB audio issues, as well as Remote Desktop Services failures and Hyper-V problems after installing the KB5124008 and KB5124012 September 2026 security updates.
Last year, the company addressed a similar issue in January that triggered audio playback issues and Code 10 errors on Windows 11 24H2 systems with USB audio device drivers, and lifted a safeguard hold that prevented upgrades and caused Bluetooth headsets and speakers to malfunction on systems with Dirac audio improvement software.
Two years ago, it also confirmed an issue that caused game audio to unexpectedly increase to full volume when using USB DAC sound systems and blocked Windows 24H2 upgrades on systems with incompatible Intel Smart Sound Technology (SST) audio drivers because of blue screen of death (BSOD) issues.

articles.text:
L’injustice suprême ? Sur Reddit, l’acheteur d’un Ryzen 7 5800X3D d’occasion est confronté à un problème relativement atypique : son processeur fait l’objet d’une exclusion matérielle imposée, par le logiciel anti-triche Riot Vanguard, à son ancien propriétaire. Tout à fait fonctionnel partout ailleurs, son CPU de seconde main est bloqué sur Valorant.
L’acheteur explique avoir contacté le service en ligne de Riot, qui lui a indiqué que l’ancien propriétaire avait triché et s’était vu infliger une suspension liée directement à son identifiant matériel (ou HWID).
Protégez votre vie numérique avec Bitdefender, la protection européenne de confiance. Bitdefender vous protège contre les arnaques et les fraudes du web. Profitez de vos activités en ligne en toute tranquillité.
Une exclusion matérielle un peu trop efficace ?
Ces interdictions HWID sont en l’occurrence des restrictions lourdes qui s’appliquent à un compte Riot, mais aussi et surtout aux composants physiques d’un PC utilisé pour tricher.
Le tricheur ne peut plus jouer sous un autre compte, et réinstaller Windows, Vanguard ou le jeu ne change rien à la sanction. Mais ces composants restent bloqués sur Valorant, même une fois revendus à un joueur qui n’a rien à se reprocher.
Pire, l’utilisation d’un nouveau compte sur ces composants peut même conduire, dans certains cas, à une suspension automatique. La double peine, d’autant qu’il n’existe pas de méthode concrète permettant de vérifier, avant achat, si un processeur d’occasion figure déjà sur une liste de composants bannis.
Derrière cette mesure se cache vraisemblablement l’utilisation, par Riot, de la clé d’homologation TPM. Un identifiant permanent que l’éditeur avait déjà indiqué utiliser dans le cadre de son dispositif d’identification matérielle. Un système redoutablement efficace… comme a pu le constater ce pauvre utilisateur de Reddit.

articles.title: Alleged ShinyHunters Leader Arrested in Jordan
articles.text:
An individual believed to be the leader of the extortion group ShinyHunters was reportedly arrested in Jordan and is cooperating with the FBI.
The suspect, Saif al-Din Khader, known as Rey, a teenage cybercriminal from Amman, is helping the FBI identify other ShinyHunters members, Reuters reports.
Khader is also a known member of the Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters group. It is unclear where he is detained.
The arrest was made shortly after the extortion group hacked and defaced the FBI’s jobs site, FBIJobs.gov, boasting about stealing 2-3 terabytes of data.
ShinyHunters sent a sample list of 5,000 FBI employees to the media, claiming to be in possession of the personal and health information of all current and former FBI employees.
Last week, the Dutch police announced the arrest of a 24-year-old man from Amsterdam as part of the FBI’s investigation into ShinyHunters.
The FBI later confirmed the arrest, saying the individual was involved in the hacking of more than 140 organizations, as well as in collecting at least $70 million in extortion payments.
While the Dutch police and the FBI refrained from revealing the suspect’s identity, independent reports have suggested he is Pepijn van der Stap, who was convicted in 2023 for hacking and extorting numerous organizations and was on supervised release after serving three years in prison.
Khader apparently pinned the recent FBI hack on van der Stap by placing a defacement image featuring the Pokémon character Umbreon. Van der Stap used the nickname Umbreon in his extortion activities, investigative journalist Brian Krebs reported.
The FBI last week said it was actively working with partners to pursue additional leads in its ShinyHunters investigation.
“More arrests are on the table,” FBI Director Kash Patel posted on X.

articles.title: Dave Jones, creador del 'GTA': "Hace como tres años que no compro un videojuego físico, soy parte del problema"
articles.text:
El mundo del videojuego se ha movido alrededor de dos puntos este verano que las torrenciales lluvias de estos días nos confirman que ha terminado. Por un lado, la sangría que se está produciendo en Xbox. Por otro, el golpe al videojuego en formato físico.
PlayStation anunció el pasado 1 de julio que, a partir de enero de 2028, dejará de haber juegos en formato físico para sus consolas. Quitando de la ecuación el 'estanterismo', que no haya juegos en formato físico con el juego dentro del propio disco (y no como vienen algunos juegos actualmente) es un problema enorme para la preservación del propio videojuego. Máxime cuando la propia Sony nos dice que sólo adquirimos licencias temporales de uso cuando adquirimos un juego digital.
Se ha hablado mucho, muchísimo del tema y nosotros mismos hemos hecho ruido al respecto, hablando de todo lo que conlleva, pero... ¿qué piensa una voz tan autorizada como la de David Jones?. Quizá por nombre no lo ubiques, pero fundó DMA Design en 1988 y de ese estudio salieron juegos como 'Lemmings' o 'Grand Theft Auto'. Sí, ese juego cuya sexta entrega numerada no llegará en formato físico.
Al final de un panel celebrado en Comic-Con, alguien entre el público hizo la pregunta que ya ni se me pasó por la cabeza porque tengo tan asumida la derrota que no quiero pensar en ello: "Me gustaría saber tu opinión sobre la lenta desaparición del juego en formato físico". La respuesta de Jones, muy interesante:
Hoy estuve haciendo una sesión de firmas y muchísima gente vino con copias originales en caja y en perfecto estado de GTA 1 que tiene como 25 o 30 años. Y las han conservado en un estado impoluto. Es increíble, incluso he visto versiones en español que nunca vi porque soy del Reino Unido. Entonces, estaba firmando las copias mientras pensaba "mierda, qué lástima si esto desaparece, ¿no?"
Sin embargo, el propio Dave admite que es parte del problema. "¡Hace como tres años que no compro un juego en formato físico!" Así que estoy en plan "joder, soy parte del problema, pero no quiero que desaparezcan". No tengo una respuesta, preferiría que nos dieran la opción de elegir, sinceramente".
Jones no está solo en esto y, aunque pocos, otros pesos pesados de la industria se han posicionado. Dan Houser, quien trabajó en DMA Design en los primeros GTA y luego fundó Rockstar Games junto a su hermano Sam, comentó recientemente que no tiene claro que a él, personalmente, le importe, pero tiene claro que "si la gente lo quiere, las empresas deberían ofrecerlo".
Eso sí, Houser apunta que "por muy críticas que sean las opiniones sobre los lanzamientos digitales, la posibilidad de actualizar y solucionar problemas en los juegos ha sido realmente útil para la calidad de los mismos".
Y aquí el problema es el que señalan ambos sin decirlo: el formato digital es obvio que tiene muchas ventajas. Es cómodo, permite que los desarrolladores trabajen de otra forma porque no tienen que preparar una versión lista para "imprimir" y luego seguir trabajando en el parche del día 1, sino que el juego digital se lanza ya con ese parche. Pero, existiendo esa comodidad, tienen claro que es una opción que no se debería perder.
Son dos perfiles de la industria del videojuego, pero luego está la parte del negocio. PlayStation ya sabemos lo que piensa, Xbox y Nintendo se han posicionado sin decirlo, unos no lanzando juegos completos en el Blu-Ray y otros con las Game Key Card y una publicidad muy agresiva orientada a que se compre en digital.
Y luego están perfiles como el de Strauss Zelnick, CEO de Take-Two y, por extensión, el mandamás de Rockstar, empresa bajo su paraguas. En su opinión:
Más del 90% de nuestro negocio se distribuye digitalmente. Ya es un negocio digital. Por eso, en ciertos casos, especialmente cuando se trata de un juego grande, los discos, y quiero recalcar que dije discos, simplemente dejan de tener sentido para el consumidor. Además, en la mayoría de los casos es necesario registrarse en línea para poder jugar de todos modos. Así que, si ya estás conectado, ¿qué importa si lo descargas digitalmente? Es lo mismo y resulta mucho más conveniente."
Siendo cierta la parte sobre la importancia del formato digital, no es cierto que en la mayoría de casos sea necesario registrarse para poder jugar. También comentó que la industria se dirige a un mercado en el que sí o sí, los juegos en disco dejan de tener sentido, como el del streaming, apuntando que es un escenario que está a tres años de distancia.
Volviendo a Jones, el diseñador cree que las cosas pueden cambiar. "Mucha gente está haciendo ruido y creo que es lo correcto. Veremos si ese mensaje que mandan puede hacer que las cosas cambien". Y, curiosamente, pone mucha responsabilidad sobre los hombros de alguien que no esperaba que saliera en la conversación: Hideo Kojima.
Otro de los pelotazos del verano fue Sony cortando la relación con el creativo japonés (padre de 'Metal Gear'). Kojima y su equipo están creando un juego de espionaje y acción con una IP nueva y, el mismo día en el que nos enteramos de la patada de PlayStation al japonés, supimos que ahora iba a seguir desarrollando ese juego... pero con ayuda de Xbox.
"Quizá sea parte de la razón por la que cambió de Sony a Microsoft", afirma Jones. "Quién sabe, creo que ese ruido puede hacer que terminen escuchando a la gente y cambie la cosa" apuntó.
Ojalá, Dave, y aunque parece que PlayStation está haciendo encuestas al respecto para conocer la opinión de los usuarios, ya han iniciado el camino de la desaparición del formato al reconvertir su fábrica de discos en Austria para que se encargue de otras cosas. Sólo el tiempo lo dirá, pero no queda tanto hasta ese enero de 2028...

articles.title: German utility launches dedicated electricity tariff for gamers with power-hungry PCs
articles.text:
In context: PC gaming, especially the kind involving high-end hardware and multiple machines, is a very expensive hobby these days – even more so than before. Not only do parts cost a fortune, the electricity they consume adds to the final bill. It's why a German power company is offering a specialized tariff to customers designed specifically for gamers.
German publication ComputerBase writes that meinGAMING is the tariff name being offered to gaming households in Germany. There are three tiers available, each with its own annual energy consumption.
The first category, Casual Gamer, is aimed at those who game for 10 or more hours per week and see gaming as a way to unwind after work or at weekends. Selecting this profile sets the calculator's estimated annual household electricity consumption to 2,500 kWh.
Pro Gamer, meanwhile, targets more dedicated players with high-end setups, multiple systems, or an interest in streaming or modding. The description refers to 30 or more hours of gaming per week, alongside working from home, and the calculator defaults to 3,500 kWh per year.
The final category, Gaming Households, is aimed at families or shared homes with two or more active gamers. Its description refers to 50 or more hours of gaming per week across devices such as PCs and consoles, with a default annual household electricity consumption estimate of 5,000 kWh.
The idea here is that gamers who use a lot of electricity might benefit from this tariff. The fixed charge is relatively high, but the price per kWh is lower, so whether it makes sense depends on your household's annual electricity usage (beyond just gaming). Those who use enough could save money compared to their current tariff. The website claims there's an energy price guarantee of up to 24 months, too.
SWK ENERGIE, Krefeld's municipal utility company, provides meinGAMING's electricity. It writes that 100% of this comes from renewable energy, which is a nice extra.
It is interesting to see an electricity tariff targeting gamers. A gaming PC with an RTX 5090 and a Core Ultra 9 285K being used for gaming 30 hours per week could use roughly 1,100 kWh per year. Include the monitor, and that could rise to more than 1,200 kWh/year, illustrating why the electricity company sees this demographic as a prime potential customer.
